loop.name: in-process-delivery-tiers
loop.what: The Agent exposes four in-process delivery entry points that differ on exactly two axes: which durable inbox list the message lands in (`next-turn` vs `next-step`) and whether the call wakes the driver. `followup` = next-turn + wake, `steer` = next-step + wake, `inject` = next-step without wake; `send(message, target, wakeup)` is the shared primitive all three delegate to. A waking message that arrives while the current activity is already aborted is reclassified to `next-turn` BEFORE insertion, so it can never join a dead activity. `ReactLoopInbox.append/prepend/replace/remove/splice` are the durable mutation surface behind them.
invariants: `inject` must never wake the driver; `followup`, `steer` and `send(..., true)` must
the waking-after-abort classification is captured before the inbox insertion so a reentrant cancel from a splice observer cannot reclassify it
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed - a splice that would leave the same message id pending in either list throws `message "<id>" is already pending` and the session event is never appended

loop.name: durable-inbox-projection
loop.what: Pending agent input is not process memory: every normalized mutation appends one `agent/inbox/spliced` session event, and the `inbox` SessionProjectionDefinition folds those splices back into `{ 'next-turn', 'next-step' }`. The fold validates index bounds and rejects duplicate pending message ids, throwing `invalid persisted inbox splice at session seq N`. `claim(target, turn)` removes the entire `next-step` batch plus at most one queued `next-turn` message and emits `agent/inbox/claimed` per claimed message; `clear()` empties next-step before next-turn.
invariants: inbox state is derived from the durable log and is never authoritative in memory
no insert or replace may produce a duplicate pending message id across the two lists
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed - a corrupt splice history makes the projection fold throw rather than silently dropping queued input

loop.name: turn-step-durable-machine
loop.what: One driver runs turn -> steps -> turn. `turn/start` is appended before the first step; each step appends `step/start`, performs the model request plus its tool calls, and appends `step/end` in a finally; `turn/end` carries a structured TurnEndReason. Steps continue while a step leaves work (tool calls that did not conclude the turn, or a non-empty next-step inbox); `max-tokens` is sticky so a later completed step cannot downgrade the turn outcome. A step decision rewritten to empty still owns the turn boundary but spends no model call.
invariants: `step/end` is appended even when the step throws, and `turn/end` always carries exactly one reason
max-tokens stays sticky for the whole turn
loop.failurePolicy: mixed - an aborted signal yields `{kind:'aborted', reason}`; any other error yields `{kind:'error', failure}` preserving LlmError facts or flattening to errorChain text under code UNKNOWN; a failure appending `turn/end` is re-reported through `agent/error`

loop.name: driver-wake-latch-and-maintenance-phase
loop.what: The driver has three phases: idle, maintenance, running. A wake that arrives while maintenance or an aborted driver owns the phase is latched in `wakeRequested` and replayed at convergence instead of dropped; a `disposed` cause never latches, so teardown waits on no model turn. `runMaintenance` throws synchronously when the agent already has active work and reserves the idle phase for non-turn work (manual compaction uses it), with later waking input withheld until the maintenance task settles.
invariants: disposal never latches a wake
runMaintenance may only be entered from the idle phase
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed - runMaintenance on a busy agent throws `agent "<id>" already has active work`; the maintenance job's own rejection is preserved to its caller while the phase always returns to idle

loop.name: per-session-serialization-and-write-ownership
loop.what: One session has at most one live agent/driver, enforced at several boundaries. The agent registry rejects a duplicate id at `enter()` (`agent "<id>" is already registered`); resume acquires the persistence write handle BEFORE reading the log so a concurrent resume of the same id is excluded by the backend; and a config-driven restore waits for a draining same-id lifecycle to leave both the agent and session registries before creating or resuming. The persistence write handle is the cross-process claim.
invariants: create/resume may prepare concurrently but only one exact registry entry may publish
resume must take write ownership before reading or repairing the log
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed - a second live agent or a lost write claim is an error, never merged

loop.name: cancellation-and-abort-semantics
loop.what: `cancel(cause, options)` clears the durable inbox unless `keepInbox` is set, drops any latched wake, and aborts the phase controller with a structured `AgentCancelCause`. Disposal is modelled as a `disposed`-cause cancel followed by `whenIdle()` and scope disposal, not a bare teardown. The tool scheduler converts an abort into ordered synthetic `tool/result` errors (`tool call aborted before dispatch`) for every unstarted call so replay stays valid, and an interrupted assistant stream commits an `assistant/message` with `interrupted: true` when partial content exists, otherwise an `assistant/attempt`.
invariants: every tool call emitted in a step has a durable result, even after cancellation
disposal is a cancel plus observed quiescence
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed for log validity (synthetic results are fabricated deliberately); the driver boundary contains and reports errors rather than propagating them to senders

loop.name: bounded-parallel-tool-scheduler
loop.what: `executeToolCalls` schedules one assistant step's calls by their live concurrency mode. An exclusive call is a one-element barrier; a parallel stretch runs through a rolling pool capped by `maxParallelToolCalls`. The mode is re-read before each start so a registry change can force a barrier mid-step. Dispatch may overlap, but `tool/result` commits, `additionalContexts` acceptance and `concludesTurn` aggregation stay in model order, and each result cites its `tool/call` seq through `sourceEventSeqs`. The cap is read through a getter at the start of each group, so a committed settings change bounds the next group without disturbing the one in flight.
invariants: results commit in model order even when dispatch overlaps
a scheduler failure stops new dispatches and drains already-started ones without fabricating results
loop.failurePolicy: mixed - abort drains started calls, records synthetic results for the rest and returns with the signal still aborted; an internal scheduler failure drains in-flight dispatches and rejects with the first failure while preserving already-recorded `tool/call` events
constants: maxParallelToolCalls must be a positive integer; 1 means serial

loop.name: agent-lifecycle-transaction
loop.what: `AgentLoop.prepare()` constructs the driver, its scope and one memoized reverse teardown before anything is published; deactivation fuses caller cancellation, owner-fiber unload and factory teardown into a single signal registered over mutable slots, so an unload arriving while the scope is still being minted finds a working disposer. `publish` enters both registries, announces the session then the agent, and emits `agent/session-start`. Teardown collects failures, always runs session-handle close, registry detach, scope unwind and bookkeeping release to quiescence, then rethrows a single error or an AggregateError.
invariants: nothing is observable before setup completes and registry publication begins
cleanup always runs to quiescence even when individual cleanup steps fail
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed - a setup throw, setup-commit throw, or owner disposal rolls the whole transaction back without publishing either id

loop.name: config-driven-agent-startup
loop.what: The `agent-loop` plugin config carries an `agents` array (`id`, `sessionId` or `resumeSessionId`, provider, model, reasoningEffort, maxTokens, cwd) and starts each entry at boot. `sessionId` and `resumeSessionId` are mutually exclusive and duplicate exact identities are rejected before any agent starts. `restoreOrCreateConfigured` resumes the materialized identity and falls back to fresh creation only on `SessionPersistenceNotFoundError`; corruption, ownership conflicts and backend failures stay loud. A failed start is reported through the `agent-loop/config-start-failed` event so identity-bound consumers reject buffered work instead of waiting forever. A launcher may also pin identities out-of-band through `CONFIGURED_AGENT_IDENTITIES_KEY`.
invariants: identity conflicts are rejected before any configured agent starts
only a genuinely absent stored session falls back to first creation
loop.failurePolicy: mixed - a failed configured start is contained and reported; the remaining configured agents still start

loop.name: canonical-request-epoch
loop.what: Before every model call the loop canonicalizes the request envelope into an `EpochHeader` and logs it as `request/header` with reason `initial` | `resume` | `change` | `series`, plus a `request/context` record whenever provider, model, contextWindow or systemPromptUpdate differ from the previous one. `startsSeries` is set when a pre-step listener declared one, the surface replacement generation advanced, or the assembled tool schemas differ from the logged header - so provider KV-cache continuity is a durable, replayable fact rather than an inference. Requests are built from `session.deriveMessages()` and deep-frozen, with a WeakSet so replaced history is not retained.
invariants: a request/header must omit `system` and must omit empty `tools` and empty `adapterDefaults`
the assembled tool set is part of the epoch identity, not an incidental argument
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed - `validateSessionEventData` rejects a header carrying `system`, an empty tools array, or empty adapterDefaults

loop.name: pre-step-waterfall
loop.what: At every step boundary the loop claims the inbox batch, assembles the system prompt, projects the runtime-context snapshot, and then dispatches the `agent/pre-step` waterfall whose default is an `enter` decision carrying the claimed messages. A listener may return `{kind:'reject'}` (the turn then ends with reason `blocked`) or rewrite the admitted message batch. Context plugins (time-context, tmux-context) and the compaction pruner hook here; tmux-context registers with `{prepend: true}` and prepends its snapshot to the decision's messages.
invariants: the claimed inbox input is already durably removed before the waterfall runs
a reject decision ends the turn with reason `blocked`
loop.failurePolicy: mixed - the waterfall composes listener results and propagates a throwing listener; agent-scoped `emit` notifications elsewhere are contained per listener

loop.name: request-error-recovery-waterfall
loop.what: A failed or aborted model attempt first commits an `assistant/attempt` record and then dispatches the `agent/request-error` waterfall carrying provider, failure, retryPolicy and signal. A listener returning `{kind:'retry'}` re-enters the attempt loop without leaving the step; any other answer raises the attempt as an `LlmError`. `compaction-basic` uses this hook to recover from a provider-confirmed context-overflow failure by compacting and retrying.
invariants: the attempt is durably recorded before the recovery waterfall runs
without a retry decision the original failure is preserved
loop.failurePolicy: fail-soft - recovery is listener-driven; the default action rethrows the original failure

loop.name: turn-boundary-projection
loop.what: `dsh-agent-loop` registers a `turnBoundary` session projection that folds `turn/start`, `turn/end`, `step/start` and `step/end` into `{ openTurnStartSeq, lastStepStartSeq, lastStepBoundary, lastTurn }`. It is the durable answer to "is a turn open and where is the last step boundary", consumed by resume repair, by other plugins' step-open decisions, and by the token meter's own replay fold.
invariants: an absent `turnBoundary` key means "no agent loop loaded" (capability absence), not a corrupt state
stateVersion is bumped when fold semantics change
loop.failurePolicy: fail-soft - readers that have a safe fallback treat absence as capability absence; readers with no safe fallback (the step-open decision) may fail loud instead

loop.name: agent-registry-and-runtime-ownership
loop.what: `AgentRegistry` (`ctx.agents`) owns the live agent store, the creation-factory slot and runtime parent ownership. `enter()` inserts a prepared but unpublished agent without announcing it; `announce()` emits `agent/created` (a synchronous listener throw vetoes publication) and pairs every announced entry with a later `agent/disposed`. A detach requested during the creation dispatch is deferred until that dispatch unwinds. `isOwnedBy`, `roots` and `list` expose runtime ownership, which is deliberately independent of durable session lineage. The registry also registers the `agent` Typert lookup and context host for the wire type.
invariants: an agent id must equal its session id
creation and disposal edges are paired; an entry rolled back before announce emits no disposed
a stale detach capability can never delete a later same-id lifecycle
loop.failurePolicy: mixed - a synchronous `agent/created` listener throw vetoes publication and rolls back; `agent/disposed` listener throws and rejections are logged and contained

loop.name: agent-initiator-scope
loop.what: An AsyncLocalStorage-based causal attribution scope carries the initiating Agent through one process-local asynchronous driver chain: `withInitiator`, `withoutInitiator`, `currentInitiator`, `requireInitiator`. `wakeDriver` establishes the boundary for every driver, and `executeToolCalls` reads it with `requireInitiator()` to obtain the owning session. Live boundaries are counted so teardown drains outstanding runs before disabling the stores, while a nested lineage that itself started the owning-fiber unload is excluded from its own drain.
invariants: ambient initiator presence is attribution only - neither liveness proof nor authorization
returned-Promise boundaries drain during teardown
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed - reads after disposal throw `agent initiator scope is disposed`, and `requireInitiator` outside a boundary throws `no initiating agent is active`

loop.name: agent-scoped-composition-at-publication
loop.what: `create`/`resume` accept a `setup(agentCtx, agent)` callback that composes the agent's own scoped world - scoped tools, prompt sections and variables, listeners, awaited child plugins - before either registry insertion, so observers can never see a half-configured agent. Setup may return an `AgentSetupCommit` whose synchronous `commit()` runs after the last setup await and immediately before publication, letting mutable provisioning revalidate at the exact publish boundary. Setup composes; it never drives.
invariants: every agentCtx registration exists before session/created, agent/created, agent/session-start and the first prompt assembly
setup composes, it never drives
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed - a setup throw, a commit throw, or owner disposal rolls the scope back without publishing either id

loop.name: agent-preset-composition-mounting
loop.what: `agent-presets` discovers preset compositions (`agent.cordis.yml` under a shipped preset root plus a user `.agent-presets` directory), validates their `preset.yml` metadata, and mounts each as a Cordis subtree under a standing scope key to which agent contexts are parented; the mounted subtree's active loader rows are the composition a session runs. Mounting is read-only by construction: the inherited loader `write()` is overridden to a no-op so a preset file is never persisted back, and mount records are pruned by observing that a fiber's `uid` cleared.
invariants: a preset is an input, never a persistence target
a preset's composition file backs every session that names it
loop.failurePolicy: mixed - a broken preset surfaces as a metadata/entry-list problem instead of being mounted; the mount set is bounded by observation-based pruning rather than a disposal hook

loop.name: default-agent-model-selection
loop.what: `agent-default-model` owns the default provider/model/reasoningEffort selection for Agents created without an explicit model. It is a Cordis service reading live through a settings section in its own `agent-default-model` namespace, so the value can be changed at runtime by any settings writer while a deployment without a settings provider keeps its composition entry. `saveSelection` writes the complete triple back through the optional settings service.
invariants: every consumer reads through `currentSelection()`, so no registration-level fact is rebuilt when the settings document changes
loop.failurePolicy: fail-soft - a deployment without a settings provider simply keeps its composition entry

session.name: append-only-jsonl-event-log
session.what: Session holds an in-memory append-only `SessionEvent[]` written only by `Session.append` (packages/core/session/src/index.ts:703-754): each call snapshots `data` as lossless JSON, validates the event payload and surface metadata, freezes the envelope, and pushes it, so the event's `seq` is exactly the pre-push log length. The JSONL backend serializes those events one JSON object per line after a `type:'session'` header record (`eventLines`/`eventLine`, session-persistence-jsonl/src/format.ts:312-323) into an immutable generation file `session.v<N>.jsonl` (optionally checksummed Zstandard frames), extending it with `persistBatch` (index.ts:807-821) or materializing a fresh generation. Cold reads decode the artifact through a bounded parsed-log handoff memo (`COLD_LOG_MEMO_MAX_ENTRIES = 2`) and one fail-closed validation pass (`decodeStoredLog`, index.ts:711-768).
invariants: Committed events are never rewritten and seq is contiguous from 0, equal to the log length (the `seq = log.length` contract)
Every event's `data` must be losslessly JSON-serializable; violations throw at the append site rather than at flush time
One JSON object per event row, with the header as exactly one JSONL line, so a physical tail is truncatable at a record boundary
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed — non-JSON payloads, invalid surface metadata, and reentrant appends throw before the log mutates (index.ts:713-735); unreadable artifact bytes become SessionPersistenceCorruptionError (index.ts:751)
constants: SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION = 3 stamped into every header line (packages/core/session/src/types.ts:88)

session.name: seq-contiguity-and-branded-sequence-types
session.what: Sequence positions are nominal types rather than bare numbers: `SessionSeq` admits only non-negative safe integers that are existing event positions and `SessionLogOffset` admits the same for gaps/prefix lengths/cursors, both rejecting `-0` (packages/core/session/src/types.ts:30-58). Contiguity is enforced at three boundaries with the same rule: the Session constructor refuses a seed whose `seq` differs from its index (index.ts:570-572), every append derives `seq` from the log length, and the persistence seam re-checks batches with `assertContiguous(id, events, cursor)` before writing (session-persistence/src/storage-contract.ts:145-151).
invariants: Stored and live logs are dense from seq 0; a gap is never representable except through the explicit `SessionLogOffset` gap/prefix type
A seed, fork prefix, or append batch must continue the stored next-seq exactly
`-0` is not a valid sequence value anywhere (JSON-unstable negative zero)
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed — TypeError from the brand constructors, `seed event at index N has seq M (expected N)` from the constructor, and `append seq mismatch` from assertContiguous

session.name: surface-projection-and-derived-history-cache
session.what: The model-visible conversation is a projection over the event log rather than a stored field: message-producing events carry a `surfaceOp` (`'append'` or `{op:'replace',startSeq,endSeq}`) and `sourceEventSeqs` (packages/core/session/src/types.ts:434-450), and `SurfaceManager.validateNext` accepts each candidate before it enters the log. `Session.deriveMessages()` walks the ordered surface nodes and folds the pure per-node rule `deriveEventMessage` (surface.ts:92-126), caching each node's projection exactly once and rebuilding only when the surface's `replaceGeneration` changes (index.ts:825-846). The same exported fold is reused by external reconstructors so a rebuilt transcript equals what the request was built from.
invariants: Derived history comes only from surface nodes; a raw event without a marker never enters the transcript
A replacement node must cite every shadowed surface node and must cover their ranges completely
The derived cache is invalidated by surface rewrite, and returned arrays are fresh snapshots while their Message objects stay shared and deep-frozen
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed — surface metadata and request-header/tool-error consistency are validated in `validateSessionEventData` and `validateNext` during append, so a bad event never enters the log

session.name: session-fork-inherited-prefix
session.what: `SessionStore.fork(source, boundary, childSessionId)` creates a live child from a stable prefix of a live source: the boundary must be an existing inclusive seq and must not end inside an open turn, otherwise typed `SessionForkError` codes are raised (index.ts:1196-1254, codes at 870-875). The child records `inheritedEventCount` = the copied prefix length and an `isSeeded` header, and the constructor appends a tagged `session/end-seed` marker at the inherited cut (index.ts:606-610) so a later reader can tell inherited history from live work; `ownEvents()`/`isOwnSeq()` expose the cut (index.ts:648-659).
invariants: The fork boundary is an inclusive, existing, contiguous seq and never lands inside an open turn
A seeded session's constructor seed length must equal its declared inherited prefix length, and an unseeded session's inherited count must be 0
The inherited cut is durable in the log (last tagged `session/end-seed`), not only in memory
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed — SessionForkError with codes SESSION_NOT_FOUND, SESSION_NOT_LIVE, SESSION_ALREADY_EXISTS, INVALID_BOUNDARY, OPEN_TURN
constants: Fork error codes: SESSION_NOT_FOUND, SESSION_NOT_LIVE, SESSION_ALREADY_EXISTS, INVALID_BOUNDARY, OPEN_TURN (packages/core/session/src/index.ts:870-875)

session.name: crash-repair-torn-tail-and-interrupted-turn-closers
session.what: Crash recovery has a physical half and a semantic half. Physically, the JSONL reader never returns a torn tail: it records `tornTruncateTo` (and, for Zstandard, the complete records recovered from a torn final frame as `recoveredTail`), and the write path truncates the torn bytes with fsync and durably rewrites recovered events before the handle's first new append (index.ts:736-739, 840-844, 1287-1296; storage.ts:328-337). Semantically, `interruptedTurnClosers(events)` synthesizes deterministic closers — error `tool/result` events for unmatched calls (codes TOOL_NOT_STARTED / TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN), then any open `step/end`, then `turn/end {reason:{kind:'interrupted'}}` — reusing the last event's timestamp; resume appends them through the write handle as an ordinary batch, and read-only observers balance a cold log in memory only.
invariants: A torn physical tail is discarded and fsynced before any new append, so duplicate seq numbers can never be written
Synthetic closers are the only crash story: an interrupted turn is closed, never resumed in place
Closer synthesis is deterministic (reuses the last event's time) and only runs for a log whose tail turn is open
session.failurePolicy: mixed — a torn-tail repair that fails rejects the append (fail-closed), while a balanced/empty log yields no closers and unmatched-call repair degrades into explicit error results the model can read

session.name: write-lease-and-lazy-materialization
session.what: A created session is visible to this process immediately but has no filesystem footprint: `create` registers a pending entry and returns a handle with `materialized:false`, and the session materializes on its first append or on an explicit flush (index.ts:308-327; storage.ts:203-212). Write ownership is claimed in two stages — an in-process claim at write-open (`tracker.claimWrite(id)` / `pendingOf`, index.ts:340-366) and a cross-process kernel lock acquired lazily right before the first materializing write (`ensureLease`, storage.ts:345-354). The lock is a non-blocking `flock(2)` on `session.lock` inside the session directory, or a Windows named kernel semaphore derived from that path, so a crashed holder never blocks a successor and no expiry can expropriate a live writer.
invariants: At most one active writer per session id — in-process claim plus kernel lock; readers never touch the lock
An unmaterialized session has no durable artifact, so a crash before first materialization means the session never existed
A POSIX lock names an inode, so after locking the holder must verify the locked inode is still the file at the lock path
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed — SessionAlreadyOwnedError on contention (EBUSY on Windows, EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK on POSIX); a failed write-open releases both the kernel lock and the in-process claim before rethrowing

session.name: write-behind-batching-and-flush-barrier
session.what: Persistence is split into a best-effort append feed and an explicit durability barrier. Published events are routed by session id into a per-handle buffer that drains through the handle's mutation chain after a bounded batching window (`LIVE_WRITE_BATCH_MAX_DELAY_MS = 200`, storage.ts:36, 274-316); a drain failure retains the batch in order and pauses the timer so a later flush can retry loudly. The barrier is `session/flush`: the backend handles it by draining the routed buffer then flushing the handle (storage.ts:534-547), `SessionStore.flush(session)` awaits every listener in parallel and rethrows the first rejection (core/session/src/index.ts:1137-1154), and the service-wide `flushAll` aggregates per-session failures into an AggregateError (storage.ts:508-523).
invariants: Only a resolved flush promises durability; a resolved append is merely accepted, ordered, and visible to later reads on the same backend instance
A failed drain must retain the buffered events in order rather than dropping or reordering them
An empty created session becomes durably listable only through flush (handle.flush materializes a header-only artifact)
session.failurePolicy: mixed — append is best-effort and background drain failures are logged with the buffer retained; the flush barrier is fail-closed (first listener rejection is rethrown; service-wide flush raises AggregateError)

session.name: semantic-checkpoint-policy
session.what: `session-checkpoint-policy` converts the raw flush barrier into semantic durability checkpoints by wrapping three boundaries: `llm/stream` defers adapter dispatch until `ctx.sessions.flush(session)` resolves for the complete logged request prefix (index.ts:29-38, 64-68), `tools/execute` flushes the recorded call before a top-level tool body runs (index.ts:70-75), and `agent/pre-step` flushes everything the preceding step committed (index.ts:79-82). Nested tool dispatches deliberately reuse the durable outer call.
invariants: A checkpoint rejection must prevent the downstream adapter or tool body from running
Only top-level tool dispatches checkpoint (exec.parent must be undefined)
Checkpoints happen before side effects, not after, so a crash cannot leave an unlogged side effect
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed at both side-effect boundaries — a rejected flush means the model call or tool body is never invoked; a tool call cancelled after the checkpoint is answered with a canonical aborted result

session.name: session-format-adjacent-migration-chain
session.what: A session log declares one monotonic logical format version (`SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION = 3`) that is bumped only for structural changes; every historical generation keeps its own physical codec and one adjacent migration edge (v0->v1, v1->v2, v2->v3). `defineSessionFormatMigration` rejects a non-adjacent edge and `CompiledSessionFormatChain` compiles the complete inventory at construction time, failing if any `vN->vN+1` step for `0..currentVersion-1` is missing, duplicated, or leads past the current version (chain.ts:24-34, 50-87); a stored version selects a precompiled contiguous slice and an unsupported/newer version produces a status or typed refusal rather than a partial read. The shipped instance is generated build-static in `session-format-catalog` with all four codecs and all three edges wired directly, so historical readability does not depend on mounted plugins.
invariants: Migration edges are adjacent, uniquely named, and complete from v0 to the build's current version — no gaps, no dynamic lookup
Both sides of every edge must agree: the chain is only valid when an older writer's codec and the edge chain are compiled together
Filenames encode the generation: version 0 is `session.jsonl`, later generations are `session.v<N>.jsonl`
session.failurePolicy: mixed — header classification is fail-soft (returns a `current | migration-required | unsupported | malformed` status object), while restore, encode, and every migration step are fail-closed with SessionFormatError / SessionFormatUnsupportedMigrationError
constants: catalog currentVersion = 3, codecs v0/v1/v2/v3, migrations v0->v1, v1->v2, v2->v3 (packages/session/session-format-catalog/src/generated.ts:14-18)

session.name: generation-migration-publication
session.what: A historical generation is never rewritten: migration streams the source through the adjacent chain into a staged temp file, verifies the staged file's bytes and sha256 digest in an isolated Worker Thread against the expected id and event count, re-checks the source's physical identity (`dev:ino:size:mtime:ctime`) to detect a concurrent writer, and only then publishes the new current generation with `link()` (deliberately not `rename()`, so two processes cannot clobber each other) followed by a directory fsync (generation.ts:879-938, 812-838). If the link reports EEXIST, the competing current file is validated instead — it must match the staged bytes/digest — so concurrent migrations converge on one winner. Without a current generation, a legacy `session.jsonl` is migrated and adopted rather than rewritten.
invariants: Immutable generations: migration writes a new file and never mutates the historical source
Publication is exclusive and no-clobber (link fails with EEXIST); a lost race is resolved by validating the winner, not by overwriting
Staged bytes/digest must equal the verified bytes/digest before publication and the source identity must be unchanged after verification
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed — digest/identity mismatch, worker failure, or a non-collision filesystem error rejects and removes the staged temp; a cleanup failure joins the primary failure in an AggregateError

session.name: unknown-event-vocabulary-refusal
session.what: The append-only log is merge-extensible, so a reader that meets an event type it does not know must refuse rather than silently skip it unless the writer marked the event `ignorable: true` (packages/core/session/src/types.ts:473-483). The build publishes its vocabulary as a generated 56-entry set `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES`, and `validateStoredEvents` refuses any stored event outside that set that lacks the marker, plus the one retired shape hiding under a known type (`request/header` with reason `"fallback"`), before adopting and freezing the events (session-persistence/src/storage-contract.ts:69-104). Writes are also constrained at append time by `assertSessionEventEnvelope`, which admits only the seven envelope keys.
invariants: Absent `ignorable` means required: an unknown required event must refuse the whole read, never be dropped
Vocabulary growth for purely informational records is expressed by the persisted `ignorable` marker, not by runtime event-name registration
Retired pre-release shapes under a still-known event type are refused explicitly
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed — SessionFormatUnsupportedError for unknown/retired vocabulary, SessionPersistenceCorruptionError for records that fail validation
constants: Envelope keys accepted by a write: type, seq, time, data, surfaceOp, sourceEventSeqs, ignorable (packages/core/session/src/index.ts:204-217)

session.name: projection-registry-checkpoint-restore
session.what: `ctx.sessionProjections` drives per-session derived state: a domain registers a unit (key, zod state schema, pure `init`/`apply`, optional wire view, `stateVersion`) and the registry folds every committed `session/event` into every registered unit, notifying the change feed only when a unit's raw view changes by `Object.is` (session-projection/src/index.ts:199-223, 233-293). The same service is the read side of the persisted cache: `checkpoint()` emits detached `(ver, seq, val)` rows, `restoreFloor()` anchors a tail read one event below the lowest usable watermark so a shrunken log is detected, and `restore()`/`viewCheckpoint()` re-seed from version-matching rows and refold the tail (index.ts:396-435, 448-509). Consumers such as `sessionStats` and `turnOutline` supply only the pure fold and register it as an effect on their own fiber.
invariants: Unit functions must be synchronous and their state must be plain JSON — the persisted-cache precondition
A row is a fold shortcut, never authority: a `ver` mismatch, a malformed value, or a watermark past the stored log end discards it and refolds
Registration is fiber-owned: unloading a domain removes its key from snapshots, and a key shared by N registrants survives until the last one unloads
session.failurePolicy: mixed — registration conflicts and a discarded row with `baseSeq > 0` throw (fail-closed), while malformed or mismatched rows are skipped so a cold consumer sees the key as not-yet-available (fail-soft)
constants: Each unit declares a non-negative integer `stateVersion`; a mismatched or absent row pulls the restore floor to 0 (packages/session/session-projection/src/index.ts:270-272, 425-435)

session.name: projection-cache-write-behind
session.what: `SessionProjectionCache` persists the projection registry's checkpoints into the `session_projcache` storage domain on a throttled write-behind: a dirty counter plus a timer, plus three mandatory write points — session creation, every `turn/end`, and disposal (the live-to-cold moment) (session-projection-cache/src/index.ts:301-352). Each session document binds the checkpoint rows to a log identity (format version, createdAt, cwd, isSeeded, inherited cut) so a recreated id or a swapped persistence root cannot seed state folded from an unrelated log, and the domain is declared `layout: 'per-record'` so a bad document is discarded per session rather than bricking the medium.
invariants: The cached record is derived data only: a stale or unreadable record costs a longer tail replay, never a wrong value
Every write binds the rows to the session's log identity; identity mismatch means the record reads as absent
The write path flushes the log before persisting a checkpoint, so a cache record can lag the log but never lead it
session.failurePolicy: fail-soft — every durable write goes through `flushSoft`, which logs a warning and leaves the cache stale, self-healing on the next write; a cold-read write-back is fire-and-forget with a logged warning
constants: domain spec: name 'session_projcache', version 7, compatibleVersions [3,4,5,6], invalidRecords 'backup-and-skip', layout 'per-record' (packages/session/session-projection-cache/src/spec.ts:98-105)
writeEveryEvents = 200 and writeIntervalMs = 5000 are required deployment config (packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:162-166)

session.name: session-lifecycle-ownership
session.what: `SessionStore` separates construction, entry, and announcement so publication is transactional: `prepare` builds a detached session (validating id, cwd, seed continuity and header fields), `enter` installs the module-private append/publication hooks and returns a detach disposer, and `announce` emits `session/created` exactly once (core/session/src/index.ts:962-1004, 1028-1062, 1083-1111). `create` folds the three into one generator effect owned by the calling fiber, so a synchronous throwing creation listener rolls the attach back with a paired `session/disposed`; a session published outside that lifecycle persists nothing. Append/announce reentrancy is refused, and detach requested during dispatch is deferred until the dispatch unwinds.
invariants: One store entry per session id: enter re-checks for a duplicate so a stale prepared session can never displace a live one
A synchronous `session/created` throw vetoes and rolls back with a paired disposal; an async rejection only logs
Detach during an in-flight announce/append is deferred, never executed mid-dispatch
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed — duplicate id, already-attached, double-announce, reentrant append, and operations on a non-live session all throw; observer failures are contained per listener and logged

session.name: versioned-kv-storage-domain
session.what: Session durability sits on a two-layer storage stack: a `storage` hub with a registry of named backends (json, sqlite) and a `storage-domain` facility that opens schema-validated, change-emitting KV domains with a per-domain declaration (`name`, `version`, `compatibleVersions`, `layout`, `invalidRecords`). The JSON backend publishes whole documents atomically — same-directory temp opened `wx` at 0o600, fsync of the file, `rename()` over the target, fsync of the parent directory on POSIX — and its per-record layout treats a malformed or version-unaccepted document as foreign (reads as absent) so one bad record cannot brick a unit. The SQLite backend stamps `PRAGMA user_version` last and rejects any non-current stamped layout, and all domain writes are ordered durability -> memory -> `domain/changed` emission on a single per-domain chain.
invariants: A domain's declaration is the single source of its identity, version, layout, and record schema; validation happens at module load
Per-record reads accept only the current version plus declared compatibleVersions; any other stamp is discarded, never migrated in place
A delivered write is atomic on the medium and durable once resolved; the unit does not serialize concurrent writers — ordering is the caller's chain
session.failurePolicy: mixed — fail-closed for open/config/version-mismatch and whole-unit layouts; fail-soft for per-record JSON (foreign/stale/unreadable documents read as absent) and for `invalidRecords: 'backup-and-skip'` (record moved aside as `<key>.json.bak.<stamp>`, error logged, domain opens without it)
constants: JSON atomic publish: temp `.<uuid>.tmp`, open 'wx' mode 0o600, file fsync, rename, POSIX directory fsync (packages/storage/storage-json/src/atomic.ts:24-40)
per-record document shape `{version, record}` serialized with 2-space indent + trailing newline (packages/storage/storage-json/src/format.ts:97-99)

session.name: session-telemetry-record-capture
session.what: `ctx.sessionTelemetry` is a backend-agnostic record seam over the canonical log: a coordinator mirrors each committed event as one ledger record (deep copy of `data`, a redaction waterfall `session-telemetry/record`, then a non-blocking `emit`) and adds ops records for `agent-error` and shutdown, with a module-scope `handoffCursor` WeakMap advanced only when a record is handed over (session-telemetry/src/coordinator.ts:92-124, 151-162). Live capture is the default and installs listeners on session creation, disposal, event, flush and agent error; the shipped OTel backend instead uses `{capture:'on-demand', includeHistory:true}` and releases a prefix only when explicit feedback authorizes it, exporting OTel log records (not spans, not metrics) through a `LoggerProvider` + `BatchLogRecordProcessor` + OTLP/HTTP exporter with a backend-owned shutdown deadline.
invariants: Capture must never alter or rewrite the canonical session log; redaction applies to the exported copy only
A capture failure withholds exactly one record and never reaches the agent loop (per-record containment)
Only feedback authored by this session (seq >= inheritedEventCount) authorizes an OTel upload; fork-inherited feedback does not
session.failurePolicy: mixed — each record is contained fail-closed (a throwing listener or backend error logs and skips that record); backend shutdown rejection is caught and logged; the OTel plugin fails closed at load on invalid exporter/processor config
constants: deployment: exporter.timeoutMillis 1000, processor scheduledDelayMillis 10000, maxQueueSize 2048, maxExportBatchSize 2048, exportTimeoutMillis 1500 (packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:188-197)

session.name: llm-backed-session-title
session.what: `ctx.sessionTitle` folds the last `session/title` event into a client-visible `title` projection (stateVersion 1) plus a host-only `titleInput` unit, and exposes a single-slot provider registry; a provider receives the eligible human messages and returns a title plus the cited `messageSeqs` (session-title/src/index.ts:263-292, 295-311). Cadence is data-driven, not timer-driven: an eligible `user/message` records a pending revision and the model call starts only once the exact request route is logged, with a revision counter plus AbortController superseding stale work. Two model providers ship: `session-title-first-prompt-llm` (registered as the base-bundle row id `session-title-llm`, automatic = first-prompt) and the opt-in `session-title-all-prompts-llm`; the shared policy package appends a log-only `session/title-llm-request` event before dispatch.
invariants: A title is durable state in the log, not mutable metadata: readers fold the latest `session/title` event
Only one provider may be registered per service; a second registration is refused
A stale revision's result must never commit — supersession is checked before the append
session.failurePolicy: mixed — explicit callers (`rename`, `refresh`) get fail-closed SessionTitleInvalidError and service-disposed errors, while the automatic path contains provider failures, logs a warning, and keeps the deterministic fallback title
constants: title-LLM policy (no library defaults): targetWords 5, targetCjkCharacters 10, maxInputBytes 4096, maxOutputTokens 64, timeoutMs 60000 (packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:57-62)

session.name: session-controller-remote-facade
session.what: `SessionController` owns the generated `ctx.remote.session` namespace and is the host-side read/dispatch facade over the session domain: list, search, create, selectModel, modelCatalog, openWorkspacePath, rename, fork, prompt, attachment, updateQueue, cancel, page, follow (stream) and control (stream), plus sibling `skills` and `fileReferences` namespaces (api/session-controller/src/index.ts:121, 222-225). It never writes the log itself — reads go through `ctx.sessionQuery` (`observeSession`, `listSessions`, `traceSession`) or `ctx.sessions.get()` + `snapshotEvents()`, and history paging is message-aligned with a backward cursor (`page`, history.ts:77-111). Background activation is the promote step: after a cold snapshot is delivered, an observation is handed to the agent controller in a tracked promise whose failure is logged rather than surfaced.
invariants: No controller operation writes the session log or dispatches `session/flush`; durability stays with the agent loop and persistence backend
Every request is validated (address, page range, through-cursor) before any storage read
Cold reads must not activate an agent; activation is a separate, tracked promotion step
session.failurePolicy: mixed — request/address/state failures throw typed RemoteError codes (session/not-found, session/conflict, session/agent-busy, gateway/bad-request, subagent/unauthorized, ...), while background promotion failure and projection-lookup failure are logged and degrade

session.name: cross-session-reference-snapshot
session.what: `sessionReferenceResolver` injects another session's projected conversation into the live one as untrusted, read-only context: an `agent/pre-step` prepend hook parses `@[label](dsh-session:...)` mentions out of direct user messages and places each prepared snapshot immediately after the message that cited it (context/session-reference/src/index.ts:127-142, 298-355). The snapshot is read from persistence via `ctx.sessionQuery.readSurface(sessionId)` — never from a live Session object — and is budgeted: a per-source UTF-8 limit derived from the model context window (4 bytes/token heuristic) with a 64 KiB floor, oldest-first whole-message dropping, then head/tail truncation of the longest message; a truncated preview carries omission facts plus a spilled full-transcript locator when spill storage is composed.
invariants: The referenced content is untrusted and read-only: it never becomes durable history of the source session and never mutates persistence
A reference to the receiving session itself is refused, and at most MAX_REFERENCES sources are accepted per message
A preview that omits text must advertise the omission (bytes, whole messages) and locate the full transcript or state that it is unavailable
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed via SessionReferenceError codes (INVALID_CONFIG, INVALID_REFERENCE, SELF_REFERENCE, TOO_MANY, READ_FAILED, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, CANCELLED), with fail-soft degradation for optional spill storage (unavailable notice) and for a missing model context capacity (falls back to the default byte budget)
constants: spilled transcript fragments text at 64 Unicode code points per line (packages/context/session-reference/src/spill.ts:77)

session.name: deepseek-session-log-contribution
session.what: `session-log-deepseek` ships the canonical log suffix to the official DeepSeek API as a request field: it registers a `dsh_session_log` contribution whose value carries `version: 1`, the session format version, wire header, `afterSeq`/`throughSeq` and the events after the last accepted watermark, and its `accept` callback appends a `session-log-deepseek/delivery-accepted` event back into the canonical log (src/index.ts:157-191). The watermark is folded incrementally from those acceptance events with a WeakMap cache (`acceptedThrough`, index.ts:117-150), so restart recovery can conservatively resend an uncertain tail without a second store. The plugin is registered in production compositions but `enabled` defaults to false, and no shipped bundle row sets it, so the contribution is inert there.
invariants: The acceptance watermark lives in the canonical log; no separate delivery store exists
A delivery-accepted event must name this session, reference an earlier seq, and carry a well-formed format version — otherwise it is a malformed log
Unaccepted suffixes are resent; accepted prefixes are never re-sent
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed on read (throws on a missing event below the captured length, a malformed acceptance format version, or a malformed watermark), with degrade-to-undefined when the request has no session id or the session is not live

context.name: compaction-engine-seam
context.what: `ctx.compaction` is an abstract `CompactionEngine` service with three entry points: `compactIfNeeded(agent, trigger, signal)` for automatic policy (`pressure` or `context-overflow`), `compactNow(agent, signal, sourceCommandId)` for an explicit idle-session compaction, and `compactRegion(start, end, agent, signal)` for a caller-chosen inclusive surface span. Implementations own trigger policy, retention and summarization; the seam fixes the contract that a successful run replaces the selected surface span with one summary node and prevents concurrent compaction of the same session. Exactly one implementation is loaded per context.
invariants: the replacement user message must use `compactCheckpointSource` with the transaction's CompactionId so consumers can recognise it independently of the backend
compactRegion edges name surface POSITIONS, not numeric seq order, and must be tool-pairing balanced
context.failurePolicy: mixed - the abstract seam declares `ManualCompactionError` codes busy/cancelled/changed/summary/commit/persistence for the manual path and an exact abort reason for cancellation; a failed attempt stays visible in the log
constants: ManualCompactionErrorCode: busy, cancelled, changed, summary, commit, persistence

context.name: compaction-durable-bracket-transaction
context.what: One compaction run is a durable transaction bracketed by two log markers. `compaction/start` (carrying compactionId, optional sourceCommandId and the owning turn) is appended BEFORE summarization yields and acts as the lock; an unmatched start makes any other compaction attempt fail busy, unless a later constructor-seed boundary proves the marker belongs to an earlier session lifecycle. After summarization the selected span is re-asserted stable, then `compaction/summary` and the replacement `user/message` are appended together without yielding, and `compaction/end` closes the bracket. A closure failure deliberately leaves the unmatched start detectable; on error the end marker records the errorChain.
invariants: the durable start marker is the lock - never a process-local flag
a summary may only be committed if the selected span is still the same present, contiguous, equally priced, balanced replacement target
`compaction/end` is attempted on every exit path, including failure
context.failurePolicy: fail-closed - the unmatched `compaction/start` marker makes subsequent compaction attempts fail busy rather than run concurrently; failed attempts remain durable in the log

context.name: surface-replace-projection
context.what: The model-visible surface is a projection over the append-only log, not a rewrite of it. `SurfaceManager` folds surface-eligible events (system/message, user/message, assistant/message, tool/result) into an ordered node list, applying `surfaceOp: 'append'` at the tail or `surfaceOp: {op:'replace', startSeq, endSeq}` as a positional substitution, and tracks a monotonic `replaceGeneration`. Compaction lands as a replace whose `sourceEventSeqs` must cite every shadowed node; append-origin events remain the durable human transcript.
invariants: `sourceEventSeqs` must densely cite earlier events, contain no duplicates, and include every shadowed surface node
a replacement covering surface node 0 while it holds the system prompt must itself be a system/message over exactly that node
a tool/result replacement must rewrite exactly one current tool/result and may change only content
context.failurePolicy: fail-closed - every rule is an assertion in `planSurfaceEvent`; a violation throws and the fold refuses the event instead of producing a divergent surface

context.name: pressure-threshold-compaction-policy
context.what: `compaction-basic` decides automatic compaction from the routed model's own capacity: it reads the latest durable `request/header` config, resolves that exact provider/model's context window through `ctx.llm.resolveModelInfo`, scales the policy into `thresholdTokens = floor(contextWindow * thresholdRatio)` and `retainTokens = floor(contextWindow * retainRatio)`, and compacts only when the measured total reaches the threshold. It lands the model-free prune pass first, remeasures, then loops up to `compactionRetries` summary attempts; per-model overrides can replace every policy field for one exact route.
invariants: retainTokens must be strictly less than thresholdTokens
retainRatio must be strictly less than thresholdRatio
policy for a route with no declared contextWindow raises TargetPressureConfigError instead of guessing
context.failurePolicy: mixed - a step-pressure failure is logged as a warning and the turn continues; a missing context capacity is reported once per target and suppressed afterwards; exhausting all retries still above threshold throws

context.name: context-overflow-recovery
context.what: When a model attempt fails with the provider-confirmed context-window-exceeded code, `compaction-basic` intercepts the `agent/request-error` waterfall, forces a compaction bypassing the normal threshold and retained-tail policy (`selectCompactableRange(..., 0)`), and returns `{kind:'retry'}` so the loop retries the step from the replacement surface. The retry budget is per agent and is reset on idle and on any successful `assistant/message`, so tool-call continuations start a fresh overflow sequence.
invariants: overflow compaction ignores the pressure threshold and retention floor
a durable surface generation advance is required before a retry is requested
context.failurePolicy: fail-soft - a recovery failure that nonetheless produced durable surface progress still counts as retry proof and increments the budget; a recovery failure with no durable progress logs a warning and preserves the original request error; cancellation always prevents the retry

context.name: tool-result-pruner
context.what: A model-free, replay-safe pruner service (`ctx.toolResultPruner`) that rewrites over-budget tool results in place on the current surface. It measures text content in Unicode code points (non-text blocks cost zero), and for any result above `thresholdChars` keeps a head and a tail around a fixed marker, splitting by code point so a surrogate pair is never broken. Each rewrite appends a `compaction/prune` shadow-price event immediately before the replacement `tool/result` carrying a single-node replace surfaceOp citing the shadowed seq.
invariants: headChars + marker + tailChars must be at most thresholdChars
the emitted replacement must be strictly smaller than the original and within threshold
each metering event and its replacement are appended synchronously adjacent
context.failurePolicy: fail-closed - a replacement that would not shrink or that exceeds the threshold throws; replacements committed earlier in the same pass remain durable

context.name: replay-aware-token-meter
context.what: `ctx.tokenMeter` is the single measurement service: it replays each session's durable tail into a per-session fold (surface nodes with prices, the latest request header, the open step, and a measurement anchor) and reports baseline, surface delta and total tokens. Provider usage is reused only when the anchored call's canonical request envelope equals the current header and its total is no lower than the fully repriced anchor; otherwise the whole envelope and surface are repriced. It also registers the `tokenUsage`, `contextPressure` and `contextBreakdown` session projections so clients read the same numbers.
invariants: every fallible step of the fold (surface plan, anchor validation) runs before any state mutation, so a malformed event stays unread on retry instead of half-applying
measurement is O(surface) and clones its positional nodes
context.failurePolicy: fail-closed - a `step/start` without a matching end, an unmatched `step/end`, or an `assistant/message` with no matching `step/start` throws during the fold
constants: no settings are supported (TokenMeterConfig rejects every key)

context.name: system-prompt-assembly
context.what: `ctx.systemPrompt` assembles the model input from named, scoped contributions: sections (ordered text), contexts (dynamic runtime-context fragments), variable providers, and tool-schema providers. Section positions come from a central `SECTION_ORDERS` table so first-party sections cannot collide, tools are canonically ordered by a configured `toolOrder` with a mandatory `<unlisted-tools>` rest marker (default lexicographic), and `{{variable}}` references are strict - a malformed, unknown or undefined reference throws and substituted text is not rescanned. Later layers (agent scope) shadow earlier ones by name.
invariants: toolOrder must contain the `<unlisted-tools>` rest entry exactly once and may not name an unregistered tool
`{{variable}}` references are strict and never resolved through Object.prototype
a scoped registration shadows the global one with the same name instead of duplicating it
context.failurePolicy: fail-closed - registration conflicts, unknown order entries and bad variable references all throw, at load time where possible and at assembly time otherwise
constants: SECTION_ORDERS span -1000 (harness identity) to 10200 (deployment persona suffix)

context.name: runtime-context-snapshot-projection
context.what: Dynamic per-step context (sandbox policy, approval policy, delegation policy, time, tmux, ...) is committed as an append-origin `user/message` whose text is a single snapshot that explicitly supersedes earlier snapshots. `RuntimeContextProjection` restores the last retained snapshot by scanning the durable log newest-first against the current surface, follows `session/event` afterwards, and only emits a new snapshot when the rendered value differs; when every contributor goes away it emits a fixed cleared marker instead of deleting history.
invariants: a snapshot is only emitted when its rendered value differs from the retained one
the cleared marker carries no contributing sections to attribute
restoration is durable, not process-local - a resumed process reconstructs the retained snapshot from the log
context.failurePolicy: fail-soft - absence of any contributor means no snapshot is emitted and the cleared marker (if any) is only written once
constants: CLEARED = 'Current runtime context: none. Earlier runtime-context snapshots no longer apply.'

context.name: prompt-series-and-surface-generation-tracking
context.what: The loop keeps provider prompt-cache continuity explicit. `SystemPromptProjection` decides per step whether the rendered prompt is appended as a new `system/message` after the cached history (a capable route in an unbroken series) or normalises surface node 0 and empties later active system nodes (an incapable route, a broken series, or a cleared prompt), using `replace` intents. The decision inputs are the route's in-history capability, whether the step starts a series, and whether the prompt text changed; dormant empty tails do not force repeated replacements.
invariants: the first prompt, even empty, reserves surface node 0
empty tails are inert: they supply no effective text and need no repeated replacement
a series restart is triggered by a pre-step declaration, a surface replacement generation change, or an assembled-tool change
context.failurePolicy: fail-soft - an unchanged prompt produces no commit at all, so no unnecessary surface churn

context.name: agent-instructions-discovery
context.what: A workspace instruction loader that discovers and injects AGENTS.md-compatible files. It resolves the project root from configured markers, walks the ancestor chain plus descendant directories between the root and any touched path, loads user-global instructions from `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md`, dedups by directory, hashes content into an instruction digest, and renders the result as a `<system-reminder>` envelope with the closing tag escaped. Touches of read/write/edit file paths trigger re-projection of the relevant scope instructions.
invariants: instruction content is identified by a digest so unchanged files do not re-inject
the closing `</system-reminder>` sequence in instruction text is escaped
a visible baseline is replaced only when its identity changes
context.failurePolicy: fail-soft - a disabled byte budget or a missing filesystem service yields no projection; projection composes are serialized per agent

context.name: file-reference-seam
context.what: `ctx.fileReferences` is an abstract host capability for cancellable `@`-path discovery: a UI submits the path text following `@` or `@"` and receives deterministic path-only candidates bounded by the agent's session cwd. The plugin also exports the exact model-facing `FILE_REFERENCE_PROMPT` guidance and the `@`-token grammar (`activeAtToken`, `formatFileMention`) so renderer and engine agree on the syntax. There is no production caller inside the host core - the consumer is the browser client's input surface.
invariants: discovery is bounded by the agent's session cwd
candidates are path-only; the model is told not to claim it inspected a file before reading it
context.failurePolicy: fail-soft - cancellable async discovery; the seam declares no retry or caching

context.name: tmux-location-context-injection
context.what: An opt-in pre-step listener pulls the agent process's tmux location once per turn (step 1) through the `ctx.shell` executor and injects it as durable, source-attributed context naming session, window, pane and the window layout. Genuineness is verified by matching the pane's `#{pane_tty}` against this process's own controlling terminal, so a terminal that merely inherited `$TMUX`/`$TMUX_PANE` from an ancestor reads as "not in tmux". Re-injection only happens when the rendered state changed, with an optional floor between injections.
invariants: the durable injection is compared on its stable state block, excluding the volatile turn preamble
the schedule is reconstructed from the durable log, so it survives compaction and process restarts
context.failurePolicy: fail-open - absent tmux environment, an inherited-only environment, an absent `ctx.shell`, or a failed query is a no-op, and an executor rejection is logged as a warning and the turn continues
constants: TMUX_FIELDS = 8 tab-separated format fields including window_layout
refreshIntervalMs: optional non-negative safe integer, 0/omitted means inject on every eligible change

context.name: time-context-injection
context.what: A pre-step listener injects a timestamp reading (turn, step, formatted time, optional browser time zone, and elapsed time since the preceding model-visible message or step context) as durable plugin-sourced context. A `timeContext` session projection (stateVersion 2) tracks last message time, last injection time and last turn injection time so re-injection is rate-limited and turn boundaries reset the per-turn gate.
invariants: an invalid or unresolvable time zone throws at plugin apply, not at request time
refreshIntervalMs must be a non-negative safe integer
context.failurePolicy: fail-closed at load (bad time zone or interval throws), fail-soft at request time (re-injection suppressed while within the interval)

context.name: context-window-resolution
context.what: Context capacity is adapter-owned model metadata, not a harness constant. `ctx.llm.resolveModelInfo(provider, model)` normalises the adapter's resolved model info and rejects a non-positive or non-integer `contextWindow`; the loop copies the resolved window into the durable `request/context` event, and compaction-basic reads it back to scale its pressure threshold. Model info carries context and max-output metadata alongside the model id.
invariants: a declared contextWindow must be a positive integer
the resolved envelope is persisted on `request/context` so later policy can be re-derived from the log
context.failurePolicy: fail-closed - a malformed adapter context throws during normalisation rather than being clamped

tools.name: tool-registry-and-scoped-visibility
tools.what: `ToolRuntime` (Cordis Service at `ctx.tools`, `static inject = ['systemPrompt']`) is the single registry: `register()` inserts a `ToolDefinition` into a scoped `ToolLayer`, `restrict()` appends a compiled allow/deny filter, `guard()` appends a monotonic guard, and `view(scope)` derives one `ToolView { visible, knownNames, restrictableNames }` per scope in a single layer traversal. Restrictions filter only the INHERITED surface (the global layer plus ancestor layers), never the scope's own registrations, and the reserved `run_code` transport is appended last, outside capability filtering, only for scopes whose mode presents it. Scoped registrations shadow inherited ones by name; a duplicate name inside one layer, the reserved name, an empty/no-op restriction and a restriction naming an unknown or reserved tool all throw at registration time. `schemas(scope)` projects visible definitions onto only name/description/parameters, so `execute`, `output`, `timeoutMs` and `isConcurrencySafe` are never model-visible, and `executionMode()` classifies overlap fail-closed.
invariants: `register()` rejects the reserved PTC name `run_code` unconditionally, so a name free under the deployment default can never collide once a preset mounts a code mode (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1044-1046).
A restriction filters what a scope INHERITS (global plus ancestor layers) and never what its own layer registers (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1127-1138).

`executionMode()` is fail-closed: only an exact `true` from `isConcurrencySafe` is parallel; unknown, hidden, undeclared, invalid or throwing classifiers are exclusive (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1266-1275).
tools.failurePolicy: fail-closed — duplicate/scoped-conflict/reserved-name/unknown-restriction-target all throw at registration; an invisible tool or a `ptc`-collapsed model-direct call resolves to `undefined` and materializes as an `UNKNOWN_TOOL` error result.
constants: no cap on registered-tool count or restriction-entry count

tools.name: tool-schema-dsl-and-output-contract
tools.what: Tools declare arguments and results in an author-facing DSL (`defineTool({ parameters, output })`) that `schema.ts` compiles to the enforced raw JSON Schema subset of `json-schema.ts` through a stack-safe task graph (`runSchemaCompiler`), rejecting author-only keys, `type` together with `oneOf`, a missing `additionalProperties` on an object node and circular property maps. Every successful body value is snapshotted to lossless JSON, validated against `output.schema` inside `createSuccessResult`, deep-frozen and projected through the pure `output.render` (plus `presentationMeta` for top-level calls only). `defineTool` re-validates arguments at execute time (`ToolArgsError`, code `INVALID_ARGS`), while `presentCall`/`presentResult`/`isConcurrencySafe` validate softly and fall back to `undefined`/`false` so a replay of obsolete logged arguments can never throw.
invariants: Objects must state openness explicitly: `additionalProperties` must be present and boolean, so a nested or output object never acquires an accidental JSON Schema default (packages/core/tools/src/schema.ts:365-369).

The registry snapshots `finalizeContent` when the call starts and invokes it exactly once for every normalized outcome, including pipeline failures that bypass `tools/post-execute` (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:228-239, 1388-1400).
`presentCall`/`presentResult` must never throw: a UI may call them during live streaming AND during session-log replay (packages/core/tools/src/schema.ts:594-609).
tools.failurePolicy: mixed — author/schema errors and argument violations fail closed (throw at define/execute time); a value that is not lossless JSON or violates `output.schema` fails closed as `ToolOutputError` (code `INVALID_TOOL_OUTPUT`); a throwing `render`/`presentationMeta` projector is converted into that same canonical invalid-output error instead of escaping.
constants: type inference bounded to 16 container levels before falling back to `JsonValue` (packages/core/tools/src/schema.ts:154)

tools.name: tool-execution-pipeline-and-guards
tools.what: One call traverses `tools/pre-execute` (waterfall returning `PreToolDecision` allow/deny/ask), then monotonic guards, then `tools/execute` (around-dispatch waterfall), then the tool body, then `tools/post-execute` (accept/replace/block), then the definition-owned `finalizeContent`, then lossless materialization and finally the `tools/result` emit. The ordered stages are exposed to the loop as a symbol-keyed `ToolRuntimeScheduler` (`prepare`/`dispatch`/`finalize`/`finish`, `TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER`) so policy stays model-ordered while only the body overlaps. Guards registered through `tools.guard()` have no allow result, so listener ordering can never turn a denial back into permission; an `ask` decision resolves through the optional `approval` seam and degrades to denial when the seam or the agent is absent. The package's own invariant companion (`tools-invariant`) fails when a stage repeats, when `execute` does not follow `pre-execute`, or when the published `tools/result` execution/outcome is not frozen.
invariants: A guard can only deny; no guard can force-allow a call another guard denied (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:696-704, 1108-1118).
A collapsed (`ptc`) or unknown call must never reach `pre-execute`, an approval `ask`, or guards (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1363-1371).

`tools/result` observers receive a frozen execution and a frozen, lossless-JSON outcome; listener failures are contained and only logged (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1646-1666; packages/core/tools/src/invariant.ts:22-30).
tools.failurePolicy: mixed — authorization is fail-closed (deny, ask-without-channel and a guard reason each materialize an `isError` result) and observers are fail-soft (a throwing `tools/result` listener is logged, a throwing waterfall listener turns the call into an `isError` result rather than rejecting the caller).
constants: `TOOL_ABORTED` = 'ABORTED' and `TOOL_ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH` = 'ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH' are the two canonical cancellation codes (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:462-465)
`ToolRunContext.deferContext()` queues context on the execution and the loop appends it only after the `tool/result` (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:397-414)

tools.name: tool-presentation-modes-and-ptc-collapse
tools.what: One registry serves three presentation modes — `native`, `ptc`, `both` (`Config.mode`, default `native`) — resolved per scope by `modeFor()` with nearest-layer-wins, and overridable per agent by `tools.presentAs(mode)`, which additionally registers scope-local `tools:ptc-only` and `tools:sdk` prompt sections. Under `ptc` the model sees only `run_code` plus a generated SDK section (`renderToolsSdk` for TypeScript, `renderToolsSdkPy` for Python), and the SAME predicate (`collapses`) denies a model-direct call naming any other tool with `UNKNOWN_TOOL` plus a route hint, while a nested sub-dispatch (a `parent` token set) may call any visible tool. `run_code` is a stateless transport built lazily by `createRunCodeTool`; its `description` and `parameters` are lazy getters that resolve the mounted runtime's language flavor at schema-emission time, and a non-native mode with no `ctx.codeRuntime`, or a runtime whose `language` has no registered renderer, fails prompt assembly loudly.
invariants: The prompt rule and the executor denial share ONE predicate, so the prompt can never state a rule the registry does not enforce (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:847-855, 1314-1316).

`run_code` is reserved presentation infrastructure: never in the global layer, never shadowable, never restrictable, and invalid in `toolOrder` under `ptc` (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:905-925, 1075-1077).
`both` renders the collapse section empty, because native calls do execute there so the rule would be false (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:844).
tools.failurePolicy: fail-closed — an absent code runtime or an unknown runtime language throws at prompt-assembly time; a model-direct call to a non-`run_code` tool under `ptc` becomes an `isError` `UNKNOWN_TOOL` result carrying the route hint.
constants: `maxParallelSubCalls` default 10 is the `run_code` program's overlap cap (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:660-666, 785, 921)

tools.name: parallel-tool-execution-with-commit-ordering
tools.what: `executeToolCalls(ctx, turn, step, toolCalls, signal, acceptContext)` plans one assistant step's calls and partitions them by live `ctx.tools.executionMode`: a `parallel` first call takes the whole remaining group, anything else is a one-call exclusive barrier. Inside `runGroup`, `fillPool()` starts calls while `inFlight.size < maxParallelToolCalls` (default 10), and only the `dispatch` stage overlaps — ordered `prepare` (pre-execute plus guards) is awaited inside the lane before the next start. Results commit through a `commitReady()` cursor that advances only across CONTIGUOUS model-order slots, so `finalize`/`finish` (post-execute), the `tool/result` append and `additionalContexts` acceptance are strictly model-ordered even though tool bodies overlap; a later call whose live mode is no longer parallel breaks the pool and stays for the next barrier. The same submission-ordered contract is re-implemented inside `run_code` for nested sub-dispatches, with `maxParallelSubCalls` as the cap.
invariants: Ordered policy is never overlapped: only the around-dispatch/body stage runs concurrently, while pre-execute, post-execute and the durable appends stay in one ordered lane (packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:86-89, 146-160, 216-218).

Dispatch overlaps, results do not: `commitReady()` stops at the first unset slot, so a slow early call blocks later commits but never later dispatch (packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:147-160).

A scheduler failure drains started dispatches and rethrows WITHOUT fabricating tool results; only cancellation fabricates the ordered synthetic `ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH` results (packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:113-121, 232-236).
tools.failurePolicy: mixed — abort is fail-soft (started calls drain and commit, unstarted calls receive ordered synthetic `isError` results so replay stays valid); an internal scheduler failure is fail-closed (replenishment stops, already-started dispatches drain via `Promise.allSettled`, the first error is rethrown and no results are fabricated).
constants: adapter validation: `maxParallelToolCalls` must be a positive integer or config resolution throws (packages/core/agent-loop/src/index.ts:191-195)

tools.name: cooperative-cancellation-classification
tools.what: Cancellation is caller-owned and cooperative: every `ToolExecutionInput` requires an `AbortSignal`, the registry keeps the original caller signal outside the wrapper-mutable execution object (`ToolCancellationState`), and after the around-dispatch wrappers run it re-fuses the caller signal with whatever replacement a wrapper installed (`fuseToolSignals`) so a replacement cannot detach caller cancellation. Which canonical failure wins depends solely on whether the body was invoked — `ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH` before, `ABORTED` after — and a started promise is never abandoned: it reaches quiescence before its outcome is replaced. The loop mirrors the split at the step boundary by appending synthetic `ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH` results, and `session-checkpoint-policy` consumes the same `tools/execute` seam to flush the session before a body runs and returns the same pre-dispatch abort result.
invariants: The registry re-fuses the original caller signal before the body, so an around-wrapper's signal replacement cannot detach caller cancellation (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:145-155, 1517-1533).
A started tool promise is never abandoned — it is awaited to quiescence and only its outcome is replaced (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:218-222, 226-239).
Caller cancellation replaces only a SUCCESSFUL accepted outcome; a tool-owned structured error survives it (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:156-166, 1580-1585).
tools.failurePolicy: mixed — cancellation is fail-closed for the call (it becomes an `isError` result with a canonical code) but fail-soft for the pipeline (post-execute still runs and deferred context is preserved on the aborted result).
constants: `TOOL_ABORTED` = 'ABORTED' when the body was invoked, `TOOL_ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH` = 'ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH' when it was not (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:462-465, 1507-1515)
aborted result text 'Error: tool call aborted' / 'Error: tool call aborted before dispatch' (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1909-1934)

tools.name: tool-call-timeout-policy
tools.what: `ToolDefinition.timeoutMs` is a cooperative budget that is never sent to the model (`schemaOf` whitelists only name/description/parameters); the `timeout-policy` plugin wraps `tools/execute`, looks the definition up with `ctx.tools.get(exec.name, exec.agent)` and — only when a budget is declared — installs `using d = deadline(exec.signal, timeoutMs, TOOL_TIMEOUT)`, swaps `exec.signal` to the derived signal for the delegated dispatch, and restores the caller signal in `finally`. If and only if ITS OWN timer fired (`timeoutOf(d.signal, TOOL_TIMEOUT) !== undefined`, which distinguishes it from a nested outer deadline) the wrapper replaces whatever the tool returned with a structured `TOOL_TIMEOUT` error result. The shared `util/timeout` library owns `clampTimeout` (`min(requested ?? def, max)`), `deadline`, the rearmable `idleWatchdog` and `timeoutOf`; it only notifies through abort signals, so each capability still has to stop its own work.
invariants: Enforcement is cooperative: a tool that ignores `exec.signal` is awaited indefinitely, so declaring `timeoutMs` asserts the tool forwards the signal to an implementation that can reach quiescence (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:240-247).

Expiry is scoped by the plugin's own code, so a nested outer deadline reads as an ordinary upstream cancel rather than as this plugin's timeout (packages/guard/timeout-policy/src/index.ts:18-25, 69-75).
The caller's own signal is restored after dispatch so post-execute listeners never see the plugin's possibly-aborted timeout signal (packages/guard/timeout-policy/src/index.ts:61-66, 77-79).
tools.failurePolicy: mixed — load/validation fails closed (`assertTimerDelay` rejects a non-positive, non-finite or over-cap delay) and the mapped expiry is fail-closed for the model (an `isError` `TOOL_TIMEOUT` result replaces the tool's own return), but a tool that never observes its signal is not forcibly stopped.
constants: `TOOL_TIMEOUT` = 'TOOL_TIMEOUT', used as both the deadline classification code and the structured error code (packages/guard/timeout-policy/src/index.ts:25)
`timeoutMs <= 0` is the internal no-timer sentinel inside `deadline`, while public configs reject zero (packages/util/timeout/src/index.ts:45-55, 96-100)
search tools attach 30_000 ms; bash-local defaults 120_000 and caps at 600_000 (packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/search-core.ts:43; packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:107-108)

tools.name: repeat-tool-call-reminder-guard
tools.what: `repeat-tool-reminder` is an advisory per-agent consecutive-repeat detector registered as a `tools/post-execute` waterfall listener plus an `agent/pre-step` reset hook. It canonicalizes a call's arguments (deep key sort through `sortJsonValue` then `JSON.stringify`), keys a per-agent `WeakMap<Agent, Chain>` on `[name, canonical]`, and when the run length hits a configured threshold prepends a plugin-sourced `UserMessage` onto whatever the downstream decision was — including a `block` — through `additionalContexts`. It observes and enriches but never vetoes or rewrites: it counts FIRST, then delegates through `next()`. `include`/`exclude` are `*`-wildcard patterns compiled to anchored RegExps; untracked calls are transparent (neither count nor reset), and a user interjection deletes the chain.
invariants: Observe-and-enrich, never veto: counting happens before delegation and the reminder rides `additionalContexts` on both decision variants (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:209-224).
