Counting lives in post-execute because denied calls flow through the same waterfall, and a model hammering a denied call is exactly the loop worth breaking (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:181-188).

The chain key always compares the FULL canonical string; `argumentsPreviewChars` bounds only the model-visible quote, never detection (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:35-42, 194-202).
tools.failurePolicy: mixed — fail-closed at plugin load (an empty `thresholds` list, a non-integer, a value below 2, a duplicate, or an `argumentsPreviewChars` below 1 all throw) and fail-open at runtime for the guarded call (it only prepends context and always calls `next()`).
constants: every threshold must be an integer >= 2 with no duplicates (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:128-141)
the first threshold uses the gentle text, keyed to `thresholds[0]` rather than a literal count (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:59-67, 199-202)

tools.name: output-spill-with-preview-and-locator
tools.what: `spill-policy` prepends a `tools/post-execute` listener that first awaits `next()`, then applies, in order: the decision must be `accept`, must not replace `value`, the call must be top-level (`exec.parent === undefined`) and the tool must not be `read`; the resulting content must be all-text and its UTF-8 length must exceed `maxInlineBytes`. It then saves the FULL text through the optional `ctx.spillStore.saveText` (owner `{sessionId}`, source `{kind:'tool', toolName, callId, label}`) and replaces the model-facing content with a head/tail preview plus a formatted notice carrying the backend locator and retrieval hint. A second arm applies the same cap to `tools/ptc-dispatch-log`, so a `run_code` sub-call's durable log copy shrinks while the program's value stays complete. `LocalSpillStore` writes to `<root>/session-<sha256(sessionId)[0..12]>/<6-random-hex>-<encodedName>` with a `wx` create at mode 0o600 inside a 0o700 directory, and a best-effort activation sweep deletes spilled files older than `cleanupPeriodDays`.
invariants: The policy NEVER emits a replacement larger than the cap: the notice's worst-case byte cost is reserved INSIDE `maxInlineBytes` before the preview budget is computed, and when the notice alone exceeds the cap the inline content is kept (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:158-181).
A spill failure must NEVER turn a successful tool call into an `isError` or hide the inline result (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:33-35, 149-156).
A bad config must fail the deployment, not the tool: `maxInlineBytes` is validated at load, never per call (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:109-114).
tools.failurePolicy: fail-soft on every spill path (no owner session, no `ctx.spillStore`, a `saveText` rejection, or no within-cap replacement each log a warning through `ctx.logger.warn` and keep the original decision/content), fail-closed at load for an invalid `maxInlineBytes`; the store seam itself is fail-closed (it rejects on a real storage failure and leaves degradation to the caller).
constants: omitted `maxInlineBytes` means the plugin registers nothing at all (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:105-108); the shipped base profile sets 50000 (packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:386)
notice reserve = `Buffer.byteLength(notice, 'utf8') + 2` and `previewBudget = Math.max(0, cap - reserve)` (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:166-167)
spill file: `open(path, 'wx', 0o600)` inside `mkdir(..., { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })`, name = 6 random bytes hex + encoded suggested name (packages/spill/spill-local/src/store.ts:109-115)

`cleanupPeriodDays` default 30, `0` disables the sweep, and only files strictly older than the cutoff expire (packages/spill/spill-local/src/index.ts:68, 96; packages/spill/spill-local/src/cleanup.ts:256)

tools.name: bounded-output-retention
tools.what: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-output-retention` is a deliberately dependency-light library (no `ctx`, no registration, no events) that owns only the mechanical question 'what did we keep, what did we omit?'. `ItemRetainer` bounds an ordered stream of logical units with the single v1 strategy `{ kind: 'head', maxItems }`, while `TextRetainer` bounds a byte-oriented stream with `head`/`tail`/`headTail` over one shared prefix/suffix accumulator, trimming a partial UTF-8 sequence at each cut ONLY when a real omitted gap exists and reporting omission against the bytes ACTUALLY returned. `describeOmitted`/`formatRetentionNotice` standardize the omission wording while the calling tool supplies the recovery sentence. Production importers include the spill policy, the terminal renderer, the search core, the jobs tool and the session-reference projection.
invariants: The library owns only retention mechanics: file grouping, line numbering, exit codes, provider error states and the model-facing prose stay in the tool (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:1-20).
`truncated` means 'the retainer omitted otherwise-available content because of a budget' and never 'the upstream was incomplete' (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:10-15).

With nothing omitted the head|tail split is artificial, so `finish()` decodes the contiguous whole; only a real gap makes each side a true UTF-8-trimmed cut (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:356-370).
tools.failurePolicy: fail-closed on a malformed budget (`assertBudget` throws from the constructor for a negative or non-integer cap); the retainers never throw on content and never reject.
constants: v1 item strategy is head-only: `{ kind: 'head', maxItems }` (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:86-91)
UTF-8 boundary trim scans back at most 3 continuation bytes (max sequence is 4) (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:211-222)
`TextRetainer` holds at most `prefixCap + suffixCap + one chunk` in memory (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:243-245)
no global thresholds: every cap is caller-supplied

tools.name: file-tool-suite-with-observation-policy
tools.what: `tool-fs` registers the model-facing `read`, `write`, `edit` (and `read_image` when `attachments` is mounted) over the `ctx.fs` seam; `read` windows lines (`READ_LIMIT` 2000), caps a single line at 2000 characters and the selected lines at 50 KiB, and switches to `streamText` at 10 MiB. Mutations pass through the single-slot `fs/write-intent` and `fs/edit-intent` waterfalls, which `fs-observation-policy` occupies with a per-owner `WeakMap<session, Map<targetKey, FsObservation>>`: an unseen or confirmed-absent target yields `createIfAbsent`, a present one yields `replaceIfVersion` at the observed version, and an unseen EDIT is rejected with `FS_NOT_OBSERVED` before any read. `LocalFileSystem` enforces the intent inside a per-`targetKey` FIFO lock and publishes through a private synced staging file (0o700 directory, `'wx'` 0o600 temp, `handle.sync()`), using a hard-link no-clobber primitive for `createIfAbsent`. `present` is the delivery endpoint: it validates 1..`maxFiles` existing regular files inside an OPEN turn and appends a durable `deliverables/presented` event only for a non-error result.
invariants: Without the observation policy the tools retain the bare provider's unconditional mutation behavior; the gate occupies the single decision slot and does NOT call `next()` (packages/fs/fs-observation-policy/src/index.ts:2-5, 116-122).
`fs/observed` must stay synchronous and non-throwing, because emit does not await promises and successful mutations have already committed (packages/fs/fs-observation-policy/src/index.ts:124-129).

A stale edit must report `FS_STALE_VERSION`, not `FS_EDIT_NOT_FOUND`/`FS_AMBIGUOUS_EDIT` against newer content, so the version guard runs BEFORE literal matching (packages/fs/fs-local/src/index.ts:238-241).
The backend `cwd` is a resolution default, not a containment boundary (packages/fs/fs-local/src/index.ts:60-63).
tools.failurePolicy: mixed — guarded mutations are fail-closed (a version mismatch, an unobserved edit and a blind overwrite each throw a coded `FsError`), `present` validation is fail-closed (non-existent or non-regular file, no open turn, over-cap file count all throw) while its durable event is fail-soft (skipped when the result is an error), and read truncation is fail-soft data on the result.
constants: staging: directory mode 0o700, temp file `<basename>.tmp` opened `'wx'` 0o600, `handle.sync()` before publication (packages/fs/fs-local/src/fsio.ts:599, 603, 609)
`createIfAbsent` publishes with `link()` (no-replace) and maps a collision to `FS_NOT_OBSERVED` (packages/fs/fs-local/src/fsio.ts:536-551, 567)

tools.name: string-replace-patch-editing
tools.what: `str_replace_editor` is an alternative single editor tool offering `view`, `create`, `str_replace` and `insert` over `ctx.fs`. `create` refuses an existing file and dispatches `fs/write-intent` defaulting to `{kind:'createIfAbsent'}`; `str_replace` requires a non-empty `old_str` and a non-null `new_str`, dispatches `fs/edit-intent`, reads the file, requires EXACTLY one literal occurrence (`FS_EDIT_NOT_FOUND` when absent, `FS_AMBIGUOUS_EDIT` carrying the offending line numbers when not unique) and writes `replaceIfVersion` at the observed version; `insert` validates `0 <= insert_line <= lines.length`. Paths must be ABSOLUTE, `view` renders `cat -n`-style numbered lines or a listing two levels deep that hides dotfiles, `node_modules` and `__pycache__`, and every result is clipped at `maxOutputChars` with the literal `<response clipped>` note. Its `MutationPolicy` mirrors the tool-fs escalation split and maps `FS_SANDBOX_DENIED` to the shared denial marker.
invariants: `old_str` must match a unique run of lines; a non-unique match is refused rather than guessed (packages/fs/tool-str-replace-editor/src/index.ts:27-30, 304-310).
A null placeholder for a parameter unused by the selected command is treated as omitted, but required parameters still need values (packages/fs/tool-str-replace-editor/src/index.ts:25, 283-285).
A long `view` result is truncated and explicitly marked with `<response clipped>` (packages/fs/tool-str-replace-editor/src/index.ts:24, 33-37).
tools.failurePolicy: fail-closed — a relative path, an existing `create` target, a missing or ambiguous match, a stale version and a sandbox denial each throw; only over-long output degrades (fail-soft) into a clipped result.
constants: `maxOutputChars` default 16_000 and must be a positive safe integer (packages/fs/tool-str-replace-editor/src/index.ts:514, 524-525)
directory listing depth limit `depth < 2`, excluding dot-prefixed names, `node_modules` and `__pycache__` (packages/fs/tool-str-replace-editor/src/index.ts:195-203)
`view_range` second element `-1` means to end of file (packages/fs/tool-str-replace-editor/src/index.ts:175-177)

tools.name: filesystem-and-shell-sandboxing
tools.what: Confinement is a per-call policy check in trusted code over model-controlled input, not a kernel boundary. `SandboxedFileSystem extends LocalFileSystem` fences ONLY `writeText`/`editText`: `checkedTarget` returns the target unfenced for `danger-full-access`, throws `FS_SANDBOX_DENIED` for `read-only`, and for `workspace-write` RE-canonicalizes the path, requires it under a root of `writableRoots(policy)` and returns the FRESH target so the checked identity is the mutated one. `SandboxBashExecutor`/`SandboxPwshExecutor` subclass their local executors, stamp `sandboxPolicy: request.sandboxPolicy ?? ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve()`, and wrap the exact local argv through `ctx.sandbox.confine(...)` for any non-full-access mode. On the tool side `FsSandboxController` advertises the `sandbox_permissions`/`justification` fields ONLY under a confining backend, so the schema validator rejects them otherwise, and it delegates the escalation approval sequence to the shared `dsh-sandbox` vocabulary so bash and fs escalate identically.
invariants: The fence narrows the symlink TOCTOU only by re-canonicalizing immediately before delegating, and containment is explicitly not a security boundary: kernel-grade isolation of untrusted CODE stays `ctx.shell`'s job (packages/fs/fs-sandbox/src/index.ts:10-18, 129-143).
The fence must return the EXACT target the mutation will use, so no check-here-write-there window opens (packages/fs/fs-sandbox/src/index.ts:111-114).
Escalation fields are advertised only under a confining backend, and a confining backend without `ctx.sandboxPolicy` throws at plugin load (packages/fs/tool-fs/src/sandbox.ts:45-49, 59-65).
tools.failurePolicy: mixed — a denial is reported as data in the sandbox shell path (`sandbox.denied`) while a taken escalation is fail-closed (approval must return a grant); a positively identified runner failure throws `SandboxUnavailableError` in the foreground and stamps `runnerFailed` on a background handle; `danger-full-access` runs unconfined by explicit opt-in.
constants: three handled modes 'danger-full-access', 'read-only', 'workspace-write', with both denials carrying `FS_SANDBOX_DENIED` (packages/fs/fs-sandbox/src/index.ts:122-143)

containment fallback compares `dev`+`ino` identity with `MISSING_CODES = {ENOENT, ENOTDIR}` and case-sensitivity default `process.platform !== 'win32'` (packages/fs/fs-sandbox/src/containment.ts:12, 42-44, 61)

tools.name: search-tools-and-native-command-resolution
tools.what: `glob` and `grep` run the packaged ripgrep binary as an ordinary foreground `ctx.subprocess.spawn` with a plain argv vector — never `ctx.shell`, never a background job — with `--no-config` prepended so a host `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` cannot inject a `--pre` preprocessor. `grep` uses a fixed line-oriented `rg --json` command (path/line/text parse without colon ambiguity), treats exit 1 as zero results, and fails with `SEARCH_RAW_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW` rather than parsing a partial stream; `glob` uses `rg --files --sort=modified` with two negated globs per VCS directory name and the search root behind `--` so a leading-dash path is never a flag. One retention pass bounds what survives inline, a separate pass bounds the serialized `presentationMeta`, and a `tools/post-execute` hook that fires only on an accepted, unmodified, direct top-level call saves the COMPLETE formatted result through `ctx.spillStore` and re-renders with the locator. `runNativeCommand` is the separate host-OS boundary: `execFile(command, args, { encoding: 'utf8', signal, windowsHide: true })` with no shell, carrying `code`/`stdout`/`stderr` on failure.
invariants: The search tools never use `ctx.shell` and never start a model-visible background task (packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/index.ts:7-11).

A truncated result means complete stdout could not be retained within the budget, so the tool fails clearly instead of parsing a silently partial stream (packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/search-core.ts:132-137).
Native implementations never invoke a shell (packages/util/native-command/src/runner.ts:8).
tools.failurePolicy: mixed — ripgrep acquisition is fail-closed (missing executable, raw-output overflow, invalid pattern and abort each throw a coded `SearchError`); retention and spill are fail-soft (a missing store or a rejected save only logs a warning and the footer states the remainder was not saved, so a successful search never becomes `isError`); `runNativeCommand` is fail-closed with no fallback path.
constants: `GREP_MAX_MATCHES` 250; `GREP_MAX_LINE_BYTES` 2000; non-UTF-8 matched lines become '(line is not valid UTF-8)' (packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/grep.ts:29, 35, 157)
search-meta drop loop keeps at least one group/path and always sets `truncated: true` when anything is dropped (packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/presentation.ts:111-116)

tools.name: workspace-resolution-and-file-apis
tools.what: `workspace/workspace` owns the durable workspace registry: `realpathNormalize` requires a fully qualified path before `realpath` and is the ONE uniqueness canon (string equality of canonicalized paths, so a symlink to an existing workspace's directory collides), `WorkspaceRegistry` writes through a versioned storage domain with a durable `pendingMutation` marker replayed before every serialized operation and rolled back on failure, and session membership requires BOTH an id in the record's account AND a session header whose canonical cwd equals the workspace path (filtered on read, never stored filtered). `api/workspace-files` exposes read-only Remote methods over `ctx.fs` with host-side page defaults (`maxBytes` 2 MiB, `maxFileBytes` 32 MiB, `maxLines` 5000, `maxEntries` 2000), a `workspaceFileScope` TypertLookup mapping a session id to its workspace root, lstat-before-resolve symlink rejection, and containment enforced only for `list`. `api/workspace-controller` owns the `workspace` Remote namespace and serializes every mutation on its own tail so title-ownership checks cannot interleave.
invariants: Workspace paths are stored canonicalized and uniqueness is string equality of canonicalized paths — a symlink to an existing workspace's directory collides (packages/workspace/workspace/src/paths.ts:41-44).

Membership requires both an id in the account and a session header whose canonical cwd equals the workspace path (packages/workspace/workspace/src/types.ts:26-29; packages/workspace/workspace/src/entity.ts:101-113).

Directory listings and change observations remain workspace-scoped while file reads follow the composed filesystem's read access, and this service exposes no mutations (packages/api/workspace-files/src/index.ts:6-11).
tools.failurePolicy: fail-closed — stored-state validation fails loud on a repeated id, an orphan record, a duplicate canonical path or a session accounted twice; a non-fully-qualified path is a `TypeError`; an out-of-workspace `list` is `workspace-file/outside-workspace` and a bad parameter is `gateway/bad-request`.
constants: storage domain name 'workspace' version 2, initial state `{ initialized: false, workspaceIds: [], archivedSessionIds: [] }`, `pendingMutation` a union of exactly 'create' | 'delete' (packages/workspace/workspace/src/spec.ts:38-41, 69-73)
`readAll` checks `info.size > limit` and then reads `limit + 1` bytes to detect overflow (packages/api/workspace-files/src/index.ts:281, 284)

tools.name: atomic-write-and-cross-process-locking
tools.what: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write` provides `writeFileAtomic(filename, content, { mode, dirMode? })`: create parents, write a random-suffix sibling `${filename}.<12 hex>.tmp` with flag `'wx'` and the caller's mode, then rename it over the target, so readers observe either the old or the new complete content and a replaced file ends up with exactly the stated mode; transient Windows `EACCES`/`EBUSY`/`EPERM` renames are retried with exponential backoff. `withFileLock(filename, operation, { waitMs? })` serializes cross-process writers through a `wx`-created `<filename>.lock` sibling holding the pid, backing off exponentially and failing on a deadline, while readers stay lock-free because the rename commit is atomic. A SECOND and different `writeFileAtomic` lives in `fs/fs-local/src/fsio.ts`: it fsyncs the staging file, preserves the Windows DACL and publishes `createIfAbsent` through a hard link.
invariants: The temp open refuses to follow a symlink planted at the temp path, the fresh inode carries `options.mode` through the rename (no chmod race), and the rename replaces a symlinked target itself instead of writing through to its referent (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:64-73).
A contender never removes an existing lock because file age cannot prove its owner stopped; orphan recovery is an operator action (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:147-151).
Crash durability (fsync) is explicitly out of scope for this package (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:73; TODO at :83-84).
tools.failurePolicy: fail-closed — any remaining rename failure removes the temp file and rethrows; lock contention outliving the deadline throws a timed-out error; a non-contention error propagates unchanged.
constants: `WINDOWS_TRANSIENT_RENAME_ERRORS` = {EACCES, EBUSY, EPERM}; retry 20 ms initial, doubling to a 200 ms cap, at most 8 retries (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:17-20)
`DEFAULT_LOCK_WAIT_MS` = 2_000; lock retry 20 ms initial with a 200 ms cap (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:114-115, 126)
lock file `<filename>.lock` with content `${process.pid}` newline, mode 0o600, flag 'wx' (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:162, 167)
random temp suffix `randomBytes(6).toString('hex')` = 12 hex chars; `mode` is REQUIRED in `WriteFileAtomicOptions` (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:53, 85)

tools.name: shell-tools-and-persistent-sessions
tools.what: `ctx.shell` is an abstract `ShellExecutor` seam (resolve, then run/start), implemented by `bash-local` and `pwsh-local`, which fill and clamp a request into a spec (`clampTimeout(request.timeoutMs, config.timeoutMs, config.maxTimeoutMs)` and `stdoutMaxBytes` from `config.maxOutputBytes`), open ONE fused deadline per foreground run (`deadline(spec.signal, spec.timeoutMs, 'BASH_TIMEOUT')`) and classify the outcome as `timedOut = timeoutOf(d.signal, code) !== undefined` versus `aborted = d.signal.aborted && !timedOut`, so a timeout and an abort racing before process close report the single first cause. Collect-mode readers cap in-memory output and spill overflow to a capped temp file; the renderers append a stable exit contract (`[timed out after Nms]`, `[killed by signal: X]`, `[exit code: N]`) that `parseExitStatus` inverts to drive the terminal card's exit pill. The persistent variants keep ONE PTY session per agent through `ctx.terminals`, wrap each command in nonce start/end markers and serialize commands per owner on a promise chain; they do NOT go through `ctx.shell`, so executor config (timeout, grace, sandbox mode) does not apply to them.
invariants: `run()` rejects only for infrastructure failures: nonzero exits, timeout kills and abort kills resolve with a `ShellRunResult` (packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts:51-53).
A still-running background process is stopped and awaited when its owning composition tears down, so a background process survives an executor-only reload (packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts:59-62).

Keep the persistent wrapper on ONE physical line: an interactive bash prints PS2 for embedded newlines before executing the buffer, which would leak terminal prompts and marker source text into the model-facing result (packages/shell/tool-bash-persistent/src/index.ts:81-83).
The exit marker must stay last because `parseExitStatus` anchors there (packages/shell/tool-bash/src/render.ts:44).
tools.failurePolicy: mixed — fail-soft at run time (a timeout, an abort or a nonzero exit is data on the result; a background handle's `done` never rejects and a provider rejection settles as `killed` with the detail on stderr) and fail-closed at resolve/load time (a non-positive or non-finite timeout, a `graceMs` above the timer cap, or a confining executor without `ctx.sandboxPolicy` throws).
constants: persistent bash/pwsh default `timeoutMs` 300_000 and `maxOutputChars` 16_000, with `SCROLLBACK_PAGE_LINES` 1_000 and `POLL_INTERVAL_MS` 25 (packages/shell/tool-bash-persistent/src/index.ts:24-25, 449-450; packages/shell/tool-pwsh-persistent/src/index.ts:486-487)
`clampTimeout` = `Math.min(requested ?? def, max)` and rejects a non-positive or non-finite hint (packages/util/timeout/src/index.ts:45-55)

tools.name: pty-terminal-sessions
tools.what: `terminal/terminal` is an in-process `TerminalSessionService` at `ctx.terminals` holding a backend registry, exact-Agent sessions, reserved names, pending spawns and owner cleanups with a memoized `disposeAll`. `terminal-bash` supplies the default backend: a headless terminal emulator plus a `BoundedTextBuffer` scrollback, a sanitizer driven by the prompt marker `133;D;` and the controlled prompt `dsh> `, and a settled-operation protocol with wait reasons (idle silence, handoff grace, timeout, exit). The real PTY is allocated by `subprocess-local`'s `spawnTerminal` through `node-pty` with `{name:'dumb', rows, cols, cwd, env}`, and `tool-terminal` registers the model-facing `terminal_open`/`terminal_send`/`terminal_read`/`terminal_signal`/`terminal_close`/`terminal_list` tools with a complete-result byte cap. Unix stdin-wait detection reads `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/syscall` (including fd-0 inspection for select/poll/epoll) to prove a foreground group is actually blocked reading the terminal; Windows hard-codes false and delivers Ctrl-C as a `\x03` write.
invariants: Whole-session quiescence is the seam contract: `spawnTerminal` owns terminal allocation, text transport, foreground groups, signalling and an awaited termination method (packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/index.ts:109-113).
Already-adopted members keep their own start identities, which every signal rechecks (packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/terminal.ts:200).

Local PTY allocation is synchronous but the provider contract permits remote asynchronous allocation; a first genuinely asynchronous step in a handle call must add the operation tracking a remote provider needs (packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/index.ts:229-230; packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/terminal.ts:51-55).
tools.failurePolicy: fail-closed for allocation and teardown (a missing program, an already-aborted signal or an `node-pty.spawn` throw rejects `spawnTerminal`; teardown throws when descendants or the shell survive the SIGTERM-grace-SIGKILL ladder; a write after exit throws); fail-open for stdin-wait detection, where every read failure returns false and readiness degrades to 'not waiting'.
constants: `terminal-bash` defaults: rows 40, cols 160, `scrollbackLines` 10_000, `scrollbackMaxBytes` 4 MiB, `maxReadBytes` 256 KiB, `pollIntervalMs` 50, `exactProbeAfterMs` 150, `idleSilenceMs` 3_000, `handoffGraceMs` 500, `timeoutMs` 30_000, `disposeGraceMs` 3_000, with `maxReadBytes <= scrollbackMaxBytes` enforced (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/config.ts:89-99, 116-117)

tools.name: subprocess-spawn-and-process-tree-control
tools.what: `SubprocessRuntime` is the abstract `ctx.subprocess` seam with `resolveExecutable`/`spawn`/`spawnTerminal`, and `subprocess-local` implements it: it scrubs credential-shaped and all `DSH_*` environment names from every child, validates argv/cwd/env for NUL bytes, resolves executables against the scrubbed PATH (reimplementing libuv's Windows search order) and owns each managed range through a selected containment mode. `selectContainmentMode` prefers a Linux user-systemd transient scope, then a Win32 Job Object for ordinary spawns, and otherwise degrades to a detached process-group/`taskkill` fallback with exactly one warning. Termination is one ladder: a one-shot `terminateWithReason` sends SIGTERM on the platform owner and arms `setTimeout(kill('SIGKILL'), graceMs)`, the spec's abort signal is wired through the same entry, and collection keeps the last `maxBytes` in memory while spilling the head to a capped temp file. `win32-process` supplies the koffi FFI layer: a kill-on-close Job created through `CreateJobObjectW`, with membership established by creating the process `CREATE_SUSPENDED`, assigning it to the Job and then resuming the thread.
invariants: The seam applies no defaults: every disposition, limit and directory is explicit, so the caller's own config decides them (packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/types.ts:69-74).
Credential-shaped names are NOT forwarded implicitly; a deliberately supplied entry survives because explicit env layers merge after the scrub (packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/index.ts:38-45).
The grace timer is deliberately NOT cleared on settlement: forced termination must still reach range survivors (packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/spawn.ts:611-612).
A Job member can never escape unowned: every failure after creation terminates the just-created process and closes the Job before throwing (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/process.ts:434-478).
tools.failurePolicy: mixed — spawn validation is fail-closed (an already-aborted signal, an empty `argv[0]`, an invalid grace or a NUL byte throws before launch, and a runner start/protocol failure is an infrastructure error); signalling delivery is fail-soft (failures are swallowed so teardown stays idempotent) and output overflow is fail-soft (the tail is retained, `lossy`/`truncated` is set, and the spill path is advertised when intact).
constants: `SENSITIVE_ENV_PATTERN` = /KEY|PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN/i and the scrub also drops every `DSH_*` name (packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/index.ts:45, 64-68)
spill: `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'dsh-subprocess-'))` at 0700 and a file created `'wx'` 0o600 with a 6-byte-hex suffix (packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/spawn.ts:97-99, 193-205)

Job limits: `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` 0x00002000 at flags offset 16 of a 144-byte `JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_SIZE`, `JobObjectExtendedLimitInformation` class 9, `ActiveProcesses` read at offset 40 of a 48-byte accounting buffer, `STARTUPINFOW` size 104 with `STARTF_USESTDHANDLES`, `CREATE_SUSPENDED` 0x4 plus `CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT` 0x400, `HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT` 0x1 (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/abi.ts:4-48; packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/process.ts:400-426)

tools.name: code-runtime-isolation
tools.what: `ctx.codeRuntime` is an abstract `CodeRuntime` seam (`language`, `isolation`, `run(request)`) owning the cross-backend portability vocabulary (`RESERVED_BINDING_GLOBALS`, `RESERVED_ERROR_MEMBERS`, `DUNDER_MEMBER`, `PORTABLE_RESERVED_WORDS`) and an error-as-field contract: program, budget, abort and substrate failures resolve inside `CodeRunResult`, while Service Definition misuse rejects. The shipped backend is `WorkerThreadCodeRuntime` (typescript, worker-thread): it type-strips the program with `stripTypeScriptTypes`, spawns a `Worker` with `env: {}`, `execArgv: []`, `stdout`/`stderr` enabled and `resourceLimits.maxOldGenerationSizeMb`, races the settle paths (done frame, output limit, ELU-poll compute budget, wall timer, abort listener, worker error/exit), re-validates and rebuilds every inbound port message field by field because the peer runs model code, and accounts combined logs plus value bytes with a hand-written JSON byte ledger that captures intrinsics so model-mutated prototypes cannot alter accounting. The private `experimental/code-runtime-python` backend runs CPython in its own process group with RLIMIT_CPU/RLIMIT_AS, an fd-3 JSON-lines protocol, SIGTERM-grace-SIGKILL escalation and a PID-reuse guard comparing `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22.
invariants: The peer runs model code, so every inbound message is re-validated and rebuilt and junk is dropped rather than thrown, because a throw in the host's `message` listener would crash the host (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:136-139, 509-512).
Executable logic stays in `bootstrap.ts` for in-process coverage, while `worker.ts` is the spawn-only entrypoint (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/worker.ts:2-3).

The Python backend is containment, not a security boundary: model code has bash-equivalent trust, contained by a tempdir-only environment, resource limits, a wall timeout and process-group kill escalation (packages/experimental/code-runtime-python/src/index.ts:4-6).
tools.failurePolicy: mixed — Service Definition misuse and invalid configuration fail closed (throwing at load or from `run()`), while everything a program or the substrate can cause (exception, invalid-output, output-limit, timeout, abort, worker-exit) resolves as `result.error`; hostile port traffic is dropped silently; crossing the output ledger converts the run into an explicit `output-limit` failure rather than a silently truncated success.
constants: `ELU_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` 25; `MIN_OUTPUT_BYTES` 4; the ledger starts at 2 bytes with +1 separator byte per extra log entry (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:63, 66, 170, 177)

`code-runtime-python` is `"private": true` and loaded by no shipped bundle, only by a snapshot profile (packages/experimental/code-runtime-python/package.json:41; snapshots/session/ptc-python-turn/cordis.yml:29-30)

tools.name: e2b-remote-execution-backends
tools.what: Three E2B packages implement the same seams against a remote sandbox instead of the host. `e2b/e2b` registers `ctx.e2b` as the single shared sandbox owner (`Sandbox.create({ apiKey, timeoutMs, secure: true, lifecycle: { onTimeout: 'kill' } })`, a fresh randomized HOME for control commands, `chmod 700` on `<cwd>/.dsh-e2b`, kill-and-rethrow on setup failure). `e2b/fs-e2b` implements `FileSystem` by running canonicalization inside the sandbox (`realpath -mz | base64`), sampling the first 8192 bytes for binary detection, and publishing writes through a private 0700 staging directory plus `rename` or a guarded `ln -T` create. `e2b/subprocess-e2b` implements `SubprocessRuntime` by resolving executables with `command -v` inside the sandbox, validating argv/cwd/env for NUL bytes, and polling remote status at a configurable cadence. In-tree, `e2b/e2b` and `e2b/fs-e2b` are referenced only by their own test-fixture composition and no shipped bundle mounts any of the three.
invariants: Each handle starts through the SHARED sandbox and retains command output/status paths in that remote world (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/index.ts:1-5).

The remote grace bound mirrors `subprocess-local`'s spawn-time check, because an unbounded grace would make the remote force-escalation deadline unreachable (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/index.ts:40-50).
A remote write must not be readable by other local users and must not be redirectable through a planted symlink (packages/e2b/fs-e2b/src/index.ts:30-32, 556-584).
tools.failurePolicy: fail-closed — `E2BRuntime.validate()` throws on an empty API key, a non-absolute Linux cwd or a non-positive `timeoutMs`; a setup failure kills the sandbox and rethrows; the fs provider throws coded `FsError`s and removes its staging directory on a failed write; `E2BSubprocessRuntime.spawn` throws before launch for a disposing service, an empty `argv[0]`, an unrepresentable grace or an already-aborted signal.
constants: `e2b`: cwd default '/home/user/workspace', `timeoutMs` default 300_000, control HOME `/.dsh-e2b-control-<uuid>`, runtime root `<cwd>/.dsh-e2b` chmod 700 (packages/e2b/e2b/src/index.ts:41, 80-81, 105, 175)
`fs-e2b`: `BINARY_SAMPLE_BYTES` 8192; staging directory `.dsh-<uuid>.tmp` at 0o700; new files 0o600 while existing files keep `mode & 0o777` (packages/e2b/fs-e2b/src/index.ts:31, 567, 574, 581-584)

subagent.name: named-provider-registry-and-capability-gate
subagent.what: SubagentRuntime (a TypertRemoteService registered on ctx.subagents) holds a Map<string, SubagentProvider> populated by registerProvider() through an effect-scoped Cordis effect that emits subagent/provider-added and, on unwind, subagent/provider-removed; expectProvider() fails loud with NO_PROVIDER and a duplicate name fails with DUPLICATE_PROVIDER. Each provider advertises SubagentCapabilities (agentOptions / outputSchema / depthLimit / toolFilter / persona) and SubagentRuntime.start() runs assertCapabilities() before dispatch, so a request needing a feature the provider lacks is rejected with UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY instead of being accepted-then-ignored. The two in-process backends advertise all five capabilities true, the ACP/Claude-Code/Codex backends advertise NO_START_CAPABILITIES (all false), and dsh-sdk advertises agentOptions only by spreading NO_START_CAPABILITIES and overriding it. tool-subagent re-checks the same flags at mount time via assertSubagentProviderConfiguration and refuses to register its tool against a provider that cannot enforce the configured maxDepth/agentOptions; prepareContinuable method presence (not a flag) is the continuable-child capability.
invariants: Provider registration is effect-scoped and HMR-safe; removing a provider blocks new starts but never revokes runs already returned to their holders.
Capability flags describe the ONE-SHOT start path only; continuable children are gated by prepareContinuable presence instead.
A request needing an unsupported start feature must be rejected before provider.start runs, never silently degraded.
constants: tool-subagent Config.maxDepth default 3; 0 forbids delegation; 'provider-managed' sends no cap (packages/subagent/tool-subagent/src/index.ts:129)

subagent.name: one-shot-run-lifecycle-and-settlement
subagent.what: SubagentRuntime.start() snapshots the durable descriptor, calls provider.start(resolved), appends the parent-owned catalog fact through establishCatalogChild(), and returns observeRun(...) — a SubagentRun whose result never rejects after publication and whose dispose() is idempotent. settleRun() maps the terminal SubagentResult.stopReason onto a JobOutcome (completed -> completed with joined text blocks, aborted without a diagnostic -> killed, everything else -> failed carrying the diagnostic) and always disposes the run before returning, prefixing the outcome detail when disposal also fails. The in-process driver builds that run in drivePublishedRun(): an abort listener maps the request signal onto child.cancel({kind:'parent'}), the prompt is submitted as one followup user message, whenIdle() is awaited, and readResult() folds the child's own event suffix after the activation boundary through foldConsumedWork + finalAssistantOutput. Out-of-process backends use settleRunResult() plus subprocessRunHandle() instead.
invariants: SubagentRun.result must never reject after publication — a model or transport failure resolves with stopReason 'error' so the tool layer maps it to an isError result.
A provider rejection before fulfillment means no run exists: no lifecycle event fires and the caller has nothing to dispose.
dispose() must be idempotent and must reach child quiescence.

subagent.name: delegation-depth-quota
subagent.what: Delegation depth is a durable recursion budget rather than a runtime counter. resolveChildDepth(parent, maxDepth) computes delegationDepthOf(parent) + 1, throws SubagentDepthError when that exceeds the request's maxDepth, and throws RangeError when it leaves the safe-integer range; delegationDepthOf(agent) returns Math.max(agent.session.header.delegationDepth ?? 0, agent.options.subagentDepth ?? 0) so the persisted session header is a monotone floor that a resumed child can only deepen, never reset to top level. childSessionMeta() persists delegationDepth into the child's durable header, and assertSubagentMaxDepth() validates the cap as a non-negative safe integer. tool-subagent owns the deployment value and rejects its own mount when the selected provider lacks the depthLimit capability.
invariants: The persisted header delegationDepth is authoritative and monotone — resumed options may deepen the count but never lower it.
A depth cap must be a non-negative safe integer, and 0 is a legal cap meaning delegation is forbidden.
A provider that cannot enforce the cap must never be mounted with a numeric maxDepth.
constants: maxDepth validity: z.natural().max(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) or the literal 'provider-managed' (packages/subagent/tool-subagent/src/index.ts:129)

subagent.name: durable-child-descriptor-and-cold-resume
subagent.what: Every session-backed child carries exactly one model-hidden subagent/descriptor session event (SUBAGENT_DESCRIPTOR_VERSION = 3) recording mode ('one-shot' | 'continuable'), the establishing provider name, the creation label, and — for continuable children — the resumable composition (agentProvider/agentModel/agentReasoningEffort/persona/toolFilter). snapshotSubagentDescriptor() validates and detaches the payload through snapshotJsonValue() before any child or Task exists; parseSubagentDescriptor() returns undefined for any version other than the current one and throws on unknown keys or a wrong-typed field; foldSubagentDescriptor() takes the FIRST descriptor in a log as authoritative. Cold resume (SubagentContinuationManager.coldResume) observes the persisted child session, authorizes lineage, folds the descriptor, and rebuilds agentOptions plus composition from it without dispatching any provider at all.
invariants: The first subagent/descriptor event in a child log is authoritative — a later same-type event can never rewrite the declared composition.
Supporting a new composition input requires a deliberate SUBAGENT_DESCRIPTOR_VERSION bump, never an implicit extra field.
Only a parsed current-version continuable descriptor makes a child cold-resumable; everything else is NOT_RESUMABLE.

subagent.name: durable-child-catalog-and-discovery-listing
subagent.what: Establishing a child appends a parent-owned subagent/catalog event (childId, childCreatedAt, mode, label) that the subagentCatalog projection folds through appendChunkedList, giving a durable per-parent discovery fact independent of the child's own log. Discovery itself never loads or resumes an Agent: listChildren()/listDescendants() build one live-preferred corpus from ctx.sessionQuery.listSessions() merged with ctx.sessions, filter on header.origin === 'subagent', and classify each candidate solely from the registered subagent projection (the identity fold over subagent/descriptor), resolving cold candidates down a ladder of projection-cache row (unseeded lifecycles only) then one shared observeSession(). listDescendants() walks the tree iteratively in stable pre-order annotating parentId and root-relative depth. Cancellation is rechecked around every await, and cold observations run under a bounded worker pool.
invariants: The registered subagent projection fold is the single classification authority — no caller may parse a descriptor itself.
A missing projection registry or session store is a deterministic configuration error, never an empty success.
A session id names a slot, not a lifecycle: a re-published session under the same id must not leak into an older parent's listing.

subagent.name: continuable-activation-residency-and-child-lock
subagent.what: ContinuableActivationRegistry owns the process-local Activation graph. startContinuable() reserves the durable child id up front (spec.childId ?? randomUUID()), snapshots the descriptor and delegated policy before the first await, and calls materialize(); materializeTracked() either creates a fresh child through ownerCtx.agents.create() (reserved sessionId, seed, inheritedEventCount, meta) or cold-resumes one through ownerCtx.agents.resume(), installs the descriptor and delegated policy in the child's creation window, and publishes the Activation (handle, SubagentInbox, ancestry WeakSet, ownedChildren, observer) into the resident map. Every durable operation on one child is linearized through ChildLock.run(childId, ...) — a promise-tail map whose tail absorbs rejections so one failed critical section cannot reject an unrelated later caller — and assertChildIdAvailable() rejects an id already owned by a live Agent or Session.
invariants: One durable Session has at most one process-local Activation at a time.
Delivery, release, and disposal for one child share a single serializer (the child lock).
The Agent inbox is the only turn queue — the manager owns durable orchestration, the Agent loop owns turn ordering.

subagent.name: activation-admission-cutoff-and-draining
subagent.what: Admission is closed by two independent facts: a manager-wide draining flag and a per-root closingScopes map keyed by the exact host-owned root Agent, carrying the live lineage members observed under it. assertAdmitting(agent) walks the agent's live lineage against scopeParent/lineage membership and throws DRAINING for any operation whose lineage reaches a closing root; entries persist until that exact Agent leaves the registry via agent/disposed, so a same-id replacement is not poisoned. drain() sets draining, awaits every already-admitted materialization through publication or rollback, computes the live ownership forest, and disposes the roots child-first; drainDescendants(parents) stops only the continuable descendants of exact live roots; drainChildren(parent, childIds) releases selected resident direct children under exact-parent authorization with a UNAUTHORIZED check. The registry registers its private scope's structural disposer BEFORE the drain so reverse Cordis unwinding runs the drain first.
invariants: Admission closes synchronously before any teardown work begins.
The scoped cutoff lasts exactly until the exact root Agent leaves the registry — never until a same-id replacement does.
Teardown of independent roots runs concurrently and reports one aggregate failure after all branches settle.

subagent.name: child-first-teardown-tree-and-ownership-gating
subagent.what: Each Activation's ownedChildren set records the child session ids it owns; holdOwnership() pre-registers a child under a continuation-managed parent so the parent cannot settle while a caller is still establishing it, acquireOwnership() commits the edge, and releaseOwnership() removes it and pokes the owner's settlement watcher. A non-empty ownedChildren set makes settlementState() return 'wait', so ownership is the gate on natural settlement. Teardown is child-first: finishDisposal() cancels with {kind:'parent'}, disposes every owned child Activation, awaits its own idle, flushes final state, captures terminal facts, disposes the handle, deletes the resident row, notifies the parent, releases ownership, and finally publishes the terminal edge; failures collected at each boundary become one ACTIVATION_TEARDOWN_FAILED. SubagentInbox.close() memoizes the release transaction so racing dispose calls share one completion.
invariants: A parent Activation must not settle while it owns a live child Activation.
The child's own session log — not the success of teardown — decides the epoch's terminal stop reason.
A delivery that loses the send-versus-dispose cutoff must retry under the same child lock rather than deliver into a closing inbox.

subagent.name: child-settlement-notification-and-lifecycle-edges
subagent.what: When an announced Activation finishes, notifySettlement() resolves the durable direct parent and delivers a subagent-settled notice built by createSettlementMessage(): a fixed one-line outcome in the parent's own task vocabulary plus the child's closing message, attributed with a distinct message source kind so a transcript never credits the child with words it did not write. During the parent's own teardown the notice is injected; otherwise it uses queue delivery when the parent is idle and steer when it is running. Independently, createLifecycleEmitter() publishes the subagent/start and subagent/end pair with per-listener exception containment (a throwing or rejecting listener is logged without starving peers), observeRun() attaches its terminal observer before dispatching start, and createActivationObserver() bounds each epoch by the child's log seq so a cold resume reports only the suffix it produced; epochStopReason() derives the reason from foldConsumedWork, treating a clean ending with dropped unrun work as aborted and a pre-step 'blocked' rejection as refusal.
invariants: subagent/start must precede subagent/end for one runId, and an end never fires for an epoch that never became resident.
An epoch's output and stop reason must come from its own log suffix, never the whole session.
A teardown failure overrides the epoch's own outcome and withholds its output — an answer the harness could not durably release is not a result.

subagent.name: subagent-control-and-messaging-surfaces
subagent.what: The model-facing coordination surface is tool-subagent-control's send_message, interrupt_agent and list_agents — thin adapters over ctx.subagents that perform no lifecycle routing of their own; send_message is symbol-marked (adjacentAgentSendMessageTool) so the continuation manager can append the withContinuableReturnGuidance block to a continuable child's first prompt, and interrupt_agent passes the caller as an exact-live-ancestor authority. SubagentRuntime.sendMessage() verifies the exact live sender, then routes to the sender's direct parent through a waking inbox delivery or to a direct continuable child (cold-resuming an inactive one); SubagentRuntime.interrupt() accepts either a durable human parent address or an exact live ancestor and checks the target's recorded lineage, self-interrupt and ACTIVATION_CLOSING before issuing cancel(..., {keepInbox: true}). The browser surface is three @Remote methods — list, prompt, interruptByParent — with a stable failure vocabulary (subagent/unauthorized, not-resumable, delivery-unavailable, projections-unavailable, invalid-time-zone) produced by rejectPrompt/rejectCatalogRead.
invariants: Adjacency is the authorization boundary: only a resident continuable child may message its direct parent, and only depth-1 children are send_message targets.
A parent-availability hint from a listing is never authoritative — the delivery path re-checks.
An interrupt stops only the current turn: unclaimed inbox work, the Activation and published descendants are preserved.

subagent.name: structured-output-capture
subagent.what: When a start request carries outputSchema, attachStructuredRuntime() registers a child-scoped structured_output tool whose parameters are the asserted JSON-Schema subset, a trailing scoped prompt instruction, and a monotonic tools.guard that refuses every later tool call once a value is captured. Capture is a two-phase commit keyed by the exact ToolExecution object identity: the tool body validates the arguments with validateJsonSchemaValue (ToolArgsError on violation) and stages the value in a WeakMap, and the authoritative tools/result notification commits it — a nested PTC capture additionally waits for the enclosing execution token's result. In the one-shot driver, readResult() reports result.structured only when a value was committed and downgrades an otherwise 'completed' run with no captured value to 'error'.
invariants: Only the tool call counts as the result — a plain text answer must never satisfy a requested schema.
Capture commits only after the authoritative tools/result succeeds, never at argument-parsing time.
Every registration is child-scoped, so concurrent structured children do not interact and disposal leaves no global residue.

subagent.name: delegated-policy-pinning-and-child-composition
subagent.what: At the delegation boundary captureDelegatedPolicyOverrides() synchronously reads the parent session's explicit sandbox-mode override through ctx.get('sandboxPolicy').overrideOf() and pins the approval policy to 'never' whenever the approval capability is composed, regardless of the parent's own policy; appendDelegatedPolicyOverrides() writes those onto the child's own log as sandbox/mode and approval/policy events with source 'delegation', so the child's effective policy is reconstructable from its log alone. applyChildComposition() joins the parent's preset into the child's scope, registers the fixed SUBAGENT_DELEGATION_CONTEXT runtime-context statement, then installs the per-child persona (shadowing deployment:persona-prefix) and the tools.restrict() filter. resolveChildAgentOptions() merges the parent's provider/model/reasoning-effort/maxTokens under the request overrides and clears a route-owned reasoning effort when the route changes without one.
invariants: Policy must be captured before the child start's first await — a later parent switch belongs to the parent's future, not to this child.
The approval policy for a delegated child is 'never' regardless of the parent's policy, so its asks are rejected deterministically.
The preset join and the per-child registrations must happen in one call: a child composed without the join sees an empty tool registry.

subagent.name: subagent-model-selection-policy
subagent.what: When modelSelectionSettings is enabled, tool-subagent exposes provider/model/reasoning_effort parameters and enforces a durable per-Session allow-list. subagentModelSelectionPolicy() reads the subagent/model-selection-policy event through its projection (which inherits from the parent session for a child session, so the decision follows the delegation tree), assertAllowedModelSelection() rejects any explicitly selected route outside that list, and preflightChildLlmRoute() resolves the effective route through the live LLM adapter before any child is created — re-checking that the provider did not change while the route was resolving. requestedAgentOptions() requires provider and model together, rejects empty values, and clears a configured route-owned reasoning effort when the route changes without an explicit effort. tool-subagent also exposes list_subagent_models so the model can inspect advertised routes and efforts.
invariants: Pure inheritance stays outside the policy — only an explicit model-facing route choice is policed.
provider and model form one route and must be supplied together; changing the route without an effort clears the old route-owned effort.
The policy is recorded once, before the definition can reach a model request.
constants: allowedModels must be a non-empty array of unique provider/model routes (packages/subagent/tool-subagent/src/model-selection-state.ts:31-34)

subagent.name: out-of-process-child-teardown-ladder
subagent.what: Out-of-process backends compose subprocessRunHandle() and settleRunResult() with their own wire drivers. dispose() is memoized: it removes the abort listener, settles local cancellation (there is no assumption the child cooperates), then runs a cooperative teardown ladder — stdin EOF gives the child a window to flush persistence and reap its own nested subprocesses, then the subprocess seam's terminate() escalation (SIGTERM, spec grace, SIGKILL on POSIX; direct force-terminate on Windows) with a whole-range exit proof. settleRunResult() guarantees the published result never rejects: a locally cancelled attempt settles as 'aborted', any other rejection is flattened to stopReason 'error' through a contained diagnostic sink, and provider diagnostics are limited to 4096 UTF-8 bytes with a visible truncation suffix that never splits a UTF-8 sequence. Configuration failures (non-positive graces, empty/relative/absent cwd) fail loud before the process boundary.
invariants: result must never reject after publication, and the abort listener must be removed on every settlement path.
dispose() is idempotent and must not assume child cooperation.
A child working directory must be absolute and enterable, or the start fails before spawning rather than binding the child to the server's launch directory.
constants: Every grace must be a positive finite number no greater than MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS = 2147483647 (packages/subagent/subagent-acp/src/index.ts:78-82)

subagent.name: background-job-registry-and-parent-wake
subagent.what: JobRegistry is the abstract ctx.jobs seam (its constructor throws when instantiated directly) and LocalJobRegistry implements it in memory: ids are registry-issued '<kind>-N' from per-kind monotone counters, access is fenced by exact owner session id in assertAccess(), start() refuses an owner no attached controller serves and refuses once the per-owner active cap is reached — checked before spec.run(), so a rejected start spawns nothing — and settle() is first-wins, releases every waiter, and announces completion LAST after every other observer has seen the committed record. tool-jobs attaches the required controller, enforces a producer-declared outputLimitBytes only at the job_output/job_kill boundary, and delivers each unreported completion to its owner: injected into a busy owner's next step, or opening a turn on an idle one under 'wakeup' delivery, bounded by a wake budget that only human input refills. Background one-shot subagents reach this registry through tool-subagent's jobs.start({kind:'subagent', ...}) call, whose done hook is settleStart/settleRun.
invariants: start() refuses work while no attached job controller serves the owner — a producer cannot start work its owner cannot collect or stop.
Settlement is first-wins with completion announced last, because a reporter may open a model turn synchronously.
A pending wait marks the job reported before listeners run, so a caller that collected the result inline is not also woken for it.
constants: tool-jobs waitTimeoutMs default 30000, maxWaitTimeoutMs default 600000, completionDelivery default 'wakeup', maxConsecutiveWakes default 3 (packages/jobs/tool-jobs/src/index.ts:48-51)

subagent.name: workflow-orchestration-engine-and-worker-containment
subagent.what: WorkflowEngine is the orchestration seam and WorkerThreadWorkflowEngine runs each model-written script in a fresh node:worker_threads Worker on a vm context with frozen agent/parallel/pipeline/phase/log/args globals and a scrubbed (empty, plus platform temp on win32) environment, bridging agent() calls to host subagents over a closed tagged JSON protocol. Caps are enforced worker-side, per run: a FIFO slot pool bounded by maxConcurrentAgents, a started >= maxTotalAgents check raising AGENT_CAP, and assertItemCap raising ITEM_CAP for oversized parallel()/pipeline() arrays; a run's per-request maxTotalAgents may only lower the engine ceiling. parallel() is a barrier mapping non-fatal throws to null, pipeline() runs each item through the stages with no cross-stage barrier, and fatality is an instanceof check against the host realm's WorkflowError so a script cannot forge it. tool-ralph drives a fixed deployment-owned script instead: one fresh structured child per round up to maxRounds, only a bounded handoff crossing rounds, round-failed on a null child, budget-limited at the limit, and a provider gate refusing a provider without outputSchema or one whose inheritsParentContext is true.
invariants: Every WorkflowErrorCode is fatal and rethrown by the combinators; per-item null is reserved for child failures and ordinary in-stage script errors.
A per-request maxTotalAgents may only lower the engine ceiling, never raise it.
The worker thread is containment, never a security boundary — realm materialization is the real JSON contract.
constants: maxTotalAgents default 1000, maxItemsPerCall default 4096, syncTimeoutMs default 5000, disposeGraceMs default 5000 (packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/src/index.ts:118-121)
tool-ralph maxRounds default 256 (deployment ceiling), maxHandoffChars 16384, maxResultChars 16384 (packages/workflow/tool-ralph/src/index.ts:35-37)

subagent.name: goal-round-budget-and-automatic-continuation
subagent.what: GoalService event-sources a same-session goal as whole-snapshot goal/change events on the owning session log, folded by the goal projection through the strict decodeGoalChange/applyGoalChange replay; roundsStarted is consumed only by an admitted user/message whose source.kind is 'goal' and whose round is exactly roundsStarted + 1 and <= maxGoalRounds, so human messages and stale reservations never consume a round. GoalActivation ('armed' | 'disarmed') is process-local, held in a WeakMap, and forced disarmed on every agent/session-start — which is what makes a resumed or forked session require a human resume. goal-round-driver reacts to agent/status idle, goal/changed and inbox insert/claim/discard with no timers of its own, coalescing onto one serialized drive loop that requires fiber ACTIVE, the exact live agent, status 'idle' and no competing queued prompt, then reserves at most one round per quiescent pass through agent.followup() with a goal-sourced message. Each reservation is fenced by a RoundAttempt (queued -> claimed -> admitted, with cancelled/stale flags) re-validated at agent/pre-step, and durability is checkpointed with ctx.sessions.flush before reserving. Deterministic faults block the goal with a stable code (round-limit, queue-failed, prompt-rejected); every other doubt disarms automatic authority.
invariants: Goal activation is never persisted — only the durable phase and roundsStarted are; session start therefore always disarms.
A round is consumed only by its own admitted goal-sourced message matching the exact id, revision and round number.
A pause must fence to the exact dropped attempt's revision, so a pause followed by an immediate resume cannot re-pause the resumed goal.
constants: A goal round is admitted only when source.round === roundsStarted + 1 and source.round <= maxGoalRounds; a corrupt checkpoint with roundsStarted > maxGoalRounds is rejected on restore (packages/goal/goal/src/fold.ts:321-331; packages/goal/goal/src/index.ts:98-100)

subagent.name: goal-human-authority-and-command-surface
subagent.what: tool-goal authenticates every call with goalToolExecution(), which requires the exact live agent, agent.status === 'running', ctx.agents.currentInitiator() === agent, and an open model turn exposed by the turnBoundary projection; requireDirectHuman() additionally demands that the agent be a runtime root and that a human user/message (source.kind 'user') appear inside the captured open-turn window. create, edit, pause and resume are therefore human-only, and the model is additionally refused resuming a durably paused goal with GOAL_TOOL_RESUME_PAUSED. complete and blocked instead use completionAuthority(), which accepts direct-human input or the exact admitted goal round, and a goal-round 'blocked' is rejected while roundsStarted is below blockedAfterConsecutiveRounds with GOAL_TOOL_BLOCK_THRESHOLD. command-goal supplies the human surface /goal [<objective>|clear|edit <objective>|pause|resume] over the same domain, mapping any GoalError to one generic soft message and rethrowing anything else.
invariants: edit, pause and resume require a direct top-level human turn — a subagent or non-human producer must not acquire that authority.
A model may not resume a durably paused goal; only a human resume re-arms it.
A blocked report must carry a concrete non-empty blocked_reason, stored durably as code 'model-reported'.
constants: blockedAfterConsecutiveRounds default 3 (packages/goal/tool-goal/src/index.ts:32, fallback ?? 3 at :126); no shipped composition overrides it

subagent.name: schedule-durable-timer-wakeups
subagent.what: ScheduleRuntime is a process-local, disposable projection of one root agent's durable schedule/change log: it folds the agent's own events, chooses the next action with dueDecision() (earliest due one-shot first, else one whole fixed-rate batch, else the next wake target), and arms a single setTimeout clamped to the Node timer ceiling, re-deriving the whole decision from the log on every wake — no cron expressions and no persisted timers. Dispatch runs inside agent.runMaintenance() so it cannot preempt other activity, and a busy idle phase makes the runtime waitForIdle() instead of forcing admission; the reminder is framed as untrusted content, appended as a user message via followup, recorded with a dispatch event, and flushed on both sides of the barrier. A corrupt log or a failed dispatch append latches faulted, permanently stopping that agent's runtime, and only root agents created after the plugin loads get a runtime at all.
invariants: No timer is persisted — the session event log is the only schedule state and every wake re-derives from it.
A firing must never preempt in-flight agent activity; it runs only inside the maintenance window.
Faulted is terminal for one agent's runtime: a corrupt log or failed dispatch append stops scheduling rather than retrying.

subagent.name: plan-mode-logged-state-machine
subagent.what: PlanModeController keeps plan mode as logged per-agent collaboration state: planProjectionDefinition folds command/run and command/done for /plan, plan/mode, and request/header into {active, pending}; a selection made during an open turn stays in the process-local pendingIntents WeakMap and is appended by the agent/pre-step hook only when a step is actually accepted, so the prompt guidance and the request tool catalog stay consistent. The plan:policy prompt section renders the deployment section only while plan mode is active or pending. exit_plan_mode stays registered while plan mode is inactive (keeping the request tool catalog stable), requires an active mode plus a plan whose first heading matches /^#\s+\S/ and a live userQuestions channel, asks an Approve / Keep planning review, and on approval records a silent pending exit applied at the next accepted pre-step.
invariants: The exit tool stays registered while plan mode is inactive so entering or leaving plan mode never changes the request tool catalog.
A pending selection must be appended before the next request assembly, and a failed durable append must leave the selection retryable rather than dropped.
A dismissed or aborted review must fail the call instead of leaving plan mode.

subagent.name: team-roster-identity-and-provisioning
subagent.what: TeamRoster derives Team membership from the exact live Agent object: tryMembership() returns undefined unless ctx.agents.get(agent.id) === agent, resolves the root through agent.session.header.parentSession, and grants a teammate identity only for a durable member row in phase 'active' or 'provisioning'; a direct child that carries its own subagent descriptor is deliberately refused a Team identity so provider-owned workers never receive nested Team membership, while a descriptor-less root becomes an implicit Lead. spawn() reserves an immutable named roster row inside a serialized Lead-log transaction (name uniqueness against all history, cap against state.members.length, whole-value team/member v2 event in phase 'provisioning'), mints a caller-reserved childId, establishes a continuable child through ctx.subagents.startContinuable(), proves the initial prompt is durably accepted via checkpointInitialPrompt()/messageAccepted(), and only then commits 'active'. Crash-left provisioning rows are reconciled by reconcileProvisioning() from the persisted child session, and only the Lead may spawn or interrupt.
invariants: A teammate's name, provider and context are immutable across events; a new member must begin in phase 'provisioning'.
Failed members keep their roster slot forever, so a name is never reused within a Team.
A provider-owned subagent child must not receive a Team identity — its descriptor disqualifies it.
constants: MEMBER_NAME = /^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/ with max 64 characters and the reserved name 'lead' (packages/experimental/agent-team/src/roster.ts:26,453)
teammate description and provider each limited to 200 characters (packages/experimental/agent-team/src/roster.ts:258,264)

subagent.name: team-durable-mailbox-and-shared-task-board
subagent.what: TeamMailbox is a durable queue with target-side acknowledgement: sendAdmitted() commits a team/message/queued snapshot inside the Lead transaction before any delivery attempt, registers the dispatch before releasing the transaction so concurrent senders enter the target-local queue in durable mailbox order, and delivery admission is serialized per target SessionId by a promise-tail map. Delivery goes through steerHostSubagentPrompt() (or root.steer for the Lead), with a persisted-log probe for an inactive target where uncertainty keeps the item queued; the acknowledgement is target-side — observing the target's own user/message carrying the matching team-message source flushes the target and then appends team/message/delivered. TeamTaskBoard is a compare-and-set board: every mutation supplies the expected revision (mismatch -> TEAM_TASK_STALE_REVISION) and each committed snapshot increments revision by exactly 1; eight actions are owner-or-Lead authorized with reassign reserved to the Lead; dependencies are validated by a whole-graph DFS in assertTaskGraphCandidate (self-block, duplicate, missing/deleted, cycle); and write scopes are normalized advisory prefixes that only produce overlap warnings.
invariants: A message is never delivered twice — the target Session's own log is the acknowledgement, not a coordinator-side flag.
Every task snapshot increments revision by exactly one, and the task dependency graph must stay acyclic with no missing or deleted blockers.
Write scopes are advisory only: overlap produces a warning and never a lock.

subagent.name: team-runtime-admission-cutoff-and-activity-wait
subagent.what: TeamRuntimeLifecycle owns one AbortController; close() aborts it with a typed TEAM_DISPOSED TeamError, and every admitted Team operation composes AbortSignal.any([request.signal, lifecycle.signal]) so service disposal cancels in-flight creation and dispatch. Disposal closes admission, wakes every waiter, settles the captured in-flight creations and dispatches with Promise.allSettled while retaining only failures that are not the runtime cancellation (detected through the Error cause chain), drains roster children through ctx.subagents.drainContinuableChildren(root, childIds) under withTimeout, and throws one AggregateError if anything failed. TeamActivity.wait registers a one-shot waiter keyed by TeamId with a single-winner finish that clears the timer, removes the abort listener and drops the waiter entry; waiters are released by the journal's post-flush commit hook, by an agent/status edge on a rostered member, by the timeout, or by abort — never by polling. tool-agent-team's wait_agent additionally short-circuits with a model-only noProgress result when no other member is running or provisioning, and reads the roster in the same synchronous span as waiter registration.
invariants: No Team operation may be admitted after the runtime cutoff, and a cancellation must never be reported as a failure.
Runtime disposal is bounded by disposalTimeoutMs and reports one aggregate failure.
wait observes only changes after the call starts and never wakes an inactive member.
constants: wait timeout bounds 10000 through 3600000 ms inclusive (packages/experimental/agent-team/src/activity.ts:23-25); tool default 30000 ms (packages/experimental/tool-agent-team/src/index.ts:240)

subagent.name: todo-list-write-and-fold
subagent.what: todo_write replaces the WHOLE list on every call: toTodoList() trims each content, rejects empty and duplicate content, counts in_progress items, and rejects more than one when the deployment's allowParallelInProgress is false; the tool then appends one todo/write session event, so the durable log is the only store and replay is last-write-wins. The todos projection registered on ctx.sessionProjections replaces state on todo/write, returns null on turn/start (clearing the standing plan when the next turn begins while turn/end keeps the finished checklist visible), and returns the same reference for every unrelated event. A non-agent caller is rejected outright because the list is per-agent-session state, and the tool's own description is composed from the deployment policy clause.
invariants: The entire list is replaced on every call — there are no partial updates or per-item edits.
Unknown item keys fail at the schema boundary so the logged snapshot equals what the model believes it wrote.
The list belongs to one owning agent session; a caller without one is rejected rather than silently no-op'd.
constants: Statuses are exactly pending | in_progress | completed (packages/todo/tool-todo/src/index.ts:26)
allowParallelInProgress is required with no default (packages/todo/tool-todo/src/index.ts:41-43)

subagent.name: scoped-store-and-event-routing
subagent.what: core/scope mints an opaque ScopeKey per composition: createScope() tags a Cordis context with the kScope symbol so registrations made through it are owned by that scope, and bindScopeParent() records single-bind parent links with a cycle check, returning a ScopeParentBinding.rebind handle to the original binder alone. scopeTarget(base, key) builds a routing-only carrier whose Context.filter preserves the base service's own filter and then admits a tagged listener iff its tag equals the dispatch key or any ANCESTOR of it, so events flow up the chain and never down; the carrier holds routing state only while the real subject travels in the event arguments. ScopedLayers keeps one eagerly built global layer plus lazily created exact-scope layers — peek() is deliberately chain-blind, chainLayers() walks the chain farthest-ancestor-first so merge() lets the nearest scope shadow a name, and effect() derives both visibility and effect ownership from scopeOf(ctx) while reclaiming a layer only when the whole aggregate becomes empty. Many dsh registries (tools, jobs, system prompt) are built on these two primitives.
invariants: A scope key is single-bind: re-linking requires the handle returned by the original bind, and a link that would close a cycle is rejected.
A listener tagged BELOW the dispatch key must stay excluded — scope events flow up the chain, never down.
Reads must never create a scoped layer; a layer is reclaimed only when every table in it is empty.

subagent.name: turn-outline-fold
subagent.what: The turnOutline projection unit is a pure incremental fold of a session log into the whole-log turn outline a client rail renders outside its paged event window. turn/start appends {turn, seq, prompt:'', response:''} guarded to strictly increasing turn numbers, the first user/message with source.kind 'user' fills the prompt preview (later steering messages keep the first), every assistant/message replaces a draft, and turn/end commits the draft into that entry's response. preview() space-joins text blocks, collapses whitespace, clips at the limit with a trailing ellipsis, and bounds each block read to limit*2 characters so a multi-megabyte block is never concatenated whole. Uninteresting events return the same state reference and draft-only applies keep the turns array identity, which is the gate that keeps the projection change feed quiet; the wire view projects only state.turns.
invariants: turn/start — not the prompt user/message — anchors each entry, because its seq is the load-through target for a jump.
Unrelated events and draft-only applies must preserve reference identity so the change feed stays quiet.
Entries must be strictly increasing by turn number.

safety.name: sandbox-mode-vocabulary-and-per-call-policy
safety.what: The confinement vocabulary is a closed three-value union SandboxMode = 'read-only' | 'workspace-write' | 'danger-full-access' (packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/index.ts:29) carried per capability call as SandboxExecutionPolicy { mode, workspaceRoot, sessionId? }, never fixed on the provider. SandboxPolicyService (ctx.sandboxPolicy) resolves one policy per call at packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy/src/index.ts:163-170 with the precedence approved explicit mode > the session's last 'sandbox/mode' override (overrideOf, line 177) > the deployment default ('read-only' is the schema default, line 112), and the workspace root is the canonical session cwd or the configured fallback. The provider treats the policy as fully specified (SandboxProvider.confine is abstract) and refuses to run unconfined: SandboxUnavailableError carries code SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE (index.ts:124-144).
invariants: Mode is resolved per call from the calling session; two consumers may confine under different policies at the same instant (index.ts:61-68).
Precedence is fixed: approved escalation grant > session sandbox/mode event > deployment default.
The abstract seam forbids silent unconfined passthrough: confine must return enforcing argv or fail closed (index.ts:152-157).
constants: default deployment mode: 'read-only' (Config schema default, sandbox-policy/src/index.ts:112)

safety.name: platform-runner-chain-selection-and-probing
safety.what: LocalSandboxProvider selects the platform's runner chain first and probes second: PLATFORM_CHAINS is linux ['bwrap','landlock'], darwin ['seatbelt'], win32 ['windows-acl'] (packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/index.ts:159-166). A sole candidate is selected with no probe and a static enforcement claim (STATIC_ENFORCEMENT: bwrap/landlock/seatbelt 'full', 'windows-acl' 'partial' because WRITE_RESTRICTED must retain Everyone and NTFS hard links alias one file object, lines 177-187); a multi-candidate chain is arbitrated once, in order, by functional probes that actually apply the read-only profile and run 'true' (defaultProbeBwrap:68-74, defaultProbeSeatbelt:85-91, landlock probe report full-vs-partial:519-539). No chain or no passing candidate yields 'unavailable', and selectRunner throws SandboxUnavailableError before anything spawns (492-510).
invariants: Selection is by platform first; probing only arbitrates among competing candidates, it never re-validates a choice that has no alternative.
The chain verdict is cached for the provider lifetime (selectedRunner, line 265/493), so probes run at most once.
An operator-supplied runnerCommand is an assertion of full enforcement and skips built-in selection and probing (317-324).
constants: probeTimeoutMs default 5_000, validated as a positive finite number because spawnSync({timeout:0}) means unbounded (index.ts:255, 194-198)
Landlock launcher failure exit code comes from LAUNCHER_FAILURE_EXIT and is documented as versioned exit-125 (index.ts:233-237)

safety.name: per-runner-profile-synthesis-and-writable-roots
safety.what: Each rung expresses one policy in its own dialect: bwrapProfileArgs emits '--ro-bind / /', '--dev /dev', '--unshare-pid', '--proc /proc', '--die-with-parent' and, under workspace-write, '--tmpfs /tmp' plus a read-write bind of the workspace root (packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/profiles.ts:16-23); landlockProfileArgs builds readOnly ['/'] with readWrite ['/dev/null'] extended by '/tmp' and the workspace root (30-36); seatbeltProfileArgs emits an SBPL profile '(allow default) (deny file-write*)' plus literal /dev/null and subpath allows for the shared writable roots (51-58). The workspace-write allow-list itself has one home: writableRoots() in packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/roots.ts:52-55 returns the canonical, deduplicated set [workspaceRoot, '/tmp', os.tmpdir()] and [] under read-only, so the Seatbelt grant and the in-process fs fence cannot drift apart. canonicalPath uses realpathSync.native and returns the as-spelled path when resolution fails, matching nothing until the root exists (30-41).
invariants: read-only yields an empty writable-root list; nothing but required sinks such as /dev/null is writable.
Roots are canonical before comparison, because Seatbelt filters and the fs fence both match resolved paths (/tmp IS /private/tmp on darwin).
bwrap and Landlock keep their own grant spellings (ephemeral /tmp mount, launcher flags); only Seatbelt and the fs fence share writableRoots().

safety.name: windows-acl-write-restricted-token
safety.what: The win32 backend mints a WRITE_RESTRICTED token via CreateRestrictedToken with flags DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE | LUA_TOKEN | WRITE_RESTRICTED and a mode-selected restricting-SID list: read-only = [logon SID, Everyone]; workspace-write = [logon SID, Everyone, workspace write SID, optional private-temp write SID] (packages/sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/src/token.ts:196-222). It is a write-only boundary by construction: the module documents that reads, network and process visibility are NOT restricted (WRITE_RESTRICTED intersects only write accesses), console isolation is unavailable, and only ACL-addressable writes are governed (index.ts:23-39). Every Win32 call is checked and any failure throws with the API name and code, so a child is never spawned unrestricted; setTokenDefaultDaclGrant merges one full-access ACE for a restricting SID into the token default DACL so newly created objects (anonymous stdio pipes) pass the pass-2 check while creation stays gated by the parent container (token.ts:112-145, called at index.ts:294).
