invariants: The restricting list is mode-selected: read-only carries no capability SID, so a standing workspace grant ACE from an earlier workspace-write period stays inert (token.ts:166-186).
Everyone remains in both lists for process initialization; that ambient surface is the documented partial-enforcement boundary, so the rung must never advertise 'full'.
Any Win32 failure throws before spawn; silent unrestricted execution is forbidden (index.ts:338-347).
constants: restricting list: 2 SIDs under read-only, 3-4 under workspace-write (token.ts:204-208)
default-DACL ACE rights: GRANT_ACCESS with FILE_ALL_ACCESS (token.ts:126-131)

safety.name: windows-acl-capability-sid-grant-lifecycle
safety.what: Write capability is an identity, not a path list: workspaceWriteSid derives a deterministic S-1-4-x-y SID from sha256 of the canonical workspace path (packages/sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/src/workspace-sid.ts:35-40) so the workspace-root ACE materializes once per workspace per machine and later provisions hit the exact-ACE skip; tempWriteSid domain-separates a private temp directory's identity with a third subauthority '-1' (49-53), so sibling sessions sharing a workspace cannot enter one another's temp trees. AclWriteGrant records standing paths (never revoked, the cross-session reuse cache) separately from revocable paths (revoked on dispose) (grant.ts:74-77, 85-103); LocalSandboxProvider holds one standing workspace grant per workspace and one revocable private-temp capability per live session/workspace pair keyed by JSON.stringify([sessionId, workspaceRoot]) (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:273-274, 392-443), creating the temp dir with mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),'dsh-')) and revoking temp ACEs plus removing temp dirs at provider dispose while reporting rather than throwing cleanup failures (454-477).
invariants: Workspace and temp write SIDs must be distinct, and the private temp directory must be disjoint from every writable directory (index.ts:208-210, path-boundary.ts:34-39); the temp root must also be outside the workspace (path-boundary.ts:22-26).
A fresh provider always chooses a new random temp path, so crash residue cannot collide with or authorize a resumed session (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:379-391, 445-453).
The ambient temp root is never granted implicitly (index.ts:64-67).
constants: private temp directory prefix: 'dsh-' under os.tmpdir() (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:415)

safety.name: escalation-ladder-and-approval-choreography
safety.what: One strictly-wider table, WIDER_MODES, defines what a call may escalate to: read-only -> [workspace-write, danger-full-access], workspace-write -> [danger-full-access] (packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/escalation.ts:28-31); ESCALATION_TARGETS is the closed schema-facing vocabulary (41). validateEscalationArgs enforces that sandbox_permissions and justification travel together and the justification is a non-empty sentence (51-61). approveEscalation runs the ordered fail-closed sequence before anything executes: strict widening against the call's EFFECTIVE mode, approver composed, agent present to route the ask, then approver.request({...}) whose four outcomes map to the granted mode or four distinct verbatim throws (157-188). The model-facing texts are shared too: sandboxDenialMarker(mode) and escalationHintMarker(subject) (71-86). Production callers are the enforcing tool families: FsSandboxController.resolvePolicy builds the escalation request from ctx.approval and the exec agent/callId/signal and re-stamps the wider mode onto exactly one call (packages/fs/tool-fs/src/sandbox.ts:87-108), and its mapError wraps a FS_SANDBOX_DENIED into the marker plus same-turn hint (124-130).
invariants: Strict widening is checked at EXECUTION against the per-call effective mode, never baked into a tool schema (the schema enum is the registry-global closed target vocabulary).
A non-widening request never prompts a human; it throws before the approval channel is consulted.
A grant is one-shot: the returned mode is stamped onto the one call that asked.

safety.name: shell-confinement-wrap-and-denial-classification
safety.what: SandboxBashExecutor extends LocalBashExecutor and wraps the exact argv through ctx.sandbox.confine(['bash','-c',command], policy) for any confined mode, running unfenced only under danger-full-access (packages/shell/bash-sandbox/src/index.ts:89-115, 179-181); the pwsh twin mirrors it call-for-call over ['pwsh', ...] (packages/shell/pwsh-sandbox/src/index.ts:52-57). Each process's wrap facts (mode, enforcement, denialSignatures, runnerFailureRules, runnerProgram, workdir) are retained per ShellProcess so overlapping calls cannot be classified against another wrap (index.ts:53-66, 136-144). Classification distinguishes the two failure meanings: a runner failure means the command never ran and outranks denial — foreground calls throw SandboxUnavailableError and background processes carry runnerFailed (108-114, 151-166) — while a denial (nonzero exit plus the backend's own stderr dialect) sets sandbox.denied. isRunnerSpawnFailure attributes ENOENT/EACCES to the runner only when error.path equals argv[0] (or is absent and the syscall names it) and the caller-owned workdir is independently usable (helpers.ts:39-53), and classifyRunnerFailure requires a nonzero exit, the rule's optional exit-code gate, and a fatal signature on a line that is not an informational exclusion (81-103).
invariants: runner failure (command did not run) outranks denial (confinement worked and blocked) because they call for different retries.
Only the selected backend's own denial dialect is matched, never a cross-backend union, so a denial is never claimed that a backend cannot produce.
Confinement facts are per process, never a shared latest-wrap value.
constants: runner-failure rules per rung: bwrap 'bwrap: '; landlock exit-gated on LAUNCHER_FAILURE_EXIT with informational line 'partial enforcement (older Landlock ABI)'; seatbelt 'sandbox-exec: '; windows-acl exit-gated 127 on 'windows-acl-run: ' (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:231-240)

denial signatures: bwrap ['read-only file system'], landlock ['permission denied'], seatbelt ['operation not permitted'], windows-acl ['access is denied','access to the path','permission denied'] (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:205-213)

safety.name: fs-mutation-containment-fence
safety.what: SandboxedFileSystem extends LocalFileSystem but adds a per-call policy fence on the two mutations only — writeText and editText both route through checkedTarget, while reads pass through untouched because every mode permits reading (packages/fs/fs-sandbox/src/index.ts:1-27, 80-109). read-only denies with FsError code FS_SANDBOX_DENIED; workspace-write re-canonicalizes NOW (resolve realpaths the deepest existing ancestor), requires containment under a root from writableRoots(policy) via isPathUnder, and delegates the mutation with THAT fresh target so the checked identity is the mutated one; danger-full-access delegates unfenced (122-144). The module states plainly that this is containment in trusted code over a model-controlled path, not a kernel boundary, and that the residual TOCTOU (an ancestor symlink swapped between re-check and syscall) is narrowed and accepted for this threat model; kernel-grade isolation of untrusted code stays ctx.shell's job. isPathUnder tries a lexical fast path and, when spellings differ, walks existing ancestors comparing dev+ino identity so Windows 8.3 aliases and casing are recognized without weakening containment to a textual approximation (containment.ts:58-75).
invariants: Only the two mutations are fenced; read paths are never gated.
The policy check and the mutation use the same freshly canonicalized target (no check-here-write-there).
A denial is a structured FsError with code FS_SANDBOX_DENIED, which the tool layer maps to the shared model-facing marker.
constants: missing-path stat codes tolerated by containment: ENOENT, ENOTDIR (containment.ts:12)

safety.name: approval-service-policy-and-audit-pair
safety.what: ApprovalService (ctx.approval) applies a session policy BEFORE any answerer sees the ask: ApprovalPolicy 'ask' delegates to the composed waterfall, 'never' resolves every ask deterministically to 'rejected' inside the service — deliberately not as a listener, because a listener registered ahead of a gate could not keep that promise (packages/interaction/user-approval/src/index.ts:50-63, 252-266). request() requires an open turn and appends the audit pair approval/asked then approval/decided so both are enclosed by the durable log's commit boundary; an idle ask throws before appending anything (207-226). decide() races the scoped 'approval/request' waterfall against the caller's signal: an aborted signal yields 'cancelled' and discards a late answer, a missing or throwing answerer yields 'unavailable', and a rogue non-vocabulary return is normalized to 'unavailable' (258-298). The model learns the policy through a system-prompt context section plus a queued change notice from setPolicy (154-166, 176-187).
invariants: 'allowed-once' is the only grant; every other path fails closed.
The asked/decided pair must be turn-enclosed; a bare event between turns is crash-tail garbage and is refused.
The 'never' policy is decided before dispatch so registration order cannot defeat it.

safety.name: permission-preset-bundling-and-knob-write-path
safety.what: PermissionPresetService presents user-facing presets over two independent knobs (sandbox mode and approval policy) without merging them: the built-in table defaults to {'workspace-write': workspace-write + ask, 'danger-full-access': danger-full-access + never} (packages/interaction/permission-presets/src/index.ts:164-181). A switch records one 'permission/preset' event then writes only the changed knobs through their canonical setters setSandboxMode/setApprovalPolicy (379-396), and the derived state 'custom' is display-only and can never name a table entry or be a switch target (73, 192-194). The service refuses to compose over an unconfined executor by checking ctx.shell.sandboxMode, and it pins missing permission facts for every session at creation so a fresh session has a durable preset, sandbox mode and approval policy (195-197, 404-429). The read side is the 'permissions' session projection (stateVersion 2) carrying the whole select value; the write side is the /permission command, and a settings section named 'permission' holds the default preset for future sessions (211-223, 237-244, 255-275).
invariants: Execution, prompt narration and replay keep reading the knob folds; the preset event only preserves user intent when two presets share a bundle.
The name 'custom' is reserved and cannot be configured as a preset.
Composing presets over an executor that does not confine is a load-time misconfiguration, not a runtime fallback.

safety.name: session-sandbox-mode-override-log
safety.what: A session's sandbox-mode override is stored in its own log: setSandboxMode appends exactly one 'sandbox/mode' event and nothing mutates mode state out of band (packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy/src/session-mode.ts:44-55). The event is log-only — durable and replayable, never in the model transcript — and source:'delegation' marks an override seeded into a child (24-39). SandboxPolicyService registers the fold as the 'sandboxMode' session projection (stateVersion 1) whose apply returns event.data.mode, so effective mode = projection state ?? deployment default and an override survives restart by replay with no external config store (sandbox-policy/src/index.ts:132-138, 177-179). The same resolved policy is contributed to the cache-safe runtime-context snapshot so replay reconstructs the mode the enforcing consumers resolved (index.ts:140-151, renderPolicyContext 41-55), and a package-owned invariant companion rejects any logged sandbox/mode carrying an unknown mode (invariant.ts:18-20).
invariants: The switch IS its event: the log is the only store, no external config, and two sessions can never see each other's state.
Last event wins; the fold never applies the deployment default itself.
Every logged mode must be a member of SANDBOX_MODES.

safety.name: hooks-as-permission-gates
safety.what: Hooks intercept tool and prompt boundaries and fold into one most-restrictive decision: mergeHookOutputs ranks deny/block 3, ask 2, approve/allow 1 and resolves deny > ask > allow, keeps the first continue:false sticky, joins only the winning rank's reasons, and accumulates additionalContext/systemMessage in hook order (packages/hooks/hook-protocol/src/merge.ts:34-99). Matching is dialect-aware — Claude word/pipe patterns are literal alternatives and everything else is an unanchored regex, Codex treats every non-empty pattern as an unanchored regex, and an invalid regex is a non-match at runtime while config parsers reject it with a diagnostic (matcher.ts:37-64). runHook executes through ctx.shell with the hook's timeoutSec (wire unit: seconds) overriding the bridge's defaultTimeoutMs, which defaults to DEFAULT_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS = 600_000; an infrastructure rejection becomes an outcome with no exit code, so a hook that cannot run never crashes the calling turn (runner.ts:20, 67-105). The Claude Code bridge maps PreToolUse -> {kind:'deny'|'ask'} on tools/pre-execute, PostToolUse -> block, UserPromptSubmit -> reject, and a blocking Stop hook steers another step; updatedInput and systemMessage are logged and ignored, and merged.stop has no run-level halt yet (TODO) (hooks-claude-code/src/index.ts:174-179, 188, 222-276). The Codex bridge honors deny only, for PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit and Stop (hooks-codex/src/index.ts:223-230).
invariants: Permission precedence is deny > ask > allow and never depends on hook registration order.
A hook infrastructure failure is a non-blocking outcome (no exit code), while a hook that DOES answer deny/ask is honored as a gate.
Hook runs inherit the agent's session workspace as cwd and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, and a hookSpecificOutput block naming a different event is discarded.

safety.name: client-approval-and-permission-surfaces
safety.what: The browser half answers the host approval waterfall and drives permission switches, both over the Remote plane rather than a slash-command surface. ui-approval subscribes with ctx.remote.$on('approval/request'), wraps the request in a PendingApproval with a one-shot render key, registers it as a pending interaction and renders it as a conversation.composer takeover whose only outcomes are 'allowed-once' and 'rejected' (packages/client/ui-approval/src/client/index.ts:35-68, 90-92; ApprovalPanel.tsx:26-29); an unanswered request delegates to the next waterfall listener, and a signal abort settles it so a late answer is discarded (contract/slots.ts:122-159). ui-permission-presets decorates the host /permission command as a popupSelect reading the session's 'permissions' projection, marks the current value, filters the derived 'custom' state out of the pick targets, and attaches an explicit confirmation gate to the FULL_ACCESS_PRESET 'danger-full-access' row; a pick submits '/permission <preset>' so the host command remains the single write path (ui-permission-presets/src/client/index.ts:59-79, 145-166; presentation.ts:4). Its General-settings row separately writes the default preset for sessions created later through the host Settings API (index.ts:125-143).
invariants: Only one-shot decisions cross the client boundary: the UI cannot express 'always allow'.
The picker exists exactly while the host projection does; otherwise the bare invocation falls through to the host command.
The Full access preset always carries an explicit risk confirmation before the switch is submitted.

safety.name: human-question-tool-seam
safety.what: The ask_user_question tool is a model-facing Consumer of ctx.userQuestions: it registers a tool whose required input is an array of {id, question, header?, options?, multi_select?} and whose output is {answers:[{id, selected[], custom?}]}, mapping the wire naming (multi_select -> multiSelect) in execute (packages/interaction/tool-ask-user/src/index.ts:19-100). It passes the calling agent and the tool-execution signal into ctx.userQuestions.ask and feeds the human answer back as an ordinary tool result, so the loop pauses while a UI provider answers (80-99). The underlying seam is fail-closed: an aborted signal throws UserQuestionError ASK_ABORTED, an empty question list is refused, and a supplied agent that is not the registry's exact live runtime root throws CALLER_NOT_LIVE / DELEGATED_CALLER so an owned child with no human answerer cannot block forever (packages/interaction/user-questions/src/index.ts:41-47, 70-90).
invariants: The tool never fabricates an answer: the result is the provider's answer or a structured error.
Human interaction is valid only for the exact live runtime root, not for durable session lineage.

safety.name: advisory-repeat-tool-guard
safety.what: repeat-tool-reminder is an advisory per-agent repeat-call detector, not a gate: it observes on tools/post-execute, counts consecutive identical calls per agent in a WeakMap keyed by JSON.stringify([toolName, canonicalizedArguments]) where canonicalization deep-sorts JSON keys, and at each configured threshold injects a user-role reminder sourced as a plugin notice (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:189-207). It always delegates with next() and folds its reminder onto whatever the downstream decision was — a blocked call still gets the nudge — so it never vetoes or rewrites a call (209-224), and an agent/pre-step carrying a user message deletes the chain because repetition across an interjection is not a loop (226-232). Config is fail-loud at load: thresholds must be non-empty, integers >= 2, duplicate-free (normalized ascending, with thresholds[0] the gentle tier), and argumentsPreviewChars must be an integer >= 1 (128-141, 169-171). Only the model-visible preview is truncated; the chain key always compares the full canonical string (118-121).
invariants: Observe-and-enrich, never veto: counting happens first (state advances regardless of the downstream outcome), then the guard delegates and only prepends context.
Untracked calls (include/exclude wildcards) are transparent: they neither count nor reset.
A denied call still counts, because ToolRuntime routes denials through the same post-execute pipeline.

safety.name: preset-scope-isolation-gate
safety.what: mountPreset is the gate that keeps a per-agent preset composition from changing process-global behaviour: it refuses to mount into an unscoped context because 'its registrations would apply to every agent in the process' (packages/preset/agent-presets/src/mount.ts:378-385), then, after await() settles, it fails the mount if any row did not activate (403-406) and rejects any row that published a process-global service, telling the author to put it behind an `isolate` realm or move it to the host composition (407-413). The subtree is owned by the agent's fiber so it unwinds with the agent and a rejection leaves nothing mounted (369-376, 415-424). This is the constraint that stops a preset row from re-registering host-global capabilities such as the sandbox provider, filesystem or approval service for the whole process.
invariants: A preset mounts only into a scoped agent context; an unscoped mount is refused before anything is created.
A row that publishes a process-global service fails the whole mount instead of leaking into the host realm.
A rejected mount disposes its subtree, so failure is not partially applied.

model.name: llm-adapter-registry-and-route-resolution
model.what: LlmRuntime (ctx.llm) is an adapter registry keyed by provider route: registerAdapter(providers, adapter) is all-or-nothing (empty set, duplicate route or bad providerInfo throws INVALID_ADAPTER/DUPLICATE_ADAPTER) and publishes llm/adapters-updated with each listener contained so one broken observer cannot veto the commit, while INVARIANT-coded failures still surface (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:345-371, 387-445). Routes can be atomically replaced in one synchronous section through the returned handle, so no request observes a gap between release and re-registration, and a disposed handle throws REGISTRATION_DISPOSED (454-462, 407-415). Dormant routes an adapter could activate through configuration live in a separate directory (registerConfigurableProviders, INVALID_DIRECTORY/DUPLICATE_DIRECTORY, listConfigurableProviders @Remote) so configuration surfaces can show live and dormant providers together (481-543). Dispatch resolves strictly through registration(), which throws NO_ADAPTER for an unregistered route (964-968).
invariants: One route maps to exactly one adapter registration; a candidate route set is validated in full before anything is mutated.
Registry notifications are non-vetoing but never silently swallowed; INVARIANT failures rethrow after every listener ran.
An unregistered provider is a hard NO_ADAPTER failure, never a silent fallback.
constants: error codes on this seam: INVALID_ADAPTER, DUPLICATE_ADAPTER, REGISTRATION_DISPOSED, INVALID_DIRECTORY, DUPLICATE_DIRECTORY, NO_ADAPTER (index.ts:395-429, 496-529, 966)

model.name: model-catalogue-and-exact-model-metadata
model.what: Model knowledge has two clearly separated levels. The advisory catalogue (LlmAdapter.listModels) is validated and deduplicated by LlmRuntime (INVALID_CATALOG) but explicitly never controls routing or rejects a request (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:232-241, 691-718). Exact metadata for one route comes from resolveModel/prepareCall and is normalized by normalizeModelInfo: identity must match provider and model, context.contextWindow must be a positive integer (INVALID_MODEL_CONTEXT), defaultMaxTokens must be a positive safe integer (INVALID_MODEL_MAX_TOKENS), systemPromptUpdate must be 'in-history', and a reasoning block must carry at least one effort, unique non-empty ids, and a defaultEffort that names a declared effort (INVALID_MODEL_REASONING) (747-846). Adapters own the concrete catalogues: DeepSeek ships DEFAULT_MODELS (deepseek-flash, deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp) with contextWindow/inputModalities/image budgets/systemPromptUpdate and validates every entry (llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:92-122, 224-269), while pi-ai materializes each model as installed-catalog entry spread overridden by the profile, with contextWindow = entry ?? base ?? request.defaultContextWindow and maxTokens = entry ?? base ?? request.defaultMaxTokens (llm-pi-ai/src/catalog.ts:901-930).
invariants: Catalogue membership is advisory; an adapter may accept unlisted model ids and absence must never become request rejection.
Exact-model metadata is validated at the seam boundary, so a misbehaving adapter fails loud instead of poisoning downstream pricing/preflight decisions.
pi-ai keeps the model's capability maxTokens separate from the deployment's defaultMaxTokens, because they answer different questions (catalog.ts:809-811).
constants: DeepSeek catalog entries: 4 default models; per-entry contextWindow, maxTokens, inputModalities min 1, imagePixelBudget ('low' or positive integer), imageMaxBytes (llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:92-122, 175-185)
validation codes: INVALID_CATALOG, INVALID_MODEL_INFO, INVALID_MODEL_CONTEXT, INVALID_MODEL_MAX_TOKENS, INVALID_MODEL_REASONING (llm/llm/src/index.ts:706, 762-838)

model.name: provider-model-discovery-service
model.what: Discovery is keyed by settings namespace rather than by route, because a provider being ADDED has no route to name: registerModelDiscovery(settingsNs, discover) registers an offer that is disposed with the fiber, and discoverModels(settingsNs, request, signal) requires either a provider route or a baseURL (INVALID_DISCOVERY), throws NO_DISCOVERY for an unregistered namespace, and deduplicates by id in endpoint order (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:555-617). The same operation is exposed on the RPC plane as @Remote('discoverModels') remoteDiscoverModels, wrapping any failure in RemoteError 'llm/model-discovery-rejected' carrying the settings namespace and endpoint (627-646, declared at types.ts:274-282). The pi-ai adapter answers a route its installed catalogue ships from that catalogue with no network call, and only interrogates routes it does not describe over LISTABLE_PROTOCOLS (anthropic-messages, openai-completions, openai-responses); responses are capped at MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES (llm-pi-ai/src/discovery.ts:1-43, 48-58).
invariants: Discovery is a draft interrogation: nothing is stored, and settings.yaml remains the only thing that decides what a route serves.
A namespace is the addressing key, so a provider being added can be interrogated before it has a route.
A protocol whose listing shape is unknown reports that it cannot be interrogated rather than guessing response fields (Azure, Codex/OAuth and the remaining pi-ai protocols are deliberately absent).

model.name: reasoning-effort-translation
model.what: Harness-side reasoning effort is an opaque adapter-owned ReasoningEffortId. The seam validates it against the exact model's declared efforts and materializes the adapter's defaultEffort into the request config; an explicit unsupported effort throws UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT before any provider I/O, with no clamping or aliasing, and the materialized fields are recorded on the prepared call as adapterDefaults so logging can distinguish caller choice from adapter default (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:872-906, 925-932; call-config.ts:23-39). The DeepSeek adapter translates the resolved effort into its wire pair: 'off' -> thinking disabled (never sent as a wire effort), 'low'|'high'|'max' -> thinking enabled plus reasoning_effort, and a session-title purpose forces thinking disabled; a deployment with thinking:'disabled' rejects any non-off effort both at load and at request time (llm-deepseek/src/serialize.ts:71-99, 362-364; index.ts:311-315). Its resolved model metadata advertises either the off-only effort list or the four-level list with the configured default (llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts:168-200, 418-436).
invariants: The effort vocabulary is adapter-owned and opaque to the harness; the seam only checks membership in the declared set.
Unsupported explicit efforts reject before provider I/O; no silent clamping, aliasing or dropping.
'off' is a harness/thinking concept and must never be emitted as a provider wire effort.
constants: DeepSeek efforts: off, low, high, max; default when unset: high (llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts:168-200; llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:132, 141-142)

model.name: context-window-and-max-output-metadata
model.what: Context capacity and the output cap are resolved per exact route and materialized into the call: resolveCallWithInfo fills maxTokens from the adapter's defaultMaxTokens only when the caller omitted one, and returns the LlmModelContext alongside the config (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:872-905). prepareCall then detaches and deep-freezes the config, the context and the modalities, and records which of reasoningEffort/maxTokens the adapter supplied rather than the caller (921-942); LlmAdapter.prepareCall binds that metadata to the same adapter generation as the eventual dispatch, so a settings change between preparation and dispatch cannot combine one generation's capabilities with another's endpoint (259-274). The DeepSeek adapter defaults are DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 1,000,000 and DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 256,000 with per-model overrides, and an uncatalogued model is advertised as text-only rather than claiming unverified image capability (llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts:145-149, 400-417).
invariants: An adapter-supplied default is materialized only when the caller omitted the field; adapterDefaults records the difference for logging.
Capability metadata is captured with the dispatch generation, so preparation and dispatch never mix generations.
Unverified capability is not advertised: an unknown model is reported text-only.
constants: deepseek config bounds: fileExpiresAfterSeconds 3_600..2_592_000 (default 604_800); fileQuotaCleanupBatch 1..1_000 (default 100); filesApiTimeoutMs default 60_000; maxInlineRequestImageBytes default 20 MiB; imageOffloadByteQuantum default 64 MiB; inlineImageOffloadByteQuantum default 10 MiB; imageOffloadCountQuantum default 20; maxImagesPerRequest default 600 (llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:152-166, 195-205)

model.name: provider-credential-resolution-and-layered-sources
model.what: The credential seam has two key spaces: a CredentialRef (an environment-variable-shaped name) answers what is behind that name through layered resolution, and a CredentialKey ('<scope>/<id>') answers what credential a plugin holds for one of its own ids, where presence of the record is the whole fact and modifyRecord is the only write path because a correct write depends on the current value (packages/credentials/credentials/src/index.ts:19-22, 154-250). Resolution is per operation and must not be cached, an empty stored value is absent everywhere, and set/unset reject while a read-only source shadows the reference (175-209). The local provider lays the sources in trust order — inherited process environment (read-only, wins) > $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml (managed, writable) > cwd/.env > $DSH_HOME/.env — and reports the winning layer as the source id 'env' | 'file' | <dotenv> (credentials-local/src/index.ts:1-27, 617-639). Adapters then enforce the transport invariant: normalizeApiKey trims and accepts only printable ASCII excluding space, and assertUsableApiKey throws INVALID_CREDENTIAL without ever echoing the key (llm/llm/src/api-key.ts:15, 36-41; llm/llm/src/index.ts:145-160). DeepSeek re-resolves the key per request and sends it as 'authorization: Bearer' (llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts:479, 539-541); pi-ai refuses to fall back to ambient discovery once a profile names a credential reference, throwing MISSING_CREDENTIAL instead of silently billing another tenant (llm-pi-ai/src/index.ts:168-191).
invariants: Secrets never round-trip to a surface: describe/describeRecord/listRecords expose presence, kind and writability, never the value.
Consumers re-resolve per operation and must not cache across operations, which is what makes a changed credential reach the next request without a restart.
A named credential reference that does not resolve is a hard MISSING_CREDENTIAL, never a fallback to ambient discovery.
constants: credentials document path: $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml; file mode 0o600, dir mode 0o700; group/other bits 0o077 rejected; document version 1 (credentials-local/src/index.ts:61, 97, 167, 699)

model.name: oauth-authorization-flow-registry
model.what: ctx.authorization owns the human conversation and lifecycle of obtaining a credential, never the protocol: a plugin registers an AuthorizationFlow keyed by the CredentialKey it writes, with a label and a non-empty methods tuple, and the flow talks to whichever surface started it through one neutral vocabulary of notify/prompt (packages/credentials/authorization/src/index.ts:1-27, 90-159). Registration is one flow per key (DUPLICATE_FLOW) and a flow leaving mid-attempt aborts its running attempt, because the fiber that could answer for it is going away (202-218). begin() enforces one attempt per key at a time (ALREADY_IN_FLIGHT), refuses an unknown method (UNKNOWN_METHOD) and an unclaimed key (NO_FLOW), returns 'cancelled' for a signal already aborted before the slot is claimed, and only reports 'authorized' when the flow's record was committed and observed during the attempt (NOT_COMMITTED otherwise); the key slot is released before authorization/settled is fanned out with contained listeners (258-347). The write itself goes through ctx.credentials.modifyRecord, which the seam requires (static inject = ['credentials'], line 184); pi-ai stores its OAuth grant payload verbatim as an opaque grant record so the library keeps owning its token format (llm-pi-ai/src/auth.ts:64-100).
invariants: The seam owns the lifecycle and never the protocol: a second authorization protocol arrives as another flow, not another seam.
One attempt per key at a time; a second caller is refused rather than joined, because it would prompt a different human through the same flow.
Success requires an observed credential-record commit; a flow that resolves without writing is NOT_COMMITTED.
constants: error codes: DUPLICATE_FLOW, NO_FLOW, UNKNOWN_METHOD, ALREADY_IN_FLIGHT, NOT_COMMITTED (authorization/src/index.ts:206, 279-288, 272)
declined prompt code: 'DECLINED' via AuthorizationDeclinedError, settling the attempt as cancelled (authorization/src/index.ts:79-84)

model.name: provider-retry-policy-and-execution
model.what: Retry policy is provider-owned and resolved once when the route is registered: resolveRetryPolicy validates and freezes either a bounded 'normal' policy (mode, maxRetries, retryableCodes, backoff) or an unbounded 'always' policy, rejecting unknown keys, a non-positive or over-large delay, initialDelayMs > maxDelayMs, and an out-of-range jitter ratio (packages/llm/llm/src/retry-policy.ts:26-103, 121-194); prepareRoutes captures the resolved policy on the AdapterRegistration (llm/llm/src/index.ts:436-442) and providerRetryPolicy(provider) reads it back (653-655). Execution lives in the optional dsh-llm-retry plugin on the agent's request-recovery waterfall: a 'normal' policy only handles its configured retryable codes, an 'always' policy retries every failure until success, cancellation or disposal; the attempt is made durable as an llm/retry event BEFORE the cancellable wait and llm/retry-started after it, with the retry counter folded from the llmRetry session projection keyed by provider plus a policy key (llm-retry/src/index.ts:194-241, 123-138). A provider-supplied providerRetryAfterMs is honored only when it does not exceed maxDelayMs under a normal policy (otherwise the decision passes downstream); otherwise the delay is exponential with symmetric jitter clamped to maxDelayMs (227-240, 59-64).
invariants: The policy is immutable registration state: a change re-registers the route rather than mutating a live policy.
Every scheduled retry is durable in the session log before its cancellable wait, and a disposal aborts and drains active recovery.
The harness never retries INVALID_CREDENTIAL by default, because a malformed credential fails identically on every attempt.
constants: default retryable codes: EMPTY_RESPONSE, RATE_LIMIT, SERVER, TIMEOUT, TRANSPORT (retry-policy.ts:18-24)
delays bounded by MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS from dsh-timeout (retry-policy.ts:82-83)

model.name: streaming-call-dispatch-and-chunk-assembly
model.what: LlmRuntime.stream routes every call through the ctx.waterfall('llm/stream') chain into adapterStream, which resolves the registration, normalizes exact-model metadata, materializes the call config, projects file attachments to text handles (files are never dispatched natively) and strips images for models whose inputModalities exclude 'image' (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:1011-1058, 1106-1120). Adapter selection, dispatch, iterator construction and iteration failures all become one terminal finish chunk — {kind:'aborted'} when the signal aborted, else {kind:'error'} — while middleware, nested-call, cleanup and consumer failures stay thrown (1060-1093, 1124-1132). The consumer half is BlockAssembler, the single canonical chunk-to-message algorithm: it tolerates delta-only protocols, ignores deltas and re-closes arriving after a block was closed, drops tool-call blocks under a max-tokens finish because they cannot be executed safely, and prunes the adapter's replay envelope in step with the emitted blocks (discarding it entirely when entries do not align) (assembler.ts:38-96, 130-150). It also exposes interruptedBlocks() — closed and open text/reasoning blocks with non-whitespace content, tool calls omitted — as the prefix a cancelled stream can safely finalize (169-179).
invariants: Every adapter-side failure becomes a terminal chunk in the stream protocol; only middleware and consumer failures throw.
One keep/drop decision governs both emitted blocks and replay metadata, so stored content and stored metadata cannot disagree.
An interrupted stream finalizes text/reasoning only: a retained tool call would require a fabricated result.
constants: finish reason defaults to {kind:'stop'} when no finish chunk arrived (assembler.ts:186-189)

model.name: llm-failure-taxonomy-and-normalization
model.what: Failures are classified by a stable machine-routable code on HarnessError, explicitly never by parsing the message (packages/llm/llm/src/error.ts:13-22). The seam publishes canonical provider-neutral codes — CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED, QUOTA, EMPTY_RESPONSE (a degenerate completion carrying no content blocks, classified as a failure instead of yielding an empty assistant message, and safe to retry) and INVALID_CREDENTIAL (malformed rather than absent, deliberately outside the default retryable set) — plus regex classifiers that recognize the context-overflow wording used by OpenAI-compatible providers (error.ts:24-80). normalizeLlmFailure is the adapter-boundary chokepoint: it detaches serializable provider facts, trusts an error's carried `failure` payload only when its own `code` data property agrees after validation, reads via own-property descriptors so SDK-defined accessors cannot run, tolerates non-Error throws, and maps third-party SDK codes to 'UNKNOWN' because they are not this taxonomy (adapter-failure.ts:16-28, 40-104).
invariants: Consumers route on `code`, never on message text.
Foreign SDK codes are not adopted into the taxonomy; only Harness-owned codes survive normalization.
A degenerate empty completion is a classified failure, not an empty assistant message.
constants: status validation range 100..599 on a carried failure snapshot (adapter-failure.ts:74)

model.name: deepseek-wire-protocol-and-request-extensions
model.what: The DeepSeek adapter speaks chat-completions over SSE: it serializes thinking/reasoning_effort and messages into the wire body (llm-deepseek/src/serialize.ts:82-99, 360-364) and sends 'authorization: Bearer <key>', 'accept: text/event-stream', the mandatory attribution headers, 'x-deepseek-harness-user-id' (the anonymous harness-home id) and 'x-deepseek-harness-session-id', plus 'x-deepseek-harness-compact: 1' for a compaction-purpose request (llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts:539-551). A per-read idle watchdog enforces streamIdleTimeoutMs and reports LLM_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT, while caller aborts map to ABORTED and anything else to TRANSPORT (adapter.ts:481-527, 166-167). Attribution is centralized so adapters cannot drift and cannot suppress it: attributionHeaders() defaults to APP_IDENTITY {product:'deepseek-harness', version from package.json, repository url} rendered as 'product/version (+url)' (llm/llm/src/attribution.ts:40-67), a contract stated on LlmAdapter itself (llm/llm/src/index.ts:194-199). Independent top-level request fields are owned by plugins through the deepseek-llm-api-extensions registry: register() claims one field name exclusively and prepare() runs every provider from one immutable base request, freezing cloned values and returning a joint, idempotent accept() transaction that settles every callback before reporting failures (deepseek-llm-api-extensions/src/index.ts:79-129).
invariants: Every provider HTTP request must carry the attribution headers; nothing can suppress them.
One plugin owns one top-level request field; a second registration of the same field throws.
Extension preparation failures reject before HTTP dispatch, and callers hold no mutable alias to the outgoing request.
constants: default endpoint: https://api.deepseek.com, overridable by $DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL from a trusted environment layer (llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:209-213, 394-396)
provider route: 'deepseek-official'; default credential ref: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:88-90)

model.name: plugin-package-attribution-inventory
model.what: plugin-package-inventory-deepseek contributes a 'dsh_plugin_packages' top-level field to official DeepSeek requests through the extension registry: prepare() collects the active Loader entries (excluding groups, disabled rows and non-ACTIVE fibers), optionally adds the requesting agent's standing preset tree resolved through agentPresets/standingMountFor, and resolves each entry's owning package manifest {name, version} either by bare-package search anchored on the tree base or by walking up from the module path to the nearest package.json (packages/llm/plugin-package-inventory-deepseek/src/index.ts:131-179, 186-198). Installed dependencies that no active row loads, and loose modules with no package manifest, are excluded; the payload is version 1 and the list is sorted deterministically without relying on host locale or ICU data (145-178, 192-197).
invariants: Only ACTIVE, non-structural Loader entries count as loaded plugins; an installed-but-unused dependency is not reported.
The order is deterministic independent of host locale, so the same plugin set always serializes identically.
A package entry that cannot be resolved throws rather than silently dropping from the inventory.

model.name: token-metering-and-usage-projection
model.what: TokenMeter is a replay-aware service over the durable session log: it folds a per-session surface and registers the tokenUsage, contextPressure and contextBreakdown projection units (packages/llm/token-meter/src/index.ts:100-122). measure() reuses provider usage only when the latest successful call's canonical request envelope matches the one being measured and the provider total is no lower than that call's full route-priced anchor; otherwise the whole envelope and surface are repriced, so a provider that under-reports cannot mask growth (145-150, 46-67). Provider usage is summed from disjoint buckets — inputTokens + cacheReadTokens + cacheWriteTokens + outputTokens — so reasoning output is never double-counted (69-75). Surface pricing asks the routed adapter for image pricing (LlmAdapter.imageRequestPricing, resolved per measurement, synchronous, no I/O) and fails loud if the number of prices does not match the number of image occurrences, because misalignment would silently misprice nodes (route-pricing.ts:23-76; llm/llm/src/index.ts:219-230, 666-668).
invariants: Provider usage is trusted only under a matching canonical envelope and a total no lower than the route-priced anchor.
Pricing answers must align one-to-one with the priced occurrences; a mismatch throws rather than mispricing.
The meter accepts no configuration keys at all: validateConfigKeys throws on any key.
constants: no supported config keys; any key throws (index.ts:86-91, 103)
usage buckets summed: inputTokens + cacheReadTokens + cacheWriteTokens + outputTokens (index.ts:70-75)

model.name: agent-default-model-resolution
model.what: AgentDefaultModelConfig (ctx.agentDefaultModel) owns the default model selection for Agents created without an explicit one, independently of any Host or transport: a composition entry {provider, model} is always usable on its own, and when a settings provider is mounted the 'agent-default-model' section supplies a live user layer read through currentSelection() (packages/core/agent-default-model/src/index.ts:20-38, 64-92). The projection onto the Agent-facing ModelSelection converts the stored reasoningEffort string into a branded ReasoningEffortId, and saveSelection writes the complete selection back through ctx.settings.replace, tolerating a deployment with no settings provider (48-57, 94-106). Because every consumer reads through currentSelection(), no registration-level fact needs rebuilding when the settings document changes (76-82).
invariants: The composition entry is always usable without a settings provider; the user layer is optional and read live.
The stored selection is projected into a branded ModelSelection at the boundary, so an unvalidated string never reaches request headers.
Save writes the complete selection (provider, model and optional reasoning effort) so a partial update cannot leave a stale effort behind.

model.name: http-proxy-transport-policy
model.what: Node's fetch ignores HTTP_PROXY, so this library resolves one process-wide policy from the launch environment and installs it as undici's global dispatcher, which is what fetch resolves — covering LLM adapters, web search, MCP over HTTP and telemetry without touching their code (packages/util/http-proxy/src/index.ts:1-23; install.ts:194-215). Policy resolution is pure and transport-free: it reads each name lowercase-first with the uppercase fallback and treats a blank value as unset (undici's own ?? chain would let an empty lowercase name shadow a populated uppercase one), merges LOOPBACK_NO_PROXY unconditionally because a proxying harness would route its own Web UI and local servers into a loop, routes only http:/https: URLs, and reports SOCKS/PAC values as diagnostics instead of silently dropping them (policy.ts:33-98, 109-118). A rejected slot is distinct from an absent one, so a scheme whose proxy was rejected stays direct rather than borrowing another scheme's proxy. The install publishes the resolved policy into the proxy environment variables for consumers that read the environment and for spawned children, and exposes clearedProxyEnv() as the overlay that strips every proxy name from a replay child (install.ts:70-92, 228-254, 296-314).
invariants: The loopback bypass is not optional and is always merged into the policy.
A value this package cannot route is reported, never silently dropped, and never replaced by another scheme's proxy.
The policy is plain data with no methods, so worker threads receive the identical policy through structured clone rather than re-reading a possibly different environment.
constants: routed schemes: http:, https:; SOCKS/PAC schemes only named in a diagnostic (policy.ts:57-60)
env names per field: http_proxy/HTTP_PROXY, https_proxy/HTTPS_PROXY, no_proxy/NO_PROXY, plus the all_proxy/ALL_PROXY fallback that is resolved but never written back (policy.ts:39-54)

extension.name: mcp-client-connection-supervision-and-reconnect
extension.what: startConnection() in the MCP client bridge owns one MCP SDK Client generation per plugin instance and restarts the configured server with bounded exponential backoff when the connection drops. createTransport() selects either a StdioClientTransport whose child env is built by buildChildEnv() from scrubbedParentEnv() plus spec env, or a StreamableHTTPClientTransport over an explicit URL and header map. scheduleReconnect() keeps one shared attempt budget per outage: the delay is initialDelayMs * 2 ** (failedAttempts - 1) capped at maxDelayMs, the budget resets only when a generation stayed up for at least maxDelayMs (the stability window), and exhaustion unregisters the server's tools and stops until disposal or Host restart. Generation teardown is fail-closed: a failed generation that does not emit close within GENERATION_CLOSE_TIMEOUT_MS stops reconnection rather than overlapping child processes, and apply() rejects the fiber only when failOnStartupError is set.
invariants: One outage shares one attempt budget; only a generation that survives the maxDelayMs stability window opens a fresh budget.
A generation may act only while it is the current one on a live plugin (isCurrent), so racing close/error signals stay idempotent.
An armed reconnect timer is unref'd and a generation proven unclosed aborts reconnection instead of spawning an overlapping server.
constants: RECONNECT_DEFAULTS = { enabled: true, initialDelayMs: 500, maxDelayMs: 30000, maxAttempts: 10 } (connection.ts:40-45)

extension.name: mcp-tool-bridging-and-namespace-isolation
extension.what: syncTools() bridges an MCP server's tool list into the harness ToolRuntime under deterministic server-qualified public names. publicToolName() composes mcp__<serverName>__<rawName>, replacing characters outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] and appending 12 hex chars of a SHA-256 over (serverName, rawName) whenever normalization or the 64-character function-name cap changed the name, so distinct MCP identities never collapse. The sync is two-phase: phase 1 drains paginated tools/list (duplicate raw names or a repeated continuation cursor reject as an invalid list, leaving the prior generation registered), phase 2 disposes the previous generation and registers the new one, rolling back to zero tools if a foreign registration squats the namespace. Execution sends tools/call with the raw wire name and maps MCP content blocks through projectContent(); image blocks are validated as canonical base64 and durably stored via ctx.attachments only after the exact model route proves image input, otherwise each image becomes diagnostic text while the raw value stays available to programmatic callers.
invariants: The raw MCP name is sent only on the wire and is never recovered by parsing the public name; (serverName, rawName) is the stable identity.
The model sees either the complete next tool generation or the previous one, never a partial set.
An advertised output schema unsupported by assertSupportedJsonSchema falls back to plain JsonValue rather than rejecting the tool.

extension.name: lsp-provider-registry-and-extension-routing
extension.what: ctx.lsp is a Service Definition exposing exactly four normalized operations (goToDefinition, findReferences, goToImplementation, hover) and a provider registry keyed by branded provider id and exclusive file extensions. registerProvider() validates the id, every normalized lowercase leading-dot extension, intra-provider duplicates and cross-provider conflicts before any mutation, then reserves the id and all extensions inside one ctx.effect whose disposer releases them together, so an invalid or conflicting registration publishes nothing. query() routes a request by the file's final extension only (finalExtension(), which splits on both separators and returns '' for dotfiles) and never depends on registration order; an unroutable path throws LspError LSP_UNAVAILABLE. The seam deliberately exposes no JSON-RPC escape hatch.
invariants: A published route always has a live provider: id and extensions are reserved and released atomically.
Selection is a pure function of the file's final extension, never of registration order.
An invalid or conflicting registration mutates no registry state.
constants: Stable LspError codes: LSP_INVALID_PROVIDER, LSP_CONFLICT, LSP_UNAVAILABLE, LSP_DISPOSED, LSP_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION, LSP_MALFORMED_RESPONSE (index.ts:44-49)

extension.name: lsp-stdio-server-pooling-and-transient-document-lifecycle
extension.what: lsp-stdio resolves every configured executable through ctx.subprocess.resolveExecutable before publishing any provider, then registers one LocalLspProvider per server table entry that lazily single-flights one LspInstance per canonical workspace key and serializes each query lifecycle on a per-workspace promise queue. LspInstance.initialize() sends processId: null with the workspace folder URI, the client capability set, and static initializationOptions, negotiates utf-16 position encoding, and then serves each query as textDocument/didOpen followed by the operation request and didClose; findReferences always sets context.includeDeclaration: true. raceAbort() sends $/cancelRequest and, if the request does not settle within killGraceMs, tears the instance down so an ignored cancellation cannot overlap the next queued document lifecycle; servers the host cannot drive (workspace/applyEdit) are refused and only lifecycle bookkeeping requests are acknowledged. LspConnection frames JSON-RPC itself, caps message and stderr bytes, answers workspace/configuration from static config, and treats a framing/JSON failure as fatal by failing the connection and terminating the managed process range; teardown is bounded shutdown/exit then SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL with awaited process close.
invariants: One server process per (provider id, canonical workspace); a dead or failed instance is evicted and never reused.
Queries are read-only, so a transport failure may be replaced and retried at most once per query; cancellation that the server ignores terminates the instance.
Disposal owes quiescence: process close and managed-range exit are awaited, not merely requested.

extension.name: lsp-model-facing-tool-and-result-caps
extension.what: tool-lsp registers one read-only model-facing `lsp` tool with a closed four-operation enum plus a system-prompt section positioned as a precision aid for ambiguous textual matches. The tool requires the session workspace cwd through sessionCwd(exec) with no fallback, converts the model's one-based UTF-16 line/character coordinates into the seam's positions, and renders locations or hover text through formatLocations/formatHover under maxLocations and maxResultChars caps. Its output schema is a closed oneOf over locations and hover, and the definition carries timeoutMs for the cooperative tool-call timeout policy. Config values are validated at load so a non-positive or over-large cap fails the plugin.
invariants: The tool runtime-injects only tools, lsp, and systemPrompt and imports no concrete provider.
A missing session workspace is an error, not a silent fallback to the process cwd.
Declared caps must be positive integers and the timeout must not exceed MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS.

extension.name: skill-registry-layered-precedence-and-caching
extension.what: SkillRegistry is the ctx.skills layer registry: provider catalogs and runtime contributions file into the calling context's scope layer, a read merges the global layer with the viewing scope's chain, and the nearest layer wins a duplicate name outright while rank decides duplicates only within one layer (compareIndexedCandidates orders by rank, then provider registration order, then local order). registerProvider() reserves the provider name `runtime` and aborts the registration's lifecycle signal on disposal; register() adds whole runtime definitions with rank 250 and first-wins semantics. collect() memoizes completed catalogs under JSON.stringify({cwd, scopes, revision}) with a bounded insertion-ordered cache, retries once when a concurrent mutation changed the revision, and never caches an incomplete provider observation, so consumers can keep last-good state. get() validates the loaded definition, passes the opaque locator back to the owning provider, and invalidates the entry when the returned name disagrees with the selected candidate, but only while that exact provider registration is still live.
invariants: A nearer scope layer shadows farther layers regardless of rank; rank only breaks ties inside one layer.
An incomplete provider catalog is never cached, and a skill body is validated before it reaches a consumer.
A stale-definition invalidation must not evict a newer registration's cache.

extension.name: filesystem-skill-discovery-and-watch-invalidation
extension.what: FileSystemSkillProvider scans project roots (.dsh/skills and .agents/skills under the nearest ancestor containing the project-root marker), custom dirs, user roots ($DSH_HOME/skills, ~/.agents/skills, where .system is skipped), and an optional bundled root, with fixed ranks 100/200/300/400/500/600 deciding intra-layer precedence. Directory bundles load SKILL.md and flat .md files are also accepted; parseSkillFile requires YAML frontmatter delimited by --- with string name and description, rejects legacy camelCase invocation keys, reads disable-model-invocation/user-invocable through a boolean-ish parser, and reads an optional metadata map. SkillWatchManager keeps bounded chokidar watchers (evicting the oldest project when the cap is exceeded, and watching an ancestor for a root that does not exist yet) and turns any relevant event, watcher error, or first-party fs mutation observed through the fs/observed event into one coalesced microtask catalog invalidation. The bundled dsh-badge provider registers through the same seam with BUNDLED_SKILL_RANK and a directory resourceBase.
invariants: A skill file missing frontmatter, name, description, or a valid kebab-case name is skipped with a warning, never fatal to discovery.
The bundled root is host-trusted and is read through node fs rather than the ctx.fs provider, and is only mounted when default roots are included.
Watcher counts stay bounded and a watch failure degrades the observation to incomplete instead of failing the read.
constants: Root ranks: PROJECT_DSH_RANK 100, PROJECT_AGENTS_RANK 200, CUSTOM_RANK 300, USER_DSH_RANK 400, USER_AGENTS_RANK 500, BUNDLED_SKILL_RANK 600 (index.ts:36-40, skill/skill/src/index.ts:28)

extension.name: skill-catalog-injection-and-model-facing-loader
extension.what: tool-skill registers the model-facing `skill` loader, which resolves the name through ctx.skills.list()/get() with the calling agent as the scope key and re-checks isModelInvocable on both the summary and the loaded definition before returning the body. A second agent/pre-step listener publishes the session skill catalog as a durable catalog-form user message whose recorded entries mirror the rendered lines; it republishes only when the SHA-256 digest over those durable entries changes, emits a replacement catalog when the tool registration is visible to the agent, and otherwise removes a stale catalog message. A third listener scans only source.kind === 'user' messages for whitespace-bounded /name gestures and injects the rendered <skill_content> as an instructions-form context message for user-invocable skills, which is the only entry point for disable-model-invocation skills. The browser half registers the '/' input source and single-flights the per-session skills/list RPC addressed by sessionId.
invariants: Only claimed user messages can trigger the /name gesture; unknown or user-disabled names remain ordinary prose.
Catalog identity is computed over the durable entry list, never over model-facing prose framing.
The catalog is emitted only while this plugin's exact tool definition is the visible registration, so a scoped shadow does not inherit it.

extension.name: hook-protocol-execution-and-vendor-dialect-bridges
extension.what: The non-plugin hook-protocol library runs configured command hooks through ctx.shell: runHook() serializes the bridge-built payload to stdin with an optional trailing newline (Claude Code yes, Codex no), merges explicit env after the executor's scrub, applies the per-hook timeoutSec override or the bridge's defaultTimeoutMs, and decodes the captured outcome with parseHookOutput; an infrastructure rejection becomes an outcome with no exit code so a hook can never crash the calling turn. mergeHookOutputs folds every matched hook into one most-restrictive outcome under deny > ask > allow with a sticky first continue:false stop and joined reasons, and matchesMatcher applies the dialect rule (Claude treats purely word-and-pipe patterns as literal | alternatives, Codex treats every pattern as an unanchored regex, absent/empty/'*' match all, invalid regex is a non-match). Durable logging appends a turn-enclosed hook/invoked plus hook/result pair per hook with a capped stderr summary. On top of that library hooks-claude-code and hooks-codex run unmodified vendor hooks on harness interception points: Claude Code supports SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop and SubagentStart/Stop with Claude-shaped stdin payloads, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} substitution and a per-run CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR env, while Codex supports five points with regex-only matchers, snake_case payloads, no hook environment and only blocking decisions honored; both run emit-shaped lifecycle points detached with a drained disposal, and both log-and-ignore updatedInput (CC only) and systemMessage.
invariants: A hook that cannot run is a non-blocking error: runHook never throws into the calling turn and non-numeric exit codes map to undefined.
hook/invoked and hook/result stay turn-enclosed and paired; emit-shaped lifecycle points omit the pair.
The matcher dialect decides literal-versus-regex interpretation, and the stderr summary cap is passed in by the bridge rather than defaulted by the library.
constants: Both bridges default defaultTimeoutMs to 600000 and stderrSummaryMaxChars to 500 (hooks-claude-code/src/index.ts:71-77, hooks-codex/src/index.ts:59-64)

extension.name: dynamic-cordis-package-sandbox-approval-and-client-execution
extension.what: DynamicCordisRunnerService keeps immutable package versions per plugin with one active run, mints semantic plugin IDs plus package/run/approval IDs in DynamicCordisRegistry, and evaluates a package's host half in a fresh node:vm realm whose globals are a package-tagged console, harness.handle/defineTool/registerTool, and traps that redirect require/fetch/timers to cordis services (the module documents this as inspectability and disposability, explicitly not containment). startHostHalf() awaits the cordis-dynamic group, mounts the guarded plugin as a child fiber, and disposes it before rethrowing a startup failure so a failed run never lingers, while missingServices() reports the inject names a settled-but-pending fiber still waits for. Client-bearing packages are approval-gated: run() mints and arms an approval request, emits cordis/request-run, and runHostHalf() refuses unless the request still identifies the plugin's latest run, recording per-package approval or plugin-wide approval for future versions; the browser half is served only through getClientCode for the exact active run. extension surfaces are exposed as Typert @Remote methods (runHostHalf, getClientCode, resolveRequestRun, settleUserRun, stopFromPanel, undefineFromPanel, inventory, inspect resolution, invoke, failure reports) consumed by ui-cordis, and tool-cordis registers the model-facing cordis_inspect_list, cordis_inspect_query and cordis_inspect_self tools plus the define/run/stop surface over the same service.
invariants: One active run per plugin; source and identity are immutable per package ID and Client source is served only for the exact active run.
A failed host-half activation is disposed before the error propagates, so no failed fiber stays mounted.
Approval identity is re-verified against the latest run before activation, and a plugin-wide approval only covers later versions when explicitly granted.
constants: Sandbox builtins: ctx, harness, console, btoa, atob, TextEncoder, TextDecoder (sandbox.ts:18-43)
Trapped Node APIs: require, setTimeout, setInterval, setImmediate, clearTimeout, clearInterval, fetch (sandbox.ts:96-108)

extension.name: plugin-inventory-rpc-and-configurable-settings-surfaces
extension.what: PluginInventoryGateway is a TypertRemoteService exposing a single @Remote('list') that reads ctx.loader.entries() on every call, skips group entries, and projects each entry's Cordis Fiber.state into a serializable phase (pending, loading, active, failed, unloading, or null for disposed), appending agent-preset composition rows when an agentPresets roster is composed instead of caching a second lifecycle truth. The browser half ui-settings-plugin-inventory contributes a lazy read-only tab (id 'all', order 10) into the settings.plugins.tab slot and calls ctx.remote.pluginInventory.list() per open. The companion ui-settings-plugins package mounts the configurable tab and ships per-plugin cards (shell/bash, agent loop, web search, subagent model selection) whose controllers bind a settings namespace through ctx.settingsScope and refresh on credentials/reference-updated, llm/adapters-updated, settings/document-updated and connection/reset.
invariants: The inventory is derived from the Loader on every call and never becomes a second source of plugin lifecycle state.
A settings card writes only through its own bound settings namespace scope, so cards stay unaware of one another.
A card reports credential state from forwarded credential events because a credential is not part of any settings section.
constants: Fiber phase projection covers PENDING 0, LOADING 1, ACTIVE 2, FAILED 3, DISPOSED 4 (null), UNLOADING 5 (plugin-inventory/src/index.ts:26-43)

extension.name: workspace-instruction-baseline-and-change-projection
extension.what: agent-instructions loads AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md-family workspace instruction files into durable model context. compose() finds the project root by walking up from the session cwd to the configured marker set, derives a workspaceBaselineIdentity from the discovery configuration plus the relative project root, and decides whether a resumed or forked session's visible baseline source still matches that identity before reusing its excluded scopes; otherwise loadBaselineInstructionSet rebuilds it. Successful read/write/edit tool results whose file_path lies inside an instruction scope queue dynamic projection of nested, changed, and removed files, composed against the inbox produced by earlier results for the same agent and committed only at an execution-ancestry and step boundary. Two byte budgets bound the feature: maxBytes for one rendered baseline or dynamic batch (non-positive or non-finite disables loading entirely) and maxSourceBytes per instruction file, which is ignored when exceeded; without a ctx.fs provider the plugin degrades to a no-op.
invariants: A visible baseline is reused only when its recorded identity matches the current discovery configuration and workspace.
Dynamic instruction projection composes in order per agent and commits only inside the enclosing durable step.
An instruction file larger than maxSourceBytes is ignored rather than silently truncated.
constants: File-touching tool names tracked for projection: read, write, edit (index.ts:73)

extension.name: settings-namespace-registry-and-file-backed-persistence
extension.what: SettingsProvider (ctx.settings) owns namespace registration, composition-base/schema/user-layer resolution, deep-frozen resolved values, change detection and the settings/updated commit event, while providers implement only load()/persist(). register() rejects duplicates and invalid namespace ids and files the registration as an effect on the calling fiber; each namespace carries a monotonic revision over its RAW user section so an editor holding a stale snapshot is refused with SettingsConflictError code SETTINGS_CONFLICT. Writes are serialized per namespace on settled promise chains, and path-addressed SettingsPathOp set/unset mutations exist so a caller holding a redacted (secret-stripped) descriptor can name one field without restating the section and silently deleting secrets. The file provider resolves settings.yaml under the harness home, patches a YAML/JSON document leaf-by-leaf to preserve comments and anchors, and performs every write as a lock-guarded read-modify-write with reconcileFromDisk() so an unobserved external edit cannot be resurrected; chokidar events (with an at-ready reconcile) hot-publish external edits, and the document is created owner-only (0700 dir, 0600 file). A package-owned invariant companion asserts that settings/updated fires only for a registered namespace, only with the service's authoritative resolved value, and only on an actual value change.
invariants: A namespace registration is a fiber effect: disposing the registrant removes the namespace and its observers.
A write must not resurrect unobserved on-disk state, and an unparsable existing document fails loud instead of being overwritten.
Secret-role fields never ride the verbatim default to a wire surface; redacting surfaces must pass redactSecrets.
constants: File provider debounceMs default 100 ms, watcher pollInterval = max(1, min(debounceMs, 10)) (settings-file/src/index.ts:66, settings-file/src/index.ts:241-244)
Format map: .yaml/.yml -> yaml, .json -> json; anything else fails resolution (settings-file/src/index.ts:36-40, settings-file/src/index.ts:58-61)

extension.name: durable-todo-goal-schedule-and-workflow-extension-state
extension.what: Four capabilities persist extension state in the session log or drive bounded extension runs. tool-todo appends a whole-list todo/write snapshot per call (last-write-wins on replay, non-agent callers rejected, allowParallelInProgress deciding whether several items may be in_progress), and a projection exposes the latest list to UIs. goal keeps a durable goal/change snapshot stream with an admitted-round counter: create/edit/resume/clear commit full snapshots through GoalService.commit(), a replayed round-advance user message must be exactly roundsStarted + 1 and within maxGoalRounds, and resume is refused once the round budget is exhausted. schedule folds versioned durable records (after/at/every) plus dispatch history, enforces MIN_EVERY_INTERVAL_SECONDS for fixed-rate rules, models delivery as session-local to the original session, and advances past missed occurrences using the acceptedAt decision time. The workflow engine validates a script's meta block and body parse up front, runs the body in a fresh worker thread with agent()/pipeline()/parallel()/phase()/log()/args hooks and independent provider/model overrides, and bounds the fan-out with maxConcurrentAgents (0 resolving to min(16, availableParallelism() - 2)), maxTotalAgents, maxItemsPerCall and syncTimeoutMs.
invariants: Todo state is a whole-value replacement: every call carries the complete list and the projection folds the latest snapshot.
A goal round is admitted only as the next consecutive round of the active revision and never beyond maxGoalRounds.
A workflow run's caps are enforced by the engine: tripped caps kill the script rather than dissolving into a per-item null.
constants: SCHEDULE_CHANGE_VERSION = 1, MIN_EVERY_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 300, accepted instants bounded to four-digit years 0001..9999 (schedule/src/domain.ts:21-28)

Workflow engine defaults: maxConcurrentAgents 0 (auto), maxTotalAgents 1000, maxItemsPerCall 4096, syncTimeoutMs 5000, disposeGraceMs 5000, auto concurrency min(16, availableParallelism() - 2) (workflow-worker-thread/src/index.ts:115-122, workflow-worker-thread/src/index.ts:150-157)

service.name: typert-descriptor-codegen
service.what: Build-time generation plus runtime manifest loading of the strict Typert Remote descriptors that everything else dispatches against. `typertPlugin()` is a rolldown/tsdown plugin named `dsh-typert-generator` that lowers source decorators (target ES2024) and, in writeBundle, emits local and Host-for-Client artifacts; the workspace analyzer batches package analysis (batchSize 8) and the Cordis catalog projector truncates any declaration longer than MAX_DECL_CHARS = 1500 into a stub. At runtime the `typert-loader` plugin (inject ['typert','loader']) resolves each package.json `exports["./typert"]` target, dynamically imports it, and validates the `TYPERT` manifest via validateTypertManifest before calling ctx.typert.register. The generator package itself has no Cordis plugin row; it is build tooling.
invariants: The generated descriptor version is 1; a prototype descriptor with any other version throws rather than being coerced (typert/protocol readRemoteMethodDescriptor).
A `./typert` manifest must be owned by the exact package that exports it (manifest.package === pkgName) and must declare face 'host'.
Only public instance methods with string names may carry Remote markers; decorators on private/static/symbol members throw.
constants: MAX_DECL_CHARS = 1500 (declarations longer than this render as a truncated stub)

service.name: typert-remote-rpc-plane
service.what: The primary command/API surface of dsh is a Remote method-invocation plane, not a slash-command surface. `@Remote`/`@RemoteScope` decorators record versioned method markers on the class prototype; `TypertRemoteService` binds a Cordis service key to a wire namespace; TypertRegistry (`super(ctx, 'typert')`) holds the local/remote/lookup/context descriptor stores. `TypertGatewayService` (`super(ctx, 'typertGateway')`) intercepts the shared `/api` Connection channel, claims endpoints, and dispatches through `prepareInvocation` -> `Reflect.apply`, falling back to conservative SRC descriptors derived from `Function.prototype.toString` parameter parsing when no strict definition exists. Failures ride one `RemoteError` class discriminated by `code`, never by instanceof.
invariants: Endpoint grammar is exactly two segments `<namespace>/<method>` sharing the Connection segment pattern /^[A-Za-z0-9_$.-]+$/ with '.' and '..' rejected.
Once an endpoint's strict definition has been seen (hasSeen), SRC fallback is forbidden for it forever.
Argument objects must match the descriptor exactly: extra fields and non-omissible missing fields are refused; lookup ids are never omissible.
constants: Universal gateway error codes: gateway/bad-request, gateway/cancelled, gateway/internal (plus 17 gateway infrastructure codes merged by remote-error-codes.ts)

service.name: browser-http-api-transport
service.what: The HTTP carrier for browser and non-browser consumers. `client-connection` registers a `prefix` route at API_PATH '/api' on the webServer, bridges node:http to a WHATWG fetch handler with chunked backpressure and client-disconnect abort, and exposes a carrier-neutral registry (`ctx.connection.rpc.handle/intercept`, `ctx.connection.fetch.register`) plus `requestRejection`/`authorizeIndex` for other host routes. Exact Fetch routes registered through `ctx.connection.fetch` reuse the same fence and body cap. `host/open-in-app` is the in-tree consumer of that reused fence for its three routes.
invariants: One interceptor per channel: a second `intercept('/api', ...)` throws; the reserved channel '/api' may not be registered as a normal channel.
Buffered request bodies are capped before dispatch; the cap must be at least ceil(aggregate image limit * 4/3) + 1 MiB envelope headroom or plugin load fails.
Client-disconnect detection hangs off ServerResponse 'close' (not IncomingMessage 'close'), gated on writableEnded.

service.name: service-self-auth-token-cookie
service.what: Authentication of the service itself (not of the model provider). One process launch token is minted per root context and printed as `?token=` on the URL the launcher hands the operator; `authorizeIndex` exchanges a valid single GET / token for an HMAC-SHA256-signed, authority-bound cookie (`v1.<body>.<sig>`, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/), 303-redirecting to clean '/'. Every /api request is then checked by `isAuthenticated`, which verifies the signature, the exact Host-derived authority in the payload, and the issued/expires window. The durable signing secret is a 32-byte base64url value stored as a `grant` credential record under credentialKey('client-connection','browser-session').
invariants: Cookie name is sha256(authority)-derived with the `dsh-auth-` prefix, so one Host cannot present another Host's cookie; the payload authority must also equal the request authority.
Discrimination is by the app-level authority comparison, and both token and signature comparisons are length-checked timingSafeEqual.
The failure response is always the same minimal 401 text; no state distinguishes bad token from bad cookie.

service.name: browser-trust-fence
service.what: The pre-dispatch authority fence that every /api request passes before authentication: `isTrustedApiRequest` requires a parsable Host whose hostname is loopback or a declared `trustedHosts` authority, refuses any `sec-fetch-site: cross-site` marker, and, when an Origin is attached, requires it to normalize to exactly the Host authority. Loopback covers localhost/[::1] and 127/8; a port-less `trustedHosts` entry matches any port while an explicit `host:port` entry matches exactly. Config entries are validated at plugin load by `assertTrustedAuthority` so a typo fails the fiber instead of silently widening trust.
invariants: The Host fence applies to every request, browser-looking or not; there is deliberately no marker shortcut, because a plain-HTTP browser read carries neither Origin nor Fetch-Metadata.
A configured entry must survive WHATWG parsing unchanged (canonicalization aside) or plugin load throws.
The fence is explicitly not an auth layer; network binding belongs to webserver config and authentication to BrowserAuth.
constants: HTTP 403 for a failed fence, 401 for a failed authentication (checked in that order)

service.name: remote-stream-websocket-mux
service.what: Streaming Remote methods (mode: 'stream') do not use HTTP request/response; they ride one WebSocket mux owned by the Gateway. `RemoteStreamMuxServer` is a noServer WebSocketServer mounted on the webServer upgrade route REMOTE_STREAM_MUX_PATH '/api/remote.mux'; it applies the Connection rejection before upgrading, multiplexes many logical streams per socket, and reaps dead peers with Ping/Pong heartbeats (MAX_MISSED_HEARTBEATS = 2 at the configured interval). The Gateway's `stream()` method validates that the descriptor is stream-mode and wraps the returned iterable in `cancellableStream`, which races iterator.next() against the abort signal.
invariants: One logical stream id is owned once per connection; a duplicate open is rejected and binary frames close the socket with 1003.
A unary method opened through the stream carrier (or a stream method invoked as unary) is gateway/signature-invalid, never silently coerced.
Socket close aborts every active stream and awaits each iterator's return before the connection task settles.

service.name: forwarded-host-event-bridge
service.what: The push half of the Remote plane: a single application-selected allowlist of Cordis Host events is forwarded to browser consumers so they can react to server-side state instead of polling. `API_REMOTE_FORWARDED_EVENTS` declares 19 entries with an explicit dispatch mode — 17 `emit` and 2 `waterfall` (`approval/request`, `user-questions/request`) — and is the sole declaration read by both compiler faces and by `ctx.remote.$on`'s legal key set. `api/remotes` turns each entry into a queue-backed AsyncIterable handed to `typertGateway.registerRemoteEvents`; the Gateway opens one `$events` stream per client generation, emits a `ready` frame carrying the clientId and Host facts, correlates waterfall deliveries by eventId, and accepts outcomes back over the `$events/result` unary endpoint.
invariants: A forwarded event name must be non-empty and its arguments must be lossless JSON; a non-JSON argument throws rather than shipping a lossy frame.
Only one forwarded-event source may be registered per Gateway; a second registration throws.
A scoped waterfall delivery must carry its Agent directly and the carrier Agent must be that exact object; otherwise it throws instead of guessing lineage.

service.name: sdk-jsonrpc-stdio-runtime
service.what: The out-of-process programmatic wire contract. `JsonRpcLineTransport` speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over caller-owned byte streams with a strict frame discriminator (id+method = request, id = response, method = notification), ignores malformed lines, and answers missing handlers with -32601 and handler failures with -32603. `HarnessSdkJsonRpcServer` implements exactly three request methods (`initialize`, `session/prompt`, `shutdown`) and four server notifications (`session.event`, `session.status`, `subagent.started`, `subagent.finished`), advertising the wire-stable identity `deepseek-harness-sdk-runtime`. The `HarnessClient` is the Node-side driver: it spawns `dsh --profile sdk`, fans notifications out to filtered subscriptions, and tears the child down through a stdin-EOF -> SIGTERM -> SIGKILL ladder.
invariants: The server handshake identity stays the wire-stable name 'deepseek-harness-sdk-runtime'; reinitialization is unsupported.
