`session/prompt` only reports in-process subagent runs; remote child runs are never reported as `subagent.finished`.
A timed-out request is an abandonment: the transport drops its pending entry, but the server-side work keeps running until close (there is no wire-level cancel).
constants: JSON-RPC error codes -32601 (method not found) and -32603 (handler failure)
shutdown request timeout default 1000 ms; dispose EOF grace 6000 ms; dispose kill grace 3000 ms

service.name: acp-agent-client-protocol
service.what: A second, independent external wire contract: an Agent Client Protocol server over JSON-RPC stdio for automation clients (the `acp` plugin, `dsh --profile acp`). It uses the upstream `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` `ndJsonStream` + `agent()` app and implements initialize, session/new, session/list, session/resume, session/close, session/setConfigOption, session/prompt and the session/cancel notification. Session listing is keyset-paginated with an opaque canonical base64url cursor, resume is refused for subagent-origin or child sessions and requires a physically identical cwd, and permission requests are downgraded to one-shot allow-once/reject-once choices so an unknown client response can never become a durable grant.
invariants: `additionalDirectories` is rejected as outside the automation contract; cwd must be an absolute path.
A durable session is only resumable when it is not subagent-origin, has no parentSession, and its recorded cwd resolves to the same physical directory.
The session/list cursor must be canonical (re-encoding the decoded JSON must reproduce the token byte for byte).

service.name: web-host-static-and-launch
service.what: The browser-facing host surface: `WebServer` (`super(ctx, 'webServer')`) is a node:http route registry with exact/prefix matching (longest prefix wins), a single fallback seat, exact-path upgrade routes, optional gzip with a negotiated Accept-Encoding, a structured index-injection table collected per render, and raw `tapIndex` escape hatches. `frontend-static` claims the fallback seat to serve the built SPA dist (403 on traversal outside the dist root, 404 for absent targets, 405 for non-GET/HEAD, octet-stream for unknown extensions) and routes every index response through Connection's authentication then the webserver's index render. The `web-app` bundle supplies the dist location, LAN trust snapshot, canonical URL line, default-browser handoff, `DSH_WEB_URL` shell variable and the model-visible surface prompt.
invariants: Duplicate (kind, path) routes, duplicate upgrade paths and a second fallback registration all throw: route patterns are a composition-level contract.
An upgraded socket is tracked and destroyed explicitly on teardown because Node's closeAllConnections() does not include it.
Index responses always pass Connection authorization before bytes are read; non-index assets stay public.
constants: compression default 'none'; compressionLevel default 1 (0-9); compressionThresholdBytes default 1024
Config.host is one of '127.0.0.1' | '0.0.0.0'; Config.port max 65535 and required (0 = OS-assigned)
default web port 3080 (cordis.patch.yml: `port: !!js ctx.webStartup.port ?? 3080`, not in src)

service.name: profile-boot-and-cmdline-seam
service.what: How a dsh service process comes up and who owns the command line. `boot()` resolves the harness home, layers environment (DSH_/XDG_/DYLD_/BASH_FUNC_ bootstrap plus .env), mounts the root include, awaits the Loader and audits activation; `installFailLoud` converts a late unhandled plugin-init rejection into one labelled diagnostic and exit(1). Profiles are directory-shaped: PROFILE_TEMPLATES ships acp/web/headless/sdk/sdk-minimal bundle tuples with per-profile patch reload ('live' for web, 'startup' otherwise) and PROFILE_PATCH_FILENAME 'cordis.patch.yml' is the user layer. The `cmdline` library provides `cmdlineArgs`/`appExit`/`appReady` on the root context so a launcher parses only its own flags and hands the rest to the tree verbatim; `parseCmdline` wires commander help/version/parse failures to `ctx.appExit` structurally (never instanceof), and `exitOnStdinEnd` binds stdio EOF to a bounded successful shutdown.
invariants: App rows never own launcher-level command-line status; the launcher parses its flags and hands everything after them to the tree in argv order.
Commander control-flow errors are detected structurally by a 'commander.'-prefixed code plus a numeric exitCode, because an out-of-tree plugin brings its own commander copy.
A stdio application's EOF must not mask a startup rejection: exit is requested only after AppReady commits.
constants: Fiber state mirrors FIBER_PENDING = 0, FIBER_ACTIVE = 2, FIBER_FAILED = 3

service.name: settings-and-credentials-rpc-namespace
service.what: The configuration plane exposed to external consumers as two Typert Remote namespaces on one service: `SettingsController` registers `super(ctx, 'settingsController', { namespace: 'settings' })` and mounts `CredentialsController` as its own plugin (`namespace: 'credentials'`). Reads go through `describe({ redactSecrets: true })` and are projected field by field onto a wire view, so a provider's extra enumerable properties or a `role('secret')` field cannot ride a response. Writes expose merge (`update`), wholesale replacement (`replace`) and path-addressed `mutate` with an optional `expectedRevision`; a stale writer is classified as `settings/conflict` (carrying expected/actual) rather than a malformed request. Two further Remotes open the settings document and a user-authored agent preset directory in native editors.
invariants: Both namespaces stay registered even when no provider is mounted, so a call returns an actionable missing-provider diagnostic instead of a 404.
Every remote read uses redactSecrets: true; secret fields must never be serialized onto the wire.
Credentials describe requests are bounded to 64 refs, and only the declared fields are copied out of a provider answer.

service.name: command-catalog-rpc-and-lifecycle
service.what: dsh keeps a real (but non-central) command registry for human-facing operations, exposed as Remote methods rather than as a protocol-level slash surface. `CommandRuntime` (`super(ctx, 'commands')`) merges global and calling-agent-scoped layers, validates and freezes definitions (name pattern, non-empty description, handler type), and exposes `@Remote list(agent)` and `@Remote execute(agent, line, attachments, signal)`. Execution logs a paired `command/run` / `command/done` lifecycle into the session log, admits attachments only when the definition declares `input.attachments`, honours cancellation before the handler runs, and contains `command/done` append failure on the handler-failure path so the handler's own error stays the reported one.
invariants: Command names must match /^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$/ and are the registry key: a duplicate in one layer throws, and a scoped layer shadows the global one.
Admission misses (bad syntax or unknown name) return undefined and log nothing; they never entered a handler.
Minted command ids are instance-token-prefixed (cmd-<8 hex>-<n>) so a resumed log never repeats a pairing id.

service.name: directory-picker-capability-seam
service.what: A deliberately capability-shaped (not method-shaped) host service for choosing a workspace directory. `DirectoryPicker` (`super(ctx, 'directoryPicker')`) is abstract and exposes one `capability()` returning a discriminated, merge-extensible union: a `native` backend opens one OS chooser on the host display, a `browse` backend serves one-level listing plus child creation for an in-app browser. The browse side is bounded (maxEntries default 1000, `truncated` flags a cut level) and requires fully qualified paths so a wire value never resolves against the host cwd or current drive. `directory-picker-auto` resolves once at boot which backend to mount by sampling bind host, SSH launch, platform and display availability, mounting the matching backend and surface packages as real Loader entries.
invariants: The capability object must be stable for the service lifetime; consumers may capture it across calls.
An unknown capability kind is documented to hide the picking affordance, not to fail.
Only one implementation may register `ctx.directoryPicker` (normal Cordis duplicate-service behaviour).
constants: Linux chooser binaries ['zenity','kdialog']; Windows dialog CLOSE_RETRY_MS = 150, CLOSE_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 20

service.name: webhook-ingress-and-verification
service.what: An inbound ingress surface for external systems, separate from the authenticated browser transport. `WebhookRuntime` (`super(ctx, 'webhookRuntime')`) is a rule registry keyed by provider `kind`: `dispatch` snapshots and deep-freezes the delivery, starts every matching rule fire-and-forget, and the runtime's only built-in action is creating a Workspace-backed session. `webhook-github` registers an exact POST route that requires `application/json` (with at most one UTF-8 charset parameter), reads a bounded body, requires exactly one each of `x-hub-signature-256`, `x-github-delivery` and `x-github-event`, resolves the shared secret from the credential provider, verifies the HMAC through Octokit, dispatches, and answers 202 after in-memory dispatch rather than after rule settlement.
invariants: Rule callbacks are contained: a failing invocation logs and never escapes; a registration disposer hides the rule, aborts it, then drains its active callbacks.
A delivery must be lossless JSON and carry non-empty kind/source/deliveryId and a non-negative safe-integer receivedAt; otherwise dispatch throws synchronously.
Ingress answers are not authorization: the response deliberately carries no verification detail to the sender, and an unavailable secret is a 503, not a 401.
constants: HTTP 202 accepted, 400 bad JSON/header, 401 invalid signature, 405 method, 413 body too large, 415 content type, 503 unavailable
webhook-github maxBodyBytes is required with no default (min 1, max Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)
No numeric constants in webhook/webhook src

retrieval.name: session-query-live-preferred-corpus-reads-and-traces
retrieval.what: SessionQueryEngine (ctx.sessionQuery) resolves a live-preferred logical session corpus and serves backend-independent exact reads, filters, traces and title folds. SessionCorpus binds the optional sessionPersistence service through ctx.inject and, for a known live session, never consults persistence, so an optional backend failure cannot make in-memory history unreadable; a persisted header is checked with assertSessionHeadersCompatible before it is merged with a live one and records are returned newest-first. readSession replays the loaded log through Session.create to validate it before returning snapshots, readTitleSnapshots folds foldSessionTitle per session with per-session failure isolation, traceSession walks known ancestry and descendants from one listing, and traceEvent/readEvent expose direct positional replacements and a bounded raw-log window. readWindowMax is validated per call and prepared cold observations are cached by durable revision.
invariants: A live session is always preferred and never requires persistence to be readable.
A read returns detached clones (structuredClone/snapshotSessionEvent); callers cannot mutate retained state.
Batch title reads isolate per-session failures while cancellation rejects the whole operation.
constants: Closed error taxonomy of 18 SESSION_QUERY_* codes (config.ts:29-46)

retrieval.name: session-full-text-index-and-ranked-search
retrieval.what: SqliteSessionQueryEngine adds a disposable SQLite derived read model under the same ctx.sessionQuery service. openSearchDatabase() refuses a foreign database (application_id check), refuses a non-empty unrecognized file, and resets the derived schema in place when user_version differs from SESSION_QUERY_SQLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION, then creates a persisted schema (search_state with a singleton global_generation, persisted_sessions with revision/generation, and an fts5 persisted_docs table tokenized with unicode61) plus connection-local live_sessions and live_docs tables. The engine reconciles persisted and live sessions against the index under a serialized operation tail with a stability retry, keeps per-scope cursors carrying instance id, request fingerprint and generation so a stale cursor is rejected, and answers queries with MATCH plus highlight(). Caller text is quoted into a single FTS5 phrase so query syntax stays inert data, reserved highlight noncharacters are sanitized out of indexed text and queries, and snippet extraction is bounded by snippetChars counted in Unicode code points.
invariants: The index is disposable derived state: a schema-version or application-id mismatch resets or refuses rather than migrating user data.
Indexed text and the caller query are both sanitized for the reserved highlight markers, and the query is always one quoted phrase.
A cursor is bound to instance, normalized request fingerprint and generation, so a stale or retargeted page is refused.
constants: openAt default 'startup' with 'never' disabling search entirely, journalMode default 'wal' (index.ts:208-209)

retrieval.name: model-facing-session-search-and-workspace-authorization
retrieval.what: tool-session-query registers five model-facing tools over ctx.sessionQuery: session_search, session_event_search, session_trace, session_event_trace and session_event_read, each carrying the deployment's cooperative timeout budget and a shared system-prompt section. Every entry point derives the caller from the agent-bound execution context and authorizes the target before reading: a target session is accepted only when it is the caller's own session or when a filterSessions query returns exactly one record matching the caller's cwd, and cross-session search always appends a cwd filter, so search is workspace-scoped. Search results are cursor-free and capped by maxSearchResults, while the read/trace tools are declared concurrency-safe; a caller without a workspace or without an agent is rejected with a coded HarnessError.
invariants: Every target session must be the caller's own or share the caller's workspace cwd; no caller-supplied id bypasses authorization.
Cross-session search is always constrained to the caller workspace.
A caller without an agent or without a workspace cwd is refused rather than defaulted.

retrieval.name: session-log-export-archive
retrieval.what: session-log-export registers the Web-only `/export` human command and a Host-owned streaming download route at /api/session.export. The route validates the sessionId and includeDescendants query parameters, refuses with 500 when session-query, session-persistence or attachments are not mounted, flushes a live session's log before reading it, and answers 404 when the stored log is absent; the root log is prepared before the response so a read failure becomes a plain 500 that cannot echo absolute host paths into the browser. It then streams a ZIP whose per-entry DEFLATE level comes from config (0-9, default 6), optionally including descendant sessions, with a fixed content type and a generated attachment filename; HEAD requests cancel the body.
invariants: The route is the only export surface: query parameters are validated and unknown or malformed session input is a 400.
A live session's log is flushed before it is read so the archive matches the durable log.
Preparation errors are reported as generic status text, never as raw host error detail.

retrieval.name: attachment-ingestion-and-durable-content-addressed-store
retrieval.what: AttachmentStore (ctx.attachments) is the durable binary seam: admitEncodedImages/admitEncodedFile decode wire uploads while rejecting non-canonical base64 (an empty image is rejected, an empty file is a valid zero-byte payload) and then delegate to the store, and saveImages validates the whole ordered batch before committing any member so a refused batch starts no writes. Image admission enforces media-type, per-image, count and aggregate-byte limits plus a full decode, and returns content-addressed references in input order; verbatim file storage has no admission limits and defaults to an explicit ATTACHMENT_FILES_UNSUPPORTED rejection in backends that cannot store files, with streaming save/read variants that must not collect the whole file in memory. The local backend (LocalAttachmentStore) stores normalized images under <DSH_HOME>/attachments/v1 with declared limits for max image bytes, count per message, aggregate message bytes, intrinsic pixels and per-side dimension, and runs native transformations through a bounded CompressionLimiter.
invariants: Wire input must be canonical RFC 4648 base64; no alias or whitespace form is accepted.
An image batch is all-or-nothing: every member is validated before any member is committed, and references keep input order.
Verbatim file bytes are stored exactly, and a backend without file storage must reject explicitly rather than silently drop.
constants: DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGE_BYTES = 20 MiB, DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES_PER_MESSAGE = 20, DEFAULT_MAX_MESSAGE_IMAGE_BYTES = 200 MiB, DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = 64000000, DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGE_DIMENSION = 8192 (attachment-local/src/index.ts:34-42)
Accepted media types image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif (attachment-local/src/index.ts:181)

retrieval.name: image-admission-normalization-and-request-image-projection
retrieval.what: Beyond raw storage, the attachment layer owns a normalized image representation and a per-request projection. The local store resolves a NormalizationPolicy (total-pixel budget, long-edge dimension cap and encoded-byte target) applied after admission, so a larger admitted source is downscaled rather than refused, and native transformations run under the configured concurrency limit (default 2, max 8). readImageRequest(ref, policy) derives a deterministic model-request version from the stored normalized image for an exact route pixel budget and encoded-byte target, and returns both the bytes and a cache/upload identity covering every transform input; the base store rejects with ATTACHMENT_PROJECTION_UNSUPPORTED when a backend cannot derive request images. The MCP bridge is a second consumer of the same admission path: image content blocks from an MCP server are decoded and saved through ctx.attachments only after the exact current model route proves image input, and otherwise every image in the result is projected as diagnostic text while the raw value stays available to programmatic callers.
invariants: Admission bounds what is stored; normalization bounds what rides every later model request, and normalization never refuses an admitted ordinary source.
A request-image variant identity must cover every transform input so a cached variant cannot be reused for a different policy.
An image is admitted to model context only on positive proof that the exact current route accepts image input.

retrieval.name: at-file-reference-grammar-and-fuzzy-completion-index
retrieval.what: The file-reference seam provides @-mention completion shared by terminal and web clients. activeAtToken() parses an @path or @"path with spaces token at the editor cursor (an @ inside another token such as an email is not a trigger) and formatFileMention() renders a selection back into prompt text, refusing paths the grammar cannot represent safely and keeping a directory quote open so completion can descend. LocalFileReferenceService implements list() per agent over a cancellable WorkspaceFileSearch rooted at the agent's session cwd: directory-scoped queries read live state while a bare fuzzy query shares one bounded traversal (maxEntries) that is invalidated on tool results, and rankCandidates scores and truncates to maxResults. The seam installs a system-prompt section only while the model-facing read tool is visible to that agent.
invariants: Only path text is indexed and offered; file contents never enter the completion index or the prompt.
The index is bounded per workspace and invalidated by tool results rather than re-traversed per query.
The @-mention prompt guidance is installed per agent and only while the read tool is visible.
constants: DEFAULT_FILE_SEARCH_EXCLUDED_DIRECTORIES = .git, node_modules, dist, build, out, coverage, target, .next, .nuxt, .turbo, .venv, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .gradle (search.ts:31-47)

retrieval.name: cross-session-reference-snapshot-injection
retrieval.what: SessionReferenceResolver (ctx.sessionReferenceResolver, a TypertRemoteService over ctx.sessionQuery) turns a host-adapted cross-session mention into immutable message context. A system-prompt assembly listener records the assembly's provider/model per agent so a later route check uses the model that actually served the step; an agent/pre-step listener then prepares direct messages before the step proceeds. Referenced sessions are read as an exact surface snapshot, projected into a budgeted JSON snapshot wrapped in a `<referenced-sessions>` block explicitly labelled untrusted and read-only, and refused or replaced by an omission notice when they exceed the reference budget. Config bounds how many references one message may carry, how many candidates a picker sees, the absolute reference byte budget and the fraction of the model context the block may occupy.
invariants: Referenced session content is presented as untrusted, read-only data, never as instructions.
A reference block is bounded by both an absolute byte budget and a fraction of the model context.
The route used to size the block is the route actually recorded for the step, not a caller-supplied guess.
constants: maxReferenceBytes is required configuration; maxReferences/candidateLimit are validated positive safe integers (index.ts:87-92, index.ts:105-119)

retrieval.name: request-time-and-tmux-location-context-injection
retrieval.what: Two opt-in plugins add source-attributed situational context to request preparation. time-context registers a `timeContext` session projection (stateVersion 2) folding the latest model-visible event time, its own last injection time and the current turn's injection time, then appends one durable plugin-form snapshot message per eligible step naming the sampled time, the elapsed interval since the preceding model-visible message or step context, and the resolved browser time zone when the turn's claimed user messages carry exactly one. tmux-context runs one read-only `tmux display-message` plus a `ps -o tty=` comparison through ctx.shell once per turn, confirming the process actually owns the pane's tty (a terminal that merely inherited TMUX/TMUX_PANE reads as not in tmux) before injecting the session, window, pane and window-layout fields. Both re-inject only when the rendered state changed and honour an optional refreshIntervalMs floor.
invariants: Both features are no-ops rather than errors when their inputs are absent or unknown: no tmux pane, no shell service, or a failed query injects nothing.
Time and tmux readings are attached to the exact session and turn that produced them and are re-injected only when they change.
The browser time zone is used only when the turn's messages agree on exactly one zone.
constants: tmux fields read: session_name, window_index, window_name, pane_index, pane_id, window_active, pane_active, window_layout (tmux-context/src/index.ts:51-60)
refreshIntervalMs is a non-negative safe integer; 0 or omitted means inject on every eligible change (time-context/src/index.ts:110-119)

retrieval.name: ripgrep-backed-file-search-tools
retrieval.what: tool-fs-search registers the model-facing `glob` and `grep` tools over the packaged ripgrep binary, executed as ordinary foreground spawns through ctx.subprocess with fixed argv vectors (never ctx.shell, never a background task), so no system rg install and no shell quoting layer exist. glob excludes VCS metadata directories with paired any-depth and contents negated globs, sorts by modification time and either takes the modification-time head or samples across top-level entries when a page is over cap; grep uses a fixed line-oriented `rg --json` command so path, line and text parse without colon ambiguity, retains capped flat matches and per-line previews, and spills the formatted result through ctx.spillStore.saveText() once retention caps are exceeded. Complete raw stdout is bounded by rawOutputMaxBytes and a truncated capture fails explicitly with SEARCH_RAW_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW rather than parsing a partial stream, while stderr is retained only as a bounded diagnostic excerpt embedded in coded SearchError messages.
invariants: Search runs as a plain argv spawn through the subprocess seam; there is no shell layer and no model-visible background task.
A truncated or over-cap raw capture fails with a stable code instead of being parsed as if complete.
Stable failure codes: SEARCH_INVALID_PATTERN, SEARCH_FAILED, SEARCH_RAW_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW, SEARCH_ABORTED.

retrieval.name: web-search-provider-selection-and-tool-bounds
retrieval.what: ctx.web is a provider registry plus execution-time selection: a configured searchProvider/fetchProvider id must be registered and available, a configured-but-missing or unavailable id fails with a distinct WebError code, and with no id configured exactly one usable provider is required or the call fails as ambiguous/unavailable, so selection never depends on registration order; the same fields may be fed by $DSH_WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER/$DSH_WEB_FETCH_PROVIDER. The seam truncates a provider's over-return to request.maxResults and flags `truncated`. Concrete providers register through the same seam: an Exa provider (apiKey from config or $EXA_API_KEY, empty key means unavailable), a Perplexity provider ($PERPLEXITY_API_KEY, sonar model, search_recency_filter), and a DeepSeek provider that calls the Anthropic-compatible Messages API with the native web_search server tool, resolving its key through the credentials seam, exposing a settings namespace, and logging each auxiliary request as a durable web/deepseek-search-llm-request event. The model-facing tool-web package owns schemas, enablement, prompt guidance and bounds, and fails with a structured error at execution time when no provider can run.
invariants: Provider selection is resolved at execution time and is order-independent: ambiguity is an error, never a first-registered win.
The seam, not the provider or the model, enforces the returned-source bound.
An enabled web tool stays registered and visible even when its provider is unavailable.
constants: DeepSeek search defaults: model deepseek-v4-flash, apiVersion 2023-06-01, maxTokens 4096, maxUses 5, endpoint env DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_BASE_URL (web-search-deepseek/src/index.ts:53-60, web-search-deepseek/src/index.ts:82)

retrieval.name: http-fetch-with-public-address-pinning
retrieval.what: The local http fetch provider validates a URL before any network work: bounded length, http/https only, and no embedded credentials; response bodies are classified into html or text kinds, decoded with the declared charset (an unrecognized charset fails loudly rather than producing mojibake), and a redirect that crosses origins is refused so each new origin needs a fresh tool call and a fresh address check. Destination safety is enforced by resolving the hostname once with resolvePublicAddresses and rejecting the complete answer set if any address is not globally reachable unicast (IPv4-mapped IPv6 classified by its embedded address; NAT64 and other transition prefixes stay blocked because the eventual IPv4 destination cannot be pinned), then handing the validated addresses to an address-pinned transport so the connection cannot re-resolve to a private address. An IP-literal destination that the checks would refuse never takes the proxied path.
invariants: A hostname is resolved once and the whole answer set must be public; the pinned addresses are the only ones the transport may use.
Redirects are same-origin only, so each new origin is re-validated.
An unsupported or unrecognized response encoding fails loudly instead of being decoded leniently.
constants: Defaults: maxResponseBytes 5000000, maxBodyChars 100000, timeoutMs 30000, maxRedirects 5, User-Agent deepseek-harness/0.0.1 (+https://github.com/deepseek-ai) (index.ts:45-51)
RFC 6052 NAT64 prefix lengths 32/40/48/56/64/96 and IPv4-only discovery via ipv4only.arpa with sentinels 192.0.0.170/192.0.0.171 (network.ts:37-39)

retrieval.name: session-title-projection-and-model-titling
retrieval.what: SessionTitleService (ctx.sessionTitle) folds the latest logged session/title event as the single source of truth, registers `title` and `titleInput` session projections (the latter counting eligible human messages and remembering first/last seq), and accepts at most one title provider whose automatic mode is first-prompt or all-prompts. It normalizes every accepted title: OSC/CSI/ESC sequences, remaining C0/C1 controls and directional/invisible controls are stripped, whitespace is collapsed, and the result is truncated to a UTF-8 byte budget without splitting a code point; a deterministic first-prompt fallback is derived from the leading words when no provider produces a title, and rename of text that normalizes to empty fails as SessionTitleInvalidError. The two model-backed provider plugins share one policy module: they select the first human message or all human messages, frame them as JSON so user text cannot break delimiters, require the framed input to fit maxInputBytes, resolve an explicit provider/model pair or the exact route recorded on the session's main request, log the exact auxiliary request as a durable session/title-llm-request event before dispatch, and reject tool-call or max-token finishes instead of accepting a partial title.
invariants: The logged session/title event is the only title source of truth; the projection and get() both fold the log.
An accepted title is terminal-safe and within the UTF-8 byte budget, and the fallback budget must not exceed maxTitleBytes.
A model-backed title must be text-only and produced within the configured input-byte, output-token and timeout budgets.
constants: Config requires fallbackMaxWords, fallbackMaxBytes and maxTitleBytes; fallbackMaxBytes must not exceed maxTitleBytes (index.ts:56-63, index.ts:297-323)

session-title-llm requires targetWords, targetCjkCharacters, maxInputBytes, maxOutputTokens, timeoutMs with no library defaults, and provider/model must be supplied together (session-title-llm/src/index.ts:74-82, session-title-llm/src/index.ts:129-133)

retrieval.name: user-questions-waterfall
retrieval.what: UserQuestionService (ctx.userQuestions) pauses an agent tool call until a human answers, asking the scoped `user-questions/request` waterfall on the agent's scope so UI packages compose the actual answerer. ask() validates the request before touching any UI: an already-aborted signal and an empty question list are distinct failures, a supplied agent must be the registry's exact live instance (CALLER_NOT_LIVE) and must be a live runtime root rather than an owned child (DELEGATED_CALLER, so a delegated child is told to return the question in its result instead of blocking forever), and a presentation intent is rejected unless its approve label is one of that question's own options and a plan review carries the detail it reviews. With no answerer accepting the request the waterfall resolves to NO_PROVIDER, and an abort observed anywhere in the ask is reported as ASK_ABORTED with the UserQuestionError shape restored across the waterfall boundary.
invariants: Human interaction is valid only for the exact live calling agent and only when that agent is a runtime root.
A declared presentation intent must be self-consistent with the question's options and detail before any UI sees it.
The service never invents an answer: without an accepting answerer the call fails as NO_PROVIDER.
constants: Stable codes: ASK_ABORTED, EMPTY_QUESTIONS, CALLER_NOT_LIVE, DELEGATED_CALLER, BAD_INTENT, NO_PROVIDER (index.ts:41-47, index.ts:86-151)

ops.name: session-telemetry-capture-seam
ops.what: The capture side of session telemetry: a backend-agnostic Service Definition (`SessionTelemetryBackend`, registered as `ctx.sessionTelemetry`) plus the `SessionTelemetryCoordinator` a backend composes in its constructor. Ledger records mirror canonical session-log events one-to-one through live capture (session/created, session/event, session/disposed, session/flush plus the agent/error relay) or through on-demand replay of the canonical log; ops records ('agent-error', 'shutdown') carry no event identity. Every record is a deep clone of the event data, gets a pre-mapped severity (tool/result isError and turn/end error reasons become 'error'), minimal identity attributes, and passes through the `session-telemetry/record` waterfall that is the deployment's only redaction extension point. A module-scope WeakMap handoff cursor lets a re-adopting fiber resume instead of re-handing history.
invariants: `emit` must be a non-blocking enqueue: it is called synchronously from the session/event hot path, and its errors are contained and logged rather than reaching the agent loop.
The redaction waterfall ships no rules of its own; the innermost next() passes the record through, so exported data is exactly as clean as the rules a deployment mounts.
A throwing rule withholds that one record (containment is per event) and never starves later events in the same replay.
constants: Zero numeric constants in src/ (previously handed seq starts at -1 when history is excluded)

ops.name: otel-telemetry-export
ops.what: The shipped telemetry backend: it composes the OpenTelemetry JS SDK as-is — a LoggerProvider with a BatchLogRecordProcessor and an OTLPLogExporter — and maps each captured record onto `logger.emit()` with timestamp/observedTimestamp, the severity triple, the body as AnyValue and the identity attributes. Two sharing modes exist: FEEDBACK_ONLY (default) captures session history only when feedback is explicitly submitted and wires an on-demand coordinator with includeHistory; DISABLED constructs no SDK state at all and merely warns when recorded feedback stays local. Resource attributes carry service.name/service.version from APP_IDENTITY plus OTel's standard `user.id` from the anonymous-user-id package. The plugin owns one outer shutdown deadline because the SDK's export timeout does not bound its preceding forceFlush() wait.
invariants: Capture is authorized only by a listener that is the canonical appended event (session.eventAt(event.seq) === event); a non-canonical event warns and is dropped.
Only this Session's own explicit feedback authorizes replay — events below inheritedEventCount, and message-level events for another session, never do.
The optional flush() hint is deliberately not implemented, because forwarding it to forceFlush() would be the only source of concurrent flushes and can silently drop tail records.
constants: exporter.url is required outside DISABLED and must be http(s)

ops.name: anonymous-identity-attribution
ops.what: The per-harness-home anonymous identity shared by telemetry and feedback. `getOrCreateAnonymousUserId()` reads (or mints and persists) a random UUID v4 stored as a bare line in `.anonymous-user-id` inside the harness home resolved by resolveDshHome ($DSH_HOME, else ~/.dsh). The id is never derived from hostname, network address, git remote or any other identifying source; it is scoped to the harness home rather than the machine, so every process sharing one home reports the same id and deleting the file mints a fresh identity next launch. Reads and writes are synchronous and memoized per resolved file path; a concurrent first launch is settled by an exclusive-create write whose loser rereads the winner.
invariants: The id is a random UUID with no derivation from any identifying input; the file is the only storage and contains nothing but the UUID line.
Persistence is best-effort: a read-only home still yields a usable, process-consistent id so feedback and telemetry are never blocked.
One process touches the disk once; a file deleted mid-run keeps the process's id until the next launch.

ops.name: invariant-runtime-diagnostics
ops.what: A configurable registry of package-owned runtime invariant checks. Every package registers its checks from a `./invariant` companion through `ctx.invariants.register(packageName, installer)`, so ordinary package entrypoints stay independent of diagnostics; the registry installs each contribution into its own child fiber and binds a `fail` reporter that throws a package-attributed `InvariantError` carrying code 'INVARIANT' and the owning npm package name. Selection is a global `enabled` switch plus case-sensitive JavaScript regex allowlist and blocklist over package names; a filtered-out package still has its name reserved, so a duplicate registration throws either way.
invariants: A package name may be registered at most once, and the reservation survives filtering.
Package names must be non-blank and contain no whitespace; allow/blocklist entries must be non-blank, unwhitespaced, duplicate-free and valid regexes, or the registry construction throws.
An enabled installer that rejects disposes its child fiber and releases the reservation.
constants: Config defaults: enabled = true, package_allowlist = [], package_blocklist = []
Empty allowlist admits all; blocklist applies after allowlist matching

ops.name: session-stats-projection
ops.what: Whole-session accounting figures served through the session-projection seam rather than recomputed per render. The `session-stats` plugin registers one projection unit, `sessionStats` (stateVersion 1), that folds turn and step counts plus wall-time buckets: llmMs from step/start to the closing assistant/message, ttftMs/ttftSteps from the first streamed token, and decodeMs/decodeTokens gated on a provider-reported output token count. The plugin owns only the fold — delivery through the registry snapshot, the change feed and every projection carrier is the seam's job, so paging and compaction cannot change the figures a client renders.
invariants: Uninteresting events return the same state reference (Object.is gates the change feed).
One assembled assistant message closes one step boundary, so a defensive duplicate cannot accrue twice.
Every duration is clamped with Math.max(0, ...); decode metrics require a finite non-negative provider output count.
constants: initial totals all zero: turns, steps, llmMs, toolMs, ttftMs, ttftSteps, decodeMs, decodeTokens

ops.name: token-and-cost-metering
ops.what: Replay-aware token and cost accounting for request and surface pressure. `TokenMeter` (`super(ctx, 'tokenMeter')`) is the replay owner: it registers the tokenUsage/contextPressure/contextBreakdown projection units, lazily folds each Session's durable log through `_sync` up to `session.seq`, and answers `measure(session, requestHeader?)` with a deeply frozen, structured-cloned `TokenMeasurement` (baseline, surfaceDeltaTokens, totalTokens, surfaceTokens, nodes). A fixed heuristic prices messages (4 chars per token, 4-token block and role overheads); `priceSurface` replaces attachment heuristics with the routed model's actual image pricing and the mounted LLM service's file projection, and throws if the pricing answers a different occurrence count than it was asked, because misalignment would silently misprice. Provider usage is reused only when the latest successful call's canonical envelope matches and its total is no lower than the route-priced anchor.
invariants: No settings are supported: any key in TokenMeterConfig throws rather than being ignored.
Every fallible step (surface plan and anchor validation) runs before replay state mutates, so a malformed event stays unread on retry instead of half-applying.
measure() returns detached deeply immutable values; the internal fold is never aliased to a caller.
constants: Projection state versions: tokenUsage 2, contextPressure 4, contextBreakdown 4

ops.name: message-feedback-ledger
ops.what: Durable per-message feedback stored in the canonical session log rather than a side store. `MessageFeedbackService` (`super(ctx, 'messageFeedback')`) exposes three Remote methods — list, put and delete — that derive current state by replaying `feedback/message-put` / `feedback/message-delete` events for the target session. Writes are optimistic-concurrency controlled by an item `version` UUID (`ifVersion` must equal the current version or null), a matching no-op retains the version and appends no event, and notes are bounded by a deployment-required `maxNoteBytes`. Cold operations hold write ownership across read/compare/append and never construct a Session or Agent; live operations go through the live owner and then verify the appended prefix is actually durable before acknowledging. A `feedback/committed` parallel event lets observers see a committed cold mutation without publishing a live Session.
invariants: A put only targets a message that exists as an append-surface assistant/message event in the log; otherwise it is target-not-found.
Operations are serialized per session id and drained on disposal; a new mutation after disposal begins is rejected.
maxNoteBytes is required with no default and must be a positive safe integer.
constants: maxNoteBytes: required, no default, positive safe integer
timestamps bounded by Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; version is a UUID
Failure codes: session-not-found, target-not-found, version-conflict, note-blank, note-too-large

ops.name: session-feedback-command-and-remote
ops.what: The human feedback channel. One closed category vocabulary (`FEEDBACK_CATEGORIES`, seven entries in presentation order) is exported for product surfaces, `recordFeedback(session, entry)` appends exactly one log-only `feedback/record` event with trimmed text and an optional category, and the same operation is exposed as a Typert Remote (`SessionFeedbackService`, `super(ctx, 'sessionFeedback')`, `@Remote('record')`) so a product surface records without a slash command. A `/feedback <text>` command is registered on the shared command registry as the human-facing entry point, and its acknowledgement names both the receiving session and the anonymous user id. Recording never starts model work.
invariants: An entry with neither text nor category is still recorded; surrounding whitespace is discarded and a blank text is recorded as absent.
The Remote reports `session-not-found` for an unknown live session; it never creates a session.
The command result is an error (with usage text) when no feedback text was supplied, and in that case no event is appended.
constants: FEEDBACK_CATEGORIES = task-result, instruction-following, product-interaction, service-stability, resource-cost, security-privacy-permission, other

ops.name: runtime-inspector-diagnostics
ops.what: An experimental out-of-repo diagnostics plane: a host plugin (`name = 'experimental-inspector'`, inject ['webServer']) starts a loopback HTTP + WebSocket inspector worker (port 9230 by default, occupied ports advance) and injects a client bootstrap into index.html; a browser-face plugin (inject []) provides the same `ctx.inspector` service and publishes JSON observations with a topic, a validated payload and a monotonic timestamp. The package implements a Chrome-DevTools-Protocol-shaped surface (runtime, debugger, DOM, network, sources domains over mirrored host/client realms) plus read-only Cordis runtime-tree queries, and carries more than twenty explicit memory/lifecycle bounds. Every bound is configurable and defaults come from one `resolveInspectorOptions()` call, so the schema and the library cannot drift.
invariants: Observation payloads are validated as JSON before entering the carrier; publish() does not wait for worker delivery.
The endpoint binds only 127.0.0.1 and admits only explicitly listed client origins.
Cordis tree snapshots are depth-capped and scoped: process-global inspection is not part of the client realm contract.
constants: port default 9230 (max 65535); host fixed '127.0.0.1'; captureFetch default true
maxRequestBodyBytes 8 MiB; maxResponseBodyBytes 32 MiB; maxBodyChunkBytes 48 KiB; maxJournalBytes 256 MiB

ops.name: performance-benchmark-budgets
ops.what: A source-only benchmark suite that pins cold-path and long-session performance as CI assertions rather than as reports. Six suites exist: session-open (isolated built-worker measurement of open/read/sessionRestore/projection phases, first Host history and cold Agent resume, plus a constrained-heap run), agent-continuation (request-history, tool-continuation, child-catalog and profile-continuation scenarios over an 800-turn synthetic workload), a synthetic-history seed-correctness bench, conversation-fold (compiled cold client conversation fold over a 500,000-delta window), long-session-browser (Playwright/Chromium open, paging, trajectory switch, first token, streaming responsiveness, heap and DOM node count over 240 turns) and active-stream-reconnect (ClientAssistantStream.replace over a 100,000-delta live prefix). Budgets are reference-machine durations converted by a shared calibration helper, and each suite re-asserts its own computed budget so a silent recalibration fails.
invariants: Every timed benchmark runs in a freshly built worker (`.dsh-build/**/*.js`) with NODE_OPTIONS and TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH stripped; the runtime guard rejects tsx loaders and package entries outside lib/**/*.js.
CI budgets are derived, never hand-written: ciTimeBudget(expected) = ceil(expected * CI_TIME_SCALE * PERFORMANCE_BUDGET_HEADROOM).
A stuck worker is SIGKILLed at the suite's own timeout (60 s for the heavy suites, 30 s for the browser/worker client suites).

conversation-fold: TURNS 200, LARGE_DELTAS 2000, SMALL_DELTAS 100, ATTEMPTS 3, EXPECTED_LARGE_FOLD_MS 16, EXPECTED_DELTA_SCALING 2.5
active-stream-reconnect: EXPECTED_REPLACE_CI_MS 50, REFERENCE_RETAINED_MB 24, SAMPLES 3, 100,000 deltas, REPLACE_BUDGET_MS asserted === 63
long-session-browser: HISTORY_TURNS 240, DELTAS 120, PACE_MS 16, SAMPLES 3, REFERENCE { open 200, page 260, trajectory 160, first 1100, streamTask 1800, input 500, streamWall 1000 }
agent-continuation: ATTEMPTS 5, WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS 60000, EXPECTED_MS profile-continuation 1700, REQUEST_HISTORY_BUDGET_MS 297, EXPECTED_RETAINED_HEAP_MB 23

ops.name: fail-loud-crash-handling
ops.what: Crash and fatal-failure handling on the service side. `installFailLoud` is installed before boot and turns a late unhandled plugin-init rejection into one labelled stderr diagnostic plus exit(1); a rejection already accounted for by the activation audit is ignored during its process checkpoint. The exit is deliberately deferred through an optional `release` hook raced against FAIL_LOUD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_MS, so a terminal-owning surface can hand the terminal back; the handler stays installed during the release and a latch keeps the first rejection the reported one. `assertEntriesLoaded`/`assertEntriesActivated` then audit the settled Loader and fail startup when a non-disabled entry has no fiber. The web server adds a last-resort per-request guard that logs and answers 400 instead of letting one malformed request become an unhandled rejection, and the SDK client retains a bounded stderr tail to diagnose an unexpected runtime death.
invariants: The diagnostic is written before the release runs, so a hanging disposer cannot swallow the reason.
The fatal exit is never cancelled by a wedged disposer — only delayed up to the release timeout; the timer stays referenced so Node cannot reach an empty event loop and exit 0.
A per-request failure must never exit the process: once headers are sent the response is destroyed, otherwise a 400 is written.
constants: Fiber state mirrors FIBER_PENDING = 0, FIBER_ACTIVE = 2, FIBER_FAILED = 3
last-resort HTTP status 400 (or response destroy after headers)

ops.name: profile-distribution-and-module-fallback
ops.what: Distribution, layout and update semantics of a dsh installation. Each profile is a directory under `<harness home>/profiles/<name>` whose manifest lists an ordered bundle layer array plus a user patch layer (`cordis.patch.yml`); `PROFILE_TEMPLATES` ships five templates (acp, web, headless, sdk, sdk-minimal) with a per-profile patch reload policy — 'live' only for web, 'startup' for everything else — and an installation-owned tuple map lets a shipped template be normalized after upgrade. Profiles are made resolvable through symlinked private package links in a `.dsh-module-fallback` directory that is healed on load, so a profile keeps working when the checkout layout or package manager store changes. `resolveDshHome` anchors all of this under $DSH_HOME or ~/.dsh.
invariants: The user patch layer is applied after every bundle layer, and its reload policy is a property of the profile template rather than of the file.
Custom profiles with no shipped template retain the historical live patch reload and default to the '@deepseek-ai/dsh-base' bundle list.
Module-fallback links are installation-owned and healed (not trusted) at load; a manifest that no longer matches is rewritten.
constants: PROFILE_TEMPLATES: acp = [dsh-base, dsh-acp-app] startup; web = [dsh-base, dsh-web-app] live; headless = [dsh-base, dsh-headless] startup; sdk = [dsh-base, dsh-sdk-app] startup; sdk-minimal = [dsh-sdk-minimal] startup

interface.name: session-event-stream-contract
interface.what: The event/stream contract a renderer consumes. `MutableSessionEventSource` implements `SessionEventSource` (an ObservableSnapshot of a `SessionEventWindow`) and is the client-side owner of one Session's contiguous event window. The window carries `entries`, `hasMore`, a monotonic `revision`, and the exact `SessionEventChange` delta that produced that revision ('replace' | 'prepend' | 'append' | 'settle-assistant'). Entries are `SessionEventLikeEntry`: durable Session events plus a client-only `assistant/live-chunk` transient frame carrying an attemptId. The window is a persistent concat tree materialized lazily, so prepend/append publish synchronously without copying the whole history.
invariants: Every accepted window mutation publishes synchronously through notifySubscribers; a renderer never sees a torn window.
`revision` increases by exactly one per publish; `change` always describes the delta between the previous and current revision.
A `settle-assistant` removes all transient rows for one attemptId and, when a durable settlement is supplied, inserts it at the first position whose seq is greater.
constants: initial revision = 0; initial window = { hasMore: false, change: { kind: 'replace', entries: [] } }

interface.name: session-wire-event-acceptance
interface.what: The boundary check that keeps a wire page or follow frame from entering the window contract unvalidated. `assertSessionWireEvent` narrows one value received in a follow frame or a history page: it rejects any field outside the seven-name envelope (type, seq, time, data, ignorable, surfaceOp, sourceEventSeqs), requires a non-negative safe-integer seq (rejecting -0), an integer time, a present non-undefined data, and `ignorable` only when literally true, then runs the session package's own `validateSurfaceMetadata` and `validateSessionEventData`. It deliberately does not strip or normalize wire fields, and range membership plus source existence stay Host-owned.
invariants: Event names and payloads are merge-extensible; only event-local owner rules run at this boundary.
An unexpected envelope field is an error, never silently dropped or ignored.
seq and time must be safe integers; -0 is rejected explicitly.
constants: Envelope keys: type, seq, time, data, ignorable, surfaceOp, sourceEventSeqs

interface.name: forwarded-event-subscription-contract
interface.what: The subscription half of the renderer seam: `ctx.remote.$on(event, listener)` lets a client renderer subscribe to a Host Cordis event by its declared name, with the listener type projected from the owner package's own `Events` declaration rather than a flattened restatement. The legal key set is exactly the Host assembly's `API_REMOTE_FORWARDED_EVENTS` allowlist, surfaced to consumers only when `TypertRemoteEventSelection` is augmented by the consumer face. Notifications run in registration order and isolate failures; scoped waterfalls receive the resolved Client Context and may return, delegate through next(), or reject the Host dispatch.
invariants: Nothing is forwarded unless the Host assembly allowlisted it; a consumer face that omits the selection augmentation makes `TypertRemoteEvent` never, so `$on` fails to compile rather than silently no-op.
Only two dispatch modes exist: unscoped void `emit` and scoped async `waterfall` whose last parameter is a same-result next().
A listener's disposer is owned by the calling fiber.

interface.name: client-remote-stream-supervision
interface.what: The client-side stream contract for a renderer that must survive reconnects. `ctx.remote.$stream(options)` returns a single-consumer `RemoteStream<Item>` carrying a physical generation id and a revision; three specializations sit under one abstract `RemoteJournalStream`: journal (change feed), snapshot, and remote. Reconnection is driven by `ConnectionController`, which owns generation/attempt counters privately, computes an exponential backoff cap (`min(backoffMaxMs, base * factor^(attempt-1))`) with 50-100% jitter, exposes state 'connected' | 'disconnected' | 'connecting', and warns if a generation takes longer than generationReadyWarnMs while failing at generationReadyTimeoutMs. `ctx.remote.$host` exposes fixed Host facts (home, isLoopback) as plain identity-stable reads.
invariants: A stream is single-consumer; a replayed frame cannot regress the revision.
constants: backoffBaseMs default 500; backoffFactor default 2; backoffMaxMs default 10000
retry delay is uniformly 50-100% of the current cap

interface.name: session-projection-consumer-contract
interface.what: The seam a renderer uses to read whole-session derived figures that paging and compaction cannot change. Units register on `ctx.sessionProjections` with a key, a stateVersion and a state schema, and are delivered through the registry snapshot, the change feed and every projection carrier. `session-stats` registers the `sessionStats` unit (stateVersion 1) folding turns/steps plus llmMs, toolMs, ttftMs, ttftSteps, decodeMs and decodeTokens from step/start, assistant/attempt and assistant/message; `token-meter` registers `tokenUsage` (stateVersion 2), `contextPressure` (stateVersion 4) and `contextBreakdown` (stateVersion 4). A registered key that is absent from the current cut means capability absent, not zero.
invariants: A unit's `apply` must return the same state reference for uninteresting events, because Object.is gates the change feed.
Client reads treat a missing key as capability absence (host unit unmounted, or no baseline/frame yet) and never invent a default value.
Durations are clamped with Math.max(0, ...) so clock skew cannot produce negative figures.
constants: sessionStats stateVersion = 1; tokenUsage stateVersion = 2; contextPressure stateVersion = 4; contextBreakdown stateVersion = 4

interface.name: settings-seam
interface.what: The settings seam the presentation layer configures through. `SettingsProvider` is an abstract Cordis Service registered as `ctx.settings` that owns namespace registration, resolution, validation, change detection and the `settings/updated` commit event; subclasses implement only `load()` and `persist()` and declare `writable`. Registrations produce a `SettingsScope<T>` with get/watch/update/replace. A conflicting write is signalled by `SettingsConflictError` carrying a stable `SETTINGS_CONFLICT` code plus expected/actual revisions. A redacted descriptor read (`describe({ redactSecrets })`) is the contract for configuration UIs, and path-addressed `SettingsPathOp` (`set`/`unset`) exists precisely because a UI holding a redacted view must not rebuild a section wholesale and silently delete secrets.
invariants: Paths are addressed against the section as stored, never against whatever the caller last read; writes are serialized per namespace by a write queue.
Teardown sets stopped, refusing new writes and new watchers, then settles every queued write chain and started watcher invocation before completing.
Namespace keys match /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/ and a `role('secret')` field must never appear in a redacted descriptor.

interface.name: file-settings-provider
interface.what: The shipped SettingsProvider implementation behind the seam: one YAML or JSON document (default `<harness home>/settings.yaml`) holds every namespace section. External edits hot-publish through a chokidar watcher with a write-settle window; the raw text of the last successful parse/persist is cached and a watcher event equal to that cache is a no-op, which is also the self-write suppression. Every write acquires a cross-process file lock, re-reads the document, and applies a leaf-level `setIn`/`deleteIn` diff so untouched nodes and the key node of every changed pair keep their comments, anchors and formatting. Files are created 0o600 in 0o700 directories, atomically.
invariants: Only .yaml/.yml/.json extensions are accepted; anything else fails at resolution time.
The watcher write-settle window and the chokidar poll interval derive from one `debounceMs` value; defaults are resolved in one `resolveSpec`, never inline.
A non-map value (array or scalar) replaces wholesale when unequal, taking interior comments with it.
constants: chokidar stabilityThreshold = debounceMs; pollInterval = max(1, min(debounceMs, 10))
file mode 0o600, directory mode 0o700; JSON indent 2

interface.name: client-boot-manifest-announcement
interface.what: The host-announced descriptor of what the presentation layer is composed of. The node half of `client/modules` scans the Loader's entries for packages declaring `dsh.client`, composes a content-addressed `WebBootGraph` (rev, entries, batches) and injects it into index.html as the `globalThis.__DSH_BOOT__` row plus parser-blocking bootstrap and preloaded application combo scripts; before that it installs a `window.__ModuleLoader__` queue shim so bundles registering early are not lost. The browser face parses the same wire into two consumer views — a module-table view (fetch the bundle) and a cordis-plugin view (compose the entry) — and the boot-readiness deferred `__DSH_BOOT_READY__` settles after the last injected row. `ctx.remote.$host` publishes the small fixed Host fact set (home, isLoopback) that a renderer may read without a subscription.
invariants: The wire is single-sourced: the host node half and the browser parser share one `WebBootEntry`/`WebBootGraph` shape.
A dynamic package row must precede rows whose `external` requests it; Cordis activation order is unrelated and stays with fiber service waiting.
A bundle factory executes only on first import/require and is memoized; script execution registers, it does not materialize.

interface.name: directory-picker-capability-detection
interface.what: Capability detection as a first-class seam: the directory-picker service exposes a discriminated `capability()` rather than a fixed method set, and every consumer switches on `capability().kind`. The auto chooser samples the host once at boot — bind host, SSH launch, platform, Linux chooser binaries (zenity/kdialog), DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY — and mounts the matching backend plus its browser surface as genuine Loader entries, unmounting the other pair. Anything ambiguous resolves to `browse`, the interaction that works for remote clients, and the documented default for an unknown kind is to hide the picking affordance instead of failing.
invariants: The capability object must be stable across calls for one service lifetime; consumers capture and compare it by reference.
A display-dependent backend is never mounted where no OS chooser can be reached (non-loopback bind, SSH launch, or no display).
An unknown capability kind hides the affordance; it is not an error.
constants: native is available only on darwin/win32/linux

interface.name: acp-capability-advertisement
interface.what: A second capability-negotiation seam: the ACP bridge advertises what it can actually do in the `initialize` response instead of assuming the client's. It reports the single PROTOCOL_VERSION, agentInfo, `mcpCapabilities: { http: true }`, `sessionCapabilities: { close, list, resume }` and `promptCapabilities: { image: <computed>, audio: false, embeddedContext: false }`. The image flag comes from `supportsAcpImagePrompts`, which returns false whenever the attachment store, the LLM service, the configured provider or the model is absent, when the deployment's accepted media types do not intersect the image types, or when the routed model's `inputModalities` does not include 'image' — unknown is negative by construction.
invariants: Absence of any input to the check (service, route, capability, deployment media support) resolves to false; the bridge never advertises a capability it cannot honour.
A single-version agent returns its one PROTOCOL_VERSION for both the 'same version if supported' and 'latest supported' branches.
The advertised capability gates prompt admission at runtime, so advertisement and enforcement read one value.
constants: agentCapabilities: mcpCapabilities.http = true; promptCapabilities.audio = false; promptCapabilities.embeddedContext = false; sessionCapabilities = { close, list, resume }

interface.name: tool-presentation-mode-policy
interface.what: dsh's screen/presentation-mode policy for the model-facing tool surface (the backend analogue of a UI screen mode). `ToolPresentationMode` is 'native' | 'ptc' | 'both': native sends every visible schema, ptc sends only `run_code` plus a generated SDK prompt and collapses the executor to that same surface, both sends both forms; ptc requires a mounted code runtime whose language has a registered SDK renderer, and native names in toolOrder are invalid under ptc. The mode is either the deployment default (the tools row's config field) or a scoped override via `tools.presentAs(mode)`, where the nearest scope on the chain wins so one agent preset can compose PTC agents beside native ones in the same process.
invariants: `presentAs` requires a scoped (agent.ctx) context; a process-global presentation is the config field instead.
One declaration per scope: a second presentAs for the same scope throws rather than silently composing.
Switching to ptc without a code runtime whose language has a registered SDK renderer fails prompt assembly instead of degrading silently.
constants: maxParallelSubCalls default 10 (must be a positive integer)

interface.name: user-question-interaction-seam
interface.what: The seam where an engine-side tool call blocks on a human. `UserQuestionService` (`super(ctx, 'userQuestions')`) validates the request — at least one question; when an agent is supplied it must be the registry's exact live instance and a runtime root, not an owned child — and then dispatches `user-questions/request` as an Agent-scoped Cordis waterfall whose default `next()` rejects with NO_PROVIDER. Presentation intents ('plan-review' etc.) are checked at the asker: the named approve label must be one of the question's own options and the reviewed detail must be present, so a UI honouring the intent can never show a choice the asker never offered. The event is forwarded to browser consumers through the allowlist's two waterfall entries.
invariants: Human interaction is gated by runtime ownership, not durable session lineage: a resumed session that is a new runtime root may ask; an owned child may not.
A presentation intent that names a non-option approve label, or omits the detail it reviews, is an error at the asker rather than in each UI.
The default answerer rejects; there is no implicit timeout answer.
constants: Error codes EMPTY_QUESTIONS, CALLER_NOT_LIVE, DELEGATED_CALLER, BAD_INTENT, NO_PROVIDER, ASK_ABORTED

pluginKernel: dsh runs on Cordis, and that shapes every other domain: the harness is not a library with a CLI but a tree of plugins mounted by a Loader against a cordis.yml composition, where every capability is a Service looked up from the context. A plugin is a function or a `{ name, apply }` object; `apply(ctx, config)` receives a context that is a child Fiber of the mounting entry, and `export const inject = [...]` declares the service names it needs -- an entry whose dependencies are absent simply stays in FiberState.PENDING rather than failing, which is why the same package set can be composed into web, CLI, SDK and ACP profiles. Services register with `super(ctx, 'key')` and augment `interface Context` through `declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis'`, so `ctx.llm`, `ctx.tools`, `ctx.agentLoop`, `ctx.sessionProjections`, `ctx.compaction` and `ctx.tokenMeter` are typed lookups resolved along the fiber tree. Teardown is structural, not conventional: `ctx.effect(() => disposer, 'label')` (or a generator effect yielding several disposers, which run LIFO) unwinds exactly the registrations made through that context, and `ctx.fiber.assertActive()` plus the FiberState set gate work against a lifecycle that is already dead. Events are the other half of the kernel: every extension point is a named event dispatched as `emit` (fire-and-forget, with failures contained per listener so one listener cannot starve a later one), `serial` (awaited in order, first bail wins) or `waterfall` (around-middleware with a `next` default) -- the loop's `agent/pre-step`, `agent/request` and `agent/request-error` are all waterfalls, and agent-subject events are dispatched through a fused carrier built by `agentEvents()` so the payload's `agent` field and the scope key cannot diverge. Composition is data, not code: shipped profiles (`packages/bundle/*`, `apps/*`) and per-agent presets (`agent.cordis.yml`) are cordis.yml trees, and `dsh-agent-presets` mounts a preset's subtree under a standing scope key to which that agent's context is parented, so its rows apply only to that agent. The scoping primitive underneath is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope`: registrations inherit DOWN the scope chain while event admission extends UP it, which is what makes a per-agent tool, prompt section or listener both local to the agent and visible to the agent's own dispatches. Boot is deliberately fail-loud: after the Loader tree settles, `assertEntriesLoaded` and `assertEntriesActivated` reject any enabled entry that failed to import, rejected during activation, or is still pending -- naming the missing services -- and `installFailLoud` turns a late unhandled rejection into one labelled stderr diagnostic followed by exit(1), waiting at most 2000 ms for a terminal-owning disposer to hand the terminal back. Layered over the same services is Typert, dsh's RPC plane: a `TypertRemoteService` subclass binds its Cordis service key to a wire namespace, `@Remote`-decorated methods become invocable endpoints (`@Remote('name')`, `@Remote({ mode: 'stream' })`, `@RemoteScope`), and a lookup/context registry maps wire ids back to host objects. That is why dsh's operational surface is an RPC namespace rather than a slash-command table: a capability is exposed by publishing a Remote, and the browser client, the SDK stdio runtime, the ACP bridge and the CLI are all thin adapters over the same service tree.

Command-surface note: dsh has no central slash-command table -- a capability is exposed either as a Cordis service method, as a model-facing tool, or as a Typert @Remote endpoint, and the three standalone command packages (/compact, /feedback, /goal) plus the inline /permission, /plan and /export registrations are thin adapters over those. Evidence policy: every mechanism carries at least one path:line or path:line-line reference into src/, and every cited line was opened by the agent that recorded it; all 1284 references across the file were additionally machine-checked to resolve to an existing file with in-range line numbers (0 missing, 0 out of range), and a sample of the first citation of every mechanism was read back and matched against its claim. Where a capability exists but has no shipped production caller this is stated in the mechanism's `what` (for example: the agent-teams stack is unshipped, storage-sqlite and the v0-to-v1/v1-to-v2 session-format migrations have no production importer, session-log-deepseek defaults to disabled, queueHostSubagentPrompt has no production caller, experimental/inspector's host endpoint is unmounted, and no job_start/job_wait tool exists). Nothing in this file is an evaluation of the design.
